5. **F85 IS DE-TARGETED, and this is Chris's ruling, not an Architect's read.** *"My point about finishing a mock in 45 minutes was just an example not a target … I think we're good."* **The under-45-minute bar stops being a gate**, the spec's acceptance-criteria sentence is amended to say so, and **no MP or AP task is measured against it.** **F92 survives on its own merits** — the CPU nomination still rides the 5-second sweep, and that is a real pacing cost — but it is now *"a thing worth fixing"*, not *"the other term in a bar we must hit."*


- **D233 — The storage shape is an INVESTIGATION, and what the measurement already establishes**

1. **MP.1 decides it, and it comes first.** The question: **can the draft engine operate on mock-owned storage without duplicating the auction/snake logic?** The answer is a measurement, not a preference, and **the deliverable is a decision with evidence, not code.**
2. **What is already measured, so MP.1 starts from facts rather than a blank page (§1.3).** The engine is **58 live functions / 6,252 lines** of plpgsql; it names its tables **literally** (`drafts` in 37 functions, `draft_picks` 15, `league_chat` 15, `draft_bids` 11, `draft_liveness` 5, `draft_queues` 2); and **dynamic SQL is essentially absent — one function in the family contains `EXECUTE`, and it is `draft_actor_name`.**
3. **So the ruling's own guardrail is the likely finding, and MP.1 must state it plainly if it reaches it: separate mock tables mean either two copies of the auction rules or a rewrite of 6,252 lines into table-agnostic dynamic SQL — and BOTH are worse than either option.** Duplication is worse for the obvious reason. Dynamic SQL is worse for a less obvious one: it would break the `search_path=''` discipline every one of these functions is built on (tasks-M* §4.1), and it would make the pgTAP suites assert against a body that no longer names what it touches.
4. **The same-tables path is now priced honestly and it is task-sized** (§1.3, correcting D228(2)): four `NOT NULL` drops, five RLS policy arms on four tables, eleven in-body auth sites across eight functions. **"You own it" is one predicate** — `config->'mock'->>'launched_by' = auth.uid()::text`, the idiom `draft_pause`/`draft_resume` already ship (`069:404–415`).
5. **MP.1 must nevertheless check the thing that would change the answer:** whether a nullable `league_id` weakens any **real-league** guarantee. A policy that reads *"member of the league OR launcher of this mock"* must be provably no more permissive for a row that HAS a league. **If that cannot be shown, the answer changes and the task says so.**
6. **Do not pick the shape by preference, and do not let this decision be made inside a task that is also building something.** The MS.1 precedent: a task that audits *and* enables will report on its own work.

**2026-08-20 — Architect (the MS mock-sandbox breakdown; transcribed verbatim from `tasks-MS-mock-sandbox.md` §3.5 at merge, per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 / tasks-M3 D126–D143 / tasks-AP D197–D203 precedent).**

- **D216 — Lane charter, numbering, and why MS is its own lane.** **Number note (D161's grep-together rule).** R, D, F, Q **and E** swept together across `main` @ `90178a7` and the one open branch (PR **#180**, `docs/DR2-draft-room-v2`) — the full table is tasks-MS §1.9. `main` tops at **R467 / D215 / F97 / Q18 / E70**; #180 holds **D204–D212 / F87–F91 / Q19–Q21 / E71–E74**. R312 first-filed-keeps, so this session takes **D216–D221**, files **F98–F100**, opens **Q22**, and takes edge cases **E75–E76** and spec version **v2.15**. **The amendment round (Chris's order ruling, same day) adds D222–D223, F101 and E77**, re-derived rather than continued: re-swept at amendment time across `main` (**R467 / D215 / F97 / Q18 / E70**, the `spec-tier-view.md` hexes excluded per D180) and **both** open PRs — #180 (**D204–D212 / F87–F91 / Q19–Q21 / E71–E74**) and this one. Re-sweep at merge. (1) **MS is a new lane with its own prefix, not an append to tasks-M3 §6 or to tasks-AP.** The AP/DR2 precedent exactly: Chris drove a *shipped* surface (Mock Draft Mode), ruled changes to it, and those changes get their own Architect document plus an ACTIVE-BUILD clause, while the milestone's approved breakdown stays what it is. MS's subject — who may drive a mock — is orthogonal to M3's exit criteria, to AP's pacing and to DR2's layout. (2) **The lane is small and it is a permissions change with one product consequence.** Six tasks, three of them without a migration. It is filed as a lane rather than as one big task because **the audit must be a separate deliverable from the change it authorizes** (D218), and because the §8.8 pins are the point rather than an afterthought. (3) **Task ids are `MS.1`–`MS.6`.** No `L.C`, `AP.` or `DR2.` id is reused, retired or renumbered. (4) **This PR folds the spec, and it has to.** §8.8's v2.8.16 erratum (`spec:567`) is LAW and says every §8.7 control refuses mocks. Cutting tasks that contradict LAW would oblige the first Builder to stop and file a spec question — a halt this session would have manufactured. The fold is deliberately narrow (§10 item 1) and takes **v2.15** because #180 already filed v2.14.

- **D217 — What D103 got right, what it missed, and the exact shape of the overturn.** (1) **D103/D110(1) were right about authority and right about the bug.** "A commissioner control on a mock is interference with a member's solo practice" is a correct sentence about a commissioner reaching into *someone else's* rehearsal, and the guard caught a live-proven `leagues` write. Neither of those is being called a mistake. (2) **What it missed is that in a mock the launcher IS the commissioner.** The doctrine was written from the *actor* side (who is reaching in) and never asked what happens when there is only one person in the room. Chris's ruling 1 supplies the missing premise, and the whole lane follows from it. (3) **The overturn is scoped to identity, not to isolation.** What changes: *who* may call a §8.7 control on a mock. What does not change: **§8.8's zero-side-effects rule** (unweakened, and now the explicit gate — D218), **D103(2)'s no-other-driver doctrine** (a commissioner who is not the launcher still gets nothing — MS.2 item 7 pins it), and every real-draft behaviour (§4 rule 13). (4) **The pattern is already in the codebase and it is 069's, not `resolveActingSeat`'s.** `draft_pause`/`draft_resume` solved this exact problem at L.B1.6 — member floor, then commissioner for real drafts, then launcher for mocks. MS.2 extracts that into one helper and applies it. The working draft of this document proposed reusing R420's `resolveActingSeat`; that is a **TypeScript API-layer seat resolver** for the F65 response-integrity check, not a server-authoritative gate, and reusing it would have put authorization in the wrong layer (§1.2). (5) **The gate ORDER is the load-bearing bug, and it is measured.** In all eleven controls `is_league_commish` fires before the mock refusal, so today's friendly P0001 is unreachable for a non-commissioner launcher — the exact person this lane is about. D110(1) recorded the consequence in one clause and nobody had a reason to act on it until now. **The reorder therefore runs at ALL ELEVEN sites, cleared AND excluded** — E75 (LAW added by this same PR) requires an excluded control to refuse *"with a message that names its own reason"*, and measured, `draft_reset` and `draft_end` answer a non-commissioner launcher with `42501 not a commissioner of this draft's league`. A reorder scoped to the cleared set would ship LAW the code cannot honour.

- **D218 — §8.8 is the gate, it is answered by measurement, and `draft_reset` was not the only breach.** (1) **The audit is its own task (MS.1) and produces a list, not a change.** Separating them is the point: a task that audits *and* enables will report on its own work, and the enable step's design will bend toward whatever the audit found convenient. MS.1 ships a cleared list with evidence per row and touches no behaviour. (2) **"Which controls are safe" is a measurement, never a reading.** §1.4 is why: two of the eleven reach a `leagues` write through a helper, so the direct write set is not the answer; and §2.2 is why a `draft_*` sweep is not the answer either — two §8.7 *panel sections* reach league verbs that no draft-function query will surface. (3) **FOUR structural breaches, found by this survey, against the working draft's assumption of one — and the fourth is MIS-TARGETED rather than blocked, which is the worse shape.** `draft_reset` (writes `leagues.status` + `settings`, and broadcasts on `league:<id>`); the **autopick toggle** (`set_team_autodraft`, 072 — keyed on `p_league_id`, mocks explicitly excluded from its lock, writes the real `league_members.is_autodraft`); **seat reassignment** (the league's invite/assignment surface, embedded in the panel); and **`draft_set_order`**, whose mock refusal is real, sits in `prosrc` at `087:2341`, and **never fires** (§1.3). The first is a body that could be narrowed; the next two are breaches *by construction*; **the fourth cannot be fixed at the RPC at all**, because the RPC is never handed the mock. None has a mock-scoped version worth building (§10 item 4). (4) **AN RPC-LEVEL AUDIT CANNOT SEE A MIS-TARGET, AND THAT IS THE FINDING THAT GENERALISES.** At the RPC layer `draft_set_order(mock_id, …)` is genuinely mock-local: the guard fires, the composite comes back clean, and the control would be **CLEARED** — the breach lives one layer up, in a resolver an RPC-level audit never executes. This is why **MS.1 drives every control through its ROUTE, with a mock in the room AND a real draft alive in the same league** (§5 MS.1 item 3): without the second draft a mis-targeted write has nothing to hit and looks clean. §1.3's original heading — *"The API layer needs almost nothing"* — was the premise that hid it, and is corrected in place rather than deleted so the failure mode stays legible. (5) **The exclusion mechanism follows the breach's shape, not a house style.** Three of the four are excluded by an in-body refusal that names its own reason; the fourth is excluded by a **service-layer block plus a UI exclusion**, and neither half alone is one — §12's server-authoritative rule means a hidden menu item is not an exclusion when the endpoint still answers. (6) **Isolation has three dimensions, and a row count is the weakest.** Rows (whole-row composites, because three enabled controls UPDATE `draft_picks` in place), **broadcast topics** (`draft_reset`'s `leagues` write reaches every member's `league:<id>` subscription), and the whole-schema sweep as the net for a table nobody enumerated. §4 rule 10 states the standard; MS.6 builds the one harness that applies it.

- **D219 — The D141 carve-out is the CLOCK, and mocks only.** (1) **The carve-out's width is Chris's ruling 1 read literally.** He named two things: *"make it as fast as possible"* and *"pause it if they need to do something"*. Pause already works. The clock is what pause-first makes expensive — you cannot try a shorter bid clock without pausing, resuming, and losing the beat you were trying to feel. (2) **The other five pause-gate consumers keep pause-first even in a mock, and that is deliberate.** `draft_undo`, `draft_reassign_pick`, `draft_move_player`, `draft_reverse_won_bid` and `draft_cancel_nomination` all edit *draft state the tick is concurrently reading*, and the pause is what takes the tick out of the race — the gate's value there is not only social. Chris's own words endorse the workflow (*"pause it if they need to do something"*). **This is a narrowing, stated as one**: widening it later is one predicate, and MS.1's measurements will say whether it is worth it. (3) **D141 and the ALIGN ruling are two events and must be cited as two.** D141 (PROGRESS §4) was enforced **auction-only**, with the snake divergence recorded and filed as **F57**. **Chris ruled ALIGN on 2026-08-18**, folded as spec §8.7 **v2.12.5** and built as migration **090 / L.C1.8**. A document that says "D141 made all clock edits pause-first on every draft type" has compressed a ruling out of the record. (4) **The implementation shape is fixed by a pin, not by taste.** `commish-auction-ops.test.ts:171` couples the gate's *consumer set* to the UI's `PAUSE_FIRST_RPC_SECTIONS`. So the carve-out changes the gate's **body** (`AND NOT p_draft.is_mock`), never which functions call it — one predicate, one place, and the coupling that keeps the UI mirror honest stays intact. (5) **"The new value governs the next clock" is inherited, not built.** Both `extend_current` arms are refusals and 090 **deleted** the snake extend machinery precisely so a future gate-weakening could not resurrect it (`090:291–303`). MS.3 must not undo that reasoning for mocks — the two false refusal messages get re-worded, the machinery stays gone.

- **D220 — `draft_reset` in a mock: the frame, the constraint, and the recommendation.** (1) **The decision is real, not a formality.** "Stays off" is defensible — *Delete practice & exit* already exists and a fresh mock is one click away. (2) **But delete-and-relaunch is rate-limited and lossy.** §22.5 caps mock creations at **5 per hour** per user (in-body, advisory-locked — D110(6)), so a launcher iterating on settings hits a wall; and a relaunch **re-seeds a `random` order** on the new mock's own id (D110(5)), so "run that same board again" is something relaunch cannot do. (3) **The shape is constrained by a measured fact, and it is not the obvious one.** A mock-safe reset **cannot** write `status = 'scheduled'`: `draft_start_internal` filters `is_mock = FALSE`, so nothing could restart it, and `draft-room.tsx:415` would render the real draft's lobby with a Start button that cannot fire (**F99**). The variant must land the mock **`live` at pick 1**. (4) **Recommendation: build it**, as a mock arm inside the one verb (never a second RPC), taking no `leagues` lock and performing no `leagues` write. **Chris can overturn this when he reviews this PR** — it is recorded here rather than decided in a Builder session because it is a product call about what a practice room is for. (5) **Either way, MS.4 owns the lane's single most important pin:** the whole `leagues` row byte-identical around a mock reset, plus the absence of a `league:<id>` broadcast. That is D110(1)'s original live proof, converted from a memory into a permanent assertion.

- **D221 — Surfacing without teaching: the room already has the seam.** (1) **Chris ruled "no" on explanatory copy and that is a build constraint (§4 rule 14).** No teaching label, no "these are the tools a commissioner has" line, no tutorial, no onboarding hint, no first-run tip. **MS.5's bar is FINDABLE, not EXPLAINED.** Ruling 2's discovery benefit is a *consequence* of the tools existing, not a feature to be built on top of them, and copy added to compensate for placement fails both halves. (2) **Recommendation: the launcher gets `Draft Options` itself, not a grown `Practice options`.** Chris's ruling 2 is that a mock is where someone learns what a commissioner has — the honest way to do that is the **same door with the same name**, not a parallel menu that happens to hold the same items. It also means **one** catalog and **one** panel: a second menu re-solving a solved surface is the LV.7 failure pattern. `Delete practice & exit` joins the destructive group beside Reset, and the single-item practice menu disappears (§10 item 3). (3) **No layout is prejudged, and that is measured rather than assumed.** `commandBarModel` already separates `draftOptions` from `practiceOptions` and already takes `isMockLauncher`; the change is which groups a pure ops function returns. DR2's nine tasks do not restructure the command bar (measured against `tasks-DR2-draft-room-v2.md`). **If a control needs a place the room does not have, that is a DR2 question and MS.5 stops and flags it** (§4 rule 15). (4) **The UI must not offer what the engine forbids** — D110(1)'s rule survives the lane that overturns its conclusion. The launcher's group list is derived from MS.1's cleared list through one predicate, not maintained by hand in two places, and **`autopick` and `seats` never render in a mock**. **`order` DOES render** (D222 — Chris ruled parity) **but only after MS.7 lands**: until the service targets the mock's own draft, that group is a one-click rewrite of the real order (§1.3). *An earlier revision of this item listed `order` as never-render; the parity ruling reversed it and a sequencing constraint replaced the exclusion.* (5) **`draft-command-bar.test.ts:151–153` pins `isCommish`'s source text by regex.** It moves to pin the new predicate; it is not deleted, and the docblock at `:21` that states the D110(1) seam is corrected with it.

- **D222 — PARITY is the lane's governing rule, and it reverses `order`'s remedy.** (1) **The ruling (Chris, 2026-08-20, after this document's first review):** *"so the point is the commish will need to set the draft order no matter, and it can always change last second. so there needs to be a way for the commish to set the order and then if real leagues can a mock league should as well so everyone can simulate their actual draft position or test different ones if they have a choice. for example, in my league last place gets to choose their draft position the next year."* (2) **The principle, stated so the lane can be tested against it: A MOCK GETS WHATEVER A REAL LEAGUE GETS.** Not *"whatever is safe to give it."* **A mock that cannot reproduce the user's actual draft position is not practice — it is a different draft.** §8.8 already said this about the engine (*"Same engine, literally… A mock that behaves differently from draft night is worse than no mock"*); D222 extends it to the commissioner surface, which is exactly what D103 had carved out. (3) **What it reverses, and it was the Architect's call rather than a Builder's slip.** The revision written after R468 excluded `draft_set_order` and put it on MS.5's must-not-render list. **Every piece of the diagnosis stands** — the mis-target, the probe, the never-firing guard. **The remedy answered the wrong question.** *"This control is unsafe"* is a reason to **fix** it, not to withhold it, and withholding it costs the user the one thing the motivating case needs. **Exclusion is now reserved for controls that write the real league BY CONSTRUCTION** (the autopick toggle, seat reassignment) **or whose product value is genuinely served another way** (`draft_reset` — MS.4's open decision, where "delete and relaunch" is a real substitute in a way that "don't set your order" is not). (4) **The fix is service-layer, and it is the shape §1.3 already identified.** `orderRequest` gains a `draft_id`; `patchDraftOrder` honours it; the mock room targets its own draft. **An RPC message change still cannot work** — the RPC is never handed the mock, so nothing it says is ever read. **MS.7** owns it. (5) **The severity note travels with the fix, and it is not about row counts.** A draft order is **negotiated property** — *"two people text messaging agree to swap picks."* Silently reversing one destroys an off-platform agreement **and posts a system line that makes it look deliberate**. That is why MS.7's pin is over the **real draft's stored order and its chat context**, not over a count. (6) **The control Chris named next does not exist, and it is NOT this lane's.** A **swap**: *"oh you like the 7th pick i like the 3rd pick. and then the commish needs to be able to swap them."* Filed as **F101** with the measurement that makes it a real gap. §6 says out-of-scope in as many words so it cannot creep in.

- **D223 — Choosing your slot at launch: the fast path, and why the seat picker cannot do this job.** (1) **The launcher already picks a SEAT, and that is a different question from a SLOT.** `mock-draft-launcher.tsx:138–156` renders a `Select` labelled *"Draft from seat"* (`aria-label="Seat to practice from"`) over `mockSeatOptions` (`mock-launcher-ops.ts:84–91`), defaulting to the launcher's own franchise (`defaultMockSeatId`, `:95–97`); the choice rides `config.mock.human_team_id`. **A seat says which franchise you play. A slot says when you pick.** (2) **And seat choice CANNOT be made to answer it — Chris's own correction is why:** *"there is no real draft order, most drafts will set the order right before."* `create_mock_draft` takes the real draft row's stored order as the candidate and resolves through the one implementation, **seeded by the MOCK's own id so an undrawn league gets a fresh deterministic shuffle per mock** (`089:935–957`, the comment says exactly this). So in the **normal** case — no order drawn yet — every launch reshuffles and the seat you chose lands wherever the shuffle puts it. **Picking a seat to get a slot works only in the minority case where an order already exists, which is backwards from how it will be used.** (3) **The task is therefore: choose your SLOT at launch — 1..N, default random — with the other franchises shuffled around you, written to the MOCK'S OWN order.** The real draft's order is neither read for this nor written by it, and is not required to exist. (4) **The fast path, deliberately — not a full order editor at launch.** `DraftOrderEditor` exists and works, and mounting it in the launch dialog would make someone drag twelve franchises into place to express *"put me third."* **The launch dialog answers one question with one control**; a launcher who wants a specific *full* order has the editor in the room once MS.7 lands. Recorded so the omission is not read as an oversight. (5) **Determinism is not optional and there is exactly one shuffle.** Reuse `draft_resolve_order_internal`'s existing seeding — the mock's own id (`089:935–957`) — rather than adding a second randomizer. Two implementations of "randomize an order" is the failure §4.7 exists to prevent, and a mock's replayability depends on it. **A slot choice is a constraint ON that shuffle, not a replacement for it.**

**2026-08-20 — Architect (the AP auction-pacing breakdown; transcribed verbatim from `tasks-AP-auction-pacing.md` §3 at merge, per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 / tasks-M3 D126–D143 / tasks-DR D147–D156 / tasks-SE D166–D175 precedent).** **Number note (D161's grep-together rule):** R, D, F and Q swept together across `main` @ `4e7170a` with **ZERO open PRs** (`gh pr list --state open` → `[]`; the SE breakdown PR #161, which §2's header still described as awaiting approval, in fact **merged 2026-08-19** — `gh pr view 161` → `MERGED`, `mergedAt 2026-08-19T16:40:38Z`). `main` topped at **R455 / D196 / F83 / Q16** (`D700`/`F97` remain the `#FFD700`/`#F97316` hexes in `spec-tier-view.md`, excluded per D180), so this session took **D197–D203**, filed **F84–F86**, and opened **Q17/Q18**.

- **D197 — Lane charter: AP is its own lane, and the reason it runs ahead of M3's tail is Chris's, not an Architect's preference.** (1) **A new lane with its own prefix, not an append to `tasks-M3` §6** — the DR precedent exactly (Chris drove a *shipped* surface, ruled changes, and those got their own document plus an ACTIVE-BUILD precedence clause while the milestone's approved breakdown stayed approved). Three reasons: M3's exit criteria are **unchanged** by anything in AP and an append would blur what the gate certifies; tasks-M3 §6 is LAW Chris merged as PR #150, and quietly inserting product changes into it makes approval stop meaning approval; and "AP before L.C4.1" is a *cross-lane* precedence statement, which is what ACTIVE-BUILD exists to carry. (2) **The counter-precedent is distinguished, not ignored:** `L.C1.8` WAS appended to tasks-M3 §6 — but F57 was an M3-*internal* alignment (auction pause-first vs snake), a question the milestone raised about itself. Nothing in AP is that; all six items are Chris changing the product. (3) The M3 gate must still cover AP's suites — filed as **F84** rather than left for the L.C6.1 Builder to rediscover (R51). (4) **The sequencing reasoning, recorded because it is Chris's:** AP lands before `L.C4.1`, `L.C5.1` and `L.C6.1` because those three encode today's behaviour as assertions — **the bid-storm spec in particular assumes today's bot cadence**, and a solvency property test written against `auction_min_bid` would pin a field AP.1 deletes. Writing them once, after the behaviour settles, is cheaper *and* yields the honest suites. (5) No `L.C` id is reused, retired or renumbered.

- **D198 — Retiring `auction_min_bid`: one derived reserve, one data migration, and what survives of C38.** (1) **The two jobs collapse into ONE number read through ONE helper** — `draft_auction_reserve(config) → INTEGER` (0 under the toggle, else 1), replacing every `COALESCE((config->>'auction_min_bid')::int, 1)` in the chain (**16 assignment sites** measured across 084/085/086/087/089 on `main` @ `4e7170a` — 084:3 · 085:2 · 086:1 · 087:5 · 089:5, by `grep -c` on the two COALESCE forms; the set AP.1 must actually edit is **smaller**, since 089's `CREATE OR REPLACE`s superseded several of those bodies, and the Builder resolves the HEAD list per AP.1 item 2 rather than trusting this count. Classified by job in tasks-AP §1.3). This is §4.7's one-authority discipline applied to a second quantity, and it is why the change is mechanical rather than delicate: the nomination floor and the per-slot reserve were **already the same variable in every body**, so making them one function preserves the algebra exactly at the default and moves both to 0 together under the toggle. (2) **The removal is a DATA migration, and skipping that half breaks every league that stored the key** — `league-settings.ts:213` is `z.strictObject` and `mergeSettings` (`:643–663`) parses the stored blob on **every read**, so a leftover `settings.draft.auction_min_bid` is a hard parse failure, not a harmless extra. Both stores are rewritten (`leagues.settings->'draft'` and every `drafts.config`), with `RAISE NOTICE` counts and a **separate count of rows that stored ≥ 2** — the only leagues whose meaning changes — because a silent conversion of somebody's settings is exactly CLAUDE.md's "never let nothing happened mean it worked". (3) **tasks-M3 C38 is superseded as to its VEHICLE and promoted as to its SUBSTANCE:** the $0 floor is no longer a value of a 0–5 field but a named toggle Chris ruled; C38's actual findings (a $0 floor is legal, raises stay `> high_bid`, boundaries pinned in pgTAP 034) become spec law at §8.6.2/§8.6.3 and **its coverage is re-pointed, never deleted**. (4) **The solvency machinery is not weakened or made conditional** — with the toggle ON it evaluates to `remaining ≥ 0` and stops firing, which §8.6.8 now states in the LAW; removing an E28 arm or a pin "because it can't fire" is an automatic review finding (tasks-M3 §4 rule 7). (5) The TS mirror moves with the SQL and the parity fixture covers **both** toggle states.

- **D199 — The uncontestable instant award.** (1) **The predicate is ONE query, never a loop** — a `CROSS JOIN LATERAL draft_team_budget` over active franchises excluding the nominator, the shape `draft_auction_solvent` (`084:386`) and `draft_end` (`087:1004`) already use, inside the held draft-row lock — and **the increment is a NAMED constant `1` compared as `high_bid + increment`**, per §8.6.9, because writing it as `> high_bid` would be a latent bug with no symptom while the increment happens to be $1. (2) **A complete roster needs no clause of its own** — `draft_team_budget` forces `max_bid = 0` at `open_slots <= 0` (`084:348–350`) and `high_bid + 1 ≥ 1 > 0`; an explicit `open_slots >= 1` term is documentation and must not be what correctness rests on. (3) **The award is EXTRACTED and reused, not reimplemented** — ARM 2.6(b)'s ~150 inline lines (`089:2480–2671`) become `draft_award_nomination_internal`, moved byte-for-byte; this is the extraction 089 already performed for `draft_system_nominate_internal` (`089:658`) when a second consumer appeared, and losslessness is proved the way 087/R367 proved its own (the exact-message pins and goldens pass **before** the new caller is added). (4) **The 3 seconds is the room's beat, and the wire mechanism is decided so nobody improvises one:** a tick-scheduled 3s cannot be 3s (the ≤5s sweep would land it in 3–8s, differently each time), so the server awards immediately and the uncontestable path performs **two UPDATEs inside the one transaction** — the nomination open with an additive `"uncontested": true` on `current_nomination`, then the award-and-advance. Both fire 088's `drafts` broadcast (`current_nomination` is in D134's payload), so every client sees announcement-then-award in one commit: **no new column, no new event, no new topic.** The additive key is the only spec-shape change (§12.3) and rides the migration banner as an erratum. (5) **Deliberately not done:** no scheduled server action, no `pg_net`, no second cron — and D200 does not need one either.

- **D200 — Reactive CPU bidding: change what PROVOKES a bot, not how often the sweep runs.** (1) A CPU response runs **in the transaction that provoked it** (a human's bid, another CPU's raise, the nomination that opened the market; the award already advances the rotation, so a CPU's turn to nominate can be served in that transaction too). The sweep keeps **expiring clocks when nobody acts** — the only job that genuinely needs a timer — and **`cron.schedule('draft-tick','5 seconds')` at `068:1265` is not touched**, because it sweeps every live draft in the system (§22.3). ARM 2.6(a)/(b)/(c1) stay as the no-actor safety net. (2) ARM 2.6(c2)'s candidate query + raise (`089:2313–2345`) is extracted to `draft_mock_cpu_respond_internal`, verbatim first and extended second, so the think-time path and the reactive path are ONE implementation. (3) **Bounded LOUDLY:** the responder recurses through `draft_place_bid_internal`, so a hard cap of `2 × team_count` raises per provoking transaction with a `RAISE EXCEPTION` — never a silent `EXIT` — because a ladder that long means the value model or the candidate query is wrong and a silent stop would hide it. (4) **Jump-bids are a seeded choice between the jump and the nibble, never above `LEAST(value, max_bid)`**, reusing the D93 24-bit PRNG already inside `draft_mock_cpu_bid_value` (`089:329–360`); a second PRNG is a review finding, and determinism is not optional (the sim, the property test and every golden depend on a mock replaying identically). Both textures are required by the ruling. (5) **The honest arithmetic, stated so the task can be judged:** reactive responses collapse the mock's cost to `nominations × (bid window + ≤ one sweep interval)` ⇒ ≈ **67 min at the shipped 20s clock** (a ~3.5× improvement on F76's 3.5–4 h) and ≈ **42 min at 10s**. **So AP.3 alone does NOT meet Chris's 45-minute bar; AP.3 + AP.4 do** — filed as **F85** rather than discovered at the gate. Both figures are estimates, and §4 rule 10 of tasks-AP requires them to be replaced by a measured wall-clock.

- **D201 — The auction's manual nomination order: F80's arm (b), and ONE editor.** (1) **Take arm (b)** — a `nomination_order` field in the §7.3.8 catalog that `draft_start` hydrates — over arm (a) (a new pre-start arm on `draft_set_order` plus a route). Arm (a) is the "honest" shape in the abstract since the order is per-draft, but arm (b) is what the snake side already does and is **one argument wide**: `draft_start` passes candidate **and** settings fallback into the snake resolver (`084:625–632`) and passes the nomination candidate with **no fallback** (`084:637–644`, whose own comment at `084:462–464` says exactly why). Arm (a) would additionally need a route, a hook, a live-only UI path, and a second place a commissioner can set the same thing. (2) **The signature trap, and the house's own answer to it:** `CREATE OR REPLACE` cannot add a parameter and a defaulted overload beside the old signature is an ambiguity trap — 087 hit this twice and solved it with an explicit `DROP FUNCTION` + `CREATE FUNCTION` (`087:1500/1502` for `draft_reassign_pick`, `087:1794/1796` for `draft_move_player`). Either follow that or resolve the candidate at the two call sites; either way **both pinned RAISE texts survive byte-identically**. (3) **One editor, two mounts — never a fork.** `DraftOrderEditor` is mounted a second time on `draft.nomination_order`; a second reorder component would be the LV.7 failure pattern. (4) **Chris's snake requirement is ALREADY MET, and this is recorded rather than quietly rebuilt** — `draft_order_mode: manual`/`custom` plus the dnd-kit editor ship today (`settings-panel.tsx:1440–1462`, `draft-order-editor.tsx`), verified by opening both files. **One honest divergence from his words:** he described *"a modal window that pops up … and then a confirm new order button"*; what ships is an **inline** editor in League settings saving through the page's atomic PATCH. **Decision: keep the inline editor for both fields** — a working, shipped, tested control is not worth re-housing to match a sketch, one pattern beats two, and the auction editor should look exactly like the snake one a commissioner has already used. **If Chris wants the modal it moves BOTH mounts together**, which is why the divergence is written down instead of ignored.

- **D202 — The split-column gate goes per-COLUMN, and the six ship under FLAT labels.** (1) Chris ruled *"ship with 6"*, so `splitGroupAvailability`'s `.every` (`auction-player-table-ops.ts:351`) becomes per-column availability. (2) **The labels are the Architect's call within his ruling, and they are flat** ("Rush Yds", "Rec TDs") rather than a group header over a partial triple — that is Q16's own option (c), and a header promising three columns while delivering two is the half-built lie L.C3.3 declined to ship; the ruling is about shipping the *data*. Groups reassemble when F81 completes each triple. `receptions` ships beside them — the blob carries it, §16.4 never listed it, and the reason to withhold it never existed. (3) C43's "no fake/empty columns ever ship" is untouched at either granularity. (4) His *"maybe we can calculate our own projections or derive them"* is filed as an **IDEA, not a task** (tasks-AP §8 item 1).

- **D203 — `draft_adjust_budget` joins the E2 contract, in exactly the shape F82 recorded.** A re-read of `087:650–820` confirms the row: the write is `v_after := v_before + p_delta` (`087:730–731`) with no `p_action_id` in the signature (`087:650–655`), while the other three auction commissioner verbs self-guard on replay. Add `p_action_id UUID DEFAULT NULL` (nullable, so no caller breaks and system paths can pass NULL) plus the select-then-insert replay under the draft-row lock (`066:915–920`), keyed in `uniq_draft_bid_action`'s partial-unique pattern, minted per submit at the hook the way the D68 verbs already do (`use-draft-controls.ts:142/144`). **The replay must return the ORIGINAL result**, not a fresh success — a retry reporting a different `adjustment_after` than the first call is a second lie on top of the first. Not a live-data hazard today (every adjustment is audited and an equal-and-opposite delta corrects one), which is why it is AP.6 and not a hotfix. **Also stated in AP.6's banner so nobody infers otherwise: an `action_id` is an idempotency key, not an audit record — `commissioner_actions` is still M6 (F32/F40).**

**2026-08-20 — Builder (AP.3, migration 091, PR TBD).**

- **D213 — Reactive CPU bidding as BUILT: the loop that replaced the recursion, the curve that has no constants, and the two things this task deliberately did not do.** (1) **AP.3 was taken OUT of tasks-AP §7's order** — AP.1 and AP.2 are still open. §7's serialization is a *head-authoring* rule (each `CREATE OR REPLACE` against the chain HEAD's file text, D137), not a logical dependency: AP.3 reads no setting AP.1 changes and no code path AP.2 adds, and AP.1/AP.2 will simply author against 091's heads when they land. Chris is waiting on the bots, so the bots went first. **This is the only ordering deviation and it is recorded rather than inferred.** (2) **The responder LOOPS; D200(3) described it RECURSING.** Both write the same ladder in the same transaction with the same `2 × team_count` cap and the same loud `RAISE EXCEPTION`; the loop keeps the counter in one place and bounds the call stack, whereas recursion would need an out-of-band per-transaction depth counter to enforce a per-transaction cap at all. The loop's cost is one transaction-local re-entrancy flag (`fieldscout.mock_cpu_responding`, `set_config(..., is_local => TRUE)` — rolled back with the (sub)transaction, so a failure trapped inside `draft_tick`'s ARM 2.6(c) cannot leave it stuck on), because the responder's own writes come back through the bid writer's reactive arm. (2b) **THE LADDER BOUND IS `GREATEST(2 × team_count, auction_budget)`, NOT D200(3)'s `2 × team_count` — and the change was forced by a measurement, not by taste.** D200(3) fixed the number on the premise that *"in practice jump-bids make the real ladder a handful of steps"*, and **on the shipped default shape that premise holds**: a full 12-team × 15-slot × $200 mock measured a LONGEST ladder of **13 raises against a cap of 24**. But a legal league can be degenerate — `league-settings.ts:444` requires only `startingSum ≥ 1`, `bench` may be 0, and `auction_budget` runs to $1000 — and on an 8-team × 2-slot × $200 board every franchise can afford ≈ $199 for one player, so the price grinds up a dollar at a time through seven willing seats and the ladder runs past 16. **pgTAP found this, not reasoning** — and the evidence is now a PIN rather than a story (039 **§C5**). **Correction of record:** an earlier draft of this entry cited §C3 and described the tripping board loosely; the section that trips the narrow bound is **§C5**, and its companion **§C6** is a deliberately MINIMISED reproduction that rewrites `nomination_order` to **two** entries — and a 2-seat board is **not a legal league** (§7.2 / changelog v2.6 lock `team_count` to 8/10/12/14/16), so §C6 on its own proves nothing about a shippable configuration. **§C5 therefore drives the grind on a LEGAL 8-team board** (seven CPU seats, the eighth the human, $200 budget, 2-slot roster — every clause passes `validateSettings`) from a directly-inserted draft row with a FIXED id, so the rung count is a stored literal: **24 raises from a $175 open**, against `2 × team_count` = 16. Swept wider on the same legal board — 120 ladders over mixed openings and seeds — **mean 8.8 rungs, max 34, and 16 of 120 (13%) past 16**, so the narrow bound would have fired on roughly one contested nomination in eight. The exception's diagnosis ("the value model or the candidate scan is wrong") would have been FALSE every time, because a nibble grind through willing seats is precisely the texture Chris asked for. A tripwire that fires on correct behaviour and then lies about why is worse than no tripwire — and on the human bid path it takes the human's own bid down with it. The bound used instead is **structural**: every rung raises by ≥ $1, no rung exceeds its bidder's max bid and no max bid exceeds the league's budget, so a legitimate ladder can never have more rungs than a franchise has dollars. D200(3)'s number is kept as the FLOOR (it is the larger of the two in a tiny-budget league), and **D200(3)'s intent is preserved exactly** — bound it, fail loudly, never a silent `EXIT`; what changes is that the exception now only fires on something that cannot legally happen, which is what makes it worth raising. The exception text was reworded to name what a breach actually implies. **Consequence, filed rather than buried: F93** — on such a degenerate shape a ladder of tens of rungs also blows §4.6's 50 ms held-lock budget, which the default shape does not (measured: ≤ 21 ms). (3) **The reactive arm went to the WRITER, not to three callers** — `draft_place_bid_internal` — so the invariant is "every bid in a mock auction provokes a response" rather than "three call sites remembered to", and `draft_place_bid` inherited it for free without being replaced. Both RPCs that can return a post-ladder state (`draft_place_bid`, `draft_nominate`) **re-read the draft row** before returning: the ladder moved the high bid, and §8.1 says an RPC returns the NEW authoritative state, so returning the row it wrote would hand the room a price the server had already superseded. (4) **THE CURVE, stated so a future session can tell a deliberate change from a drift:** `P(jump) = headroom / ceiling`; a jump is `LEAST(high + 1 + round(r × ceiling), ceiling)`; otherwise `high + 1`; `headroom ≤ 1` short-circuits with no draw. **It has no tunable constants** — the taper Chris described ("everyone spams bid until a player gets closer to their average cost value") is STRUCTURAL: as the price nears value the gap shrinks and the jump probability falls to nearly zero on its own. The `LEAST(…, ceiling)` clamp is load-bearing (E62) and is the break probe's target. Both draws come from `draft_mock_unit_random` — the D93 24-bit construction **EXTRACTED VERBATIM** out of `draft_mock_cpu_bid_value` rather than copied (D200(4): a second PRNG is a review finding), proved lossless by 038 §A's stored literals staying green. (5) **Failure containment is deliberately ASYMMETRIC:** inside `draft_tick` the existing ARM 2.6(c) handler traps a responder failure per draft (089's contract, unchanged); on the HUMAN path a responder failure propagates and rolls the human's own bid back. A mock is practice, and a bot bug that silently ate itself while the room carried on is exactly the "nothing happened means it worked" failure CLAUDE.md names. (6) **A CONSEQUENCE, stated rather than left to be discovered: `realistic` vs `fast` no longer has any RAISE think-time to govern.** §8.8's ruling makes a response untimed by construction, so the toggle now governs the NOMINATION think and ARM 2.5's snake picks only — and 089's "anti-snipe becomes VISIBLE in a mock" texture (a CPU raise landing inside the final seconds) is lost on the reactive path. Folded to spec **v2.13.1** as an erratum on §8.8's toggle bullet. (7) **NOT DONE, and filed rather than smuggled in: the CPU NOMINATION still rides the sweep.** D200(1)'s parenthetical — "the award already advances the rotation, so a CPU whose turn it is to nominate can nominate in that same transaction too" — is not in AP.3's item list and is not built; it is **F92**, with the measured cost on the row. (7b) **WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT MEASURED, and why — because lane rule 10 is satisfied by measuring what you CLAIM, not by measuring everything.** The full-size figure below is an **AFTER-only** measurement: a 12-team × 15-slot × $200 mock on 091's engine, driven start → `complete` through the real 5-second cron. **The matching ≈ 4-hour full-size BASELINE was not run**, on the orchestrator's ruling, for three recorded reasons: (a) the decision-relevant number is already measured, and the strongest fact in it is not a multiplier but the **0.0-second bidding term** — the ladder no longer costs wall clock at all, which is the thing AP.3 existed to fix; (b) the baseline would have occupied the local stack for four hours, and that stack is Chris's own testing environment, which is a bad trade for measuring a state we are deleting; (c) the "before" is not in dispute — Chris drove it and described it independently, and the **8-team × 2-slot × $20 A/B is a measured before/after on a real board** (11m37s → 6m41s, 86 → 36 bid rows, identical final board). **So the before/after MULTIPLIER in this task is measured at the 8×2×$20 shape only.** A larger multiplier at full size is expected — that shape spends $2 400 across 180 players against $86 across 16, so there are roughly 2 200 dollar-steps for jumping to remove instead of 70 — but that expectation is a **PREDICTION and is labelled one everywhere it appears**; no session may quote it as a result. (8) **Coverage MOVED, never deleted:** 038 §C/§D's F61 gate and think-time pins now run on a KICKER market (`draft_mock_cpu_need` prices K/DST at 0 for every seat, D163/R406), because on an ordinary player the launcher is no longer the standing high bidder a moment after nominating and the self-raise discriminator would be unreachable. The raise-side coverage 038 §D used to carry (the selection rule, the anti-snipe floor under a CPU raise) moved to **039**, against the behaviour that actually ships; §D gained the FOLD side of both (a fold never touches the clock, and the argmax read at the bottom of its range).
- **D214 — `auction_min_bid` as RETIRED: what the twelve heads actually were, why one helper serves two jobs and never the third, and the two consequences worth writing down.** (1) **THE HEAD SET IS TWELVE, AND THE BREAKDOWN'S SIXTEEN WAS A RAW COUNT.** tasks-AP §1.3 measured 16 assignment sites and said the real set was smaller; resolved at task time with `grep -lE '^CREATE (OR REPLACE )?FUNCTION +(public\.)?<name>\(' supabase/migrations/*.sql`, the LIVE set is **12 functions across five head files** — 084 (`draft_team_budget`, `draft_auction_solvent`, `draft_start_internal`), 087 (`draft_adjust_budget`, `draft_force_pick`), 089 (`create_mock_draft`), 090 (`draft_reassign_pick`, `draft_move_player`), 091 (`draft_place_bid_internal`, `draft_system_nominate_internal`, `draft_nominate`, `draft_tick`). **§1.3's table also MISSED two live sites** — `draft_force_pick` (087:2175, the commissioner force-nomination opens AT the floor) and `create_mock_draft` (089:1036, the practice-refusal message) — and listed one that had died: `draft_place_bid`'s own read (085:646) went away when 089 made its tail delegate to `draft_place_bid_internal`, so `draft_place_bid` is NOT replaced here. Every claimed range was re-checked to land on its own `CREATE OR REPLACE` line before extraction, and the per-function `diff -u` hunk counts are in 092's banner (12 replacements, **43 hunks, +131/−81** in total, re-derived from the SHIPPED file after the last fix cycle). (2) **ONE HELPER SERVES TWO JOBS AND IS FORBIDDEN THE THIRD — that is the ruling, not a compromise of it.** Chris ruled *"We can't have one function serving both. Nomination and Min Bid need to be different"*; the two things he named are the **nomination floor** and the **bid increment**. The retired field did THREE jobs (§7.3.8's removed row): the per-slot reserve, the nomination floor, and — never — the increment. D198(1) collapses the first two, which were already the same variable in every body, into `draft_auction_reserve(jsonb)`; the increment stays the literal `p_amount <= v_high_bid` in `draft_place_bid_internal` and **is not inside any hunk in this migration**. The code says which job it is doing at each site rather than leaving it to be inferred: the local is `v_reserve` where the number is the §8.6.1 reserve term and `v_nom_floor` in the three pure-floor bodies, and the refusal copy now says *per-slot reserve* / *nomination floor* / *price floor* where it used to say *minimum bid*. **The conflation is a pinned defect, not a convention:** pgTAP 040 §F and 034 §N drive the floor and the increment on ONE league toggled, and break probe B (below) shows both RED the moment the toggle reaches the raise clause. (3) **THE HELPER IS DELIBERATELY NOT STRICT.** `COALESCE((NULL::jsonb->>'x')::int, 1)` was 1; a STRICT helper would answer NULL on a NULL config and turn every downstream `max_bid` into a silent unknown — the exact shape CLAUDE.md's *never let "nothing happened" mean "it worked"* rule names. Pinned twice: the value (040 §A) and the catalog flag (`not proisstrict`, 040 §H). (4) **THE REFUSAL COPY HAD TO MOVE, and two messages were pointing at a knob that no longer exists.** `draft_start_internal`'s two arms and `create_mock_draft`'s practice refusal ended *"or lower the minimum bid in League settings → Draft setup"*. They now end *"or allow $0 nominations"*. This is the one behavioural change outside the arithmetic, and every pin that asserted the old strings moved with them (033/034/035/036/038 + `auction-commish-api-db.test.ts`). (5) **CONSEQUENCE — AND THE ONE THING THIS BUILDER GOT WRONG, CORRECTED IN PLACE AT REVIEW (R456; spec v2.13.3 withdraws v2.13.2's erratum 2).** The claim shipped in the first revision was that §7.3.8's auction solvency arm is *vacuous for schema-valid settings in both columns*, because `auction_budget ≥ 50` and `deriveRosterSize` *"tops out at 20 starters + 20 bench + 6 IR = 46"*. **That premise is FALSE and is withdrawn.** The 20-slot starting cap is not a schema bound — it is a **sibling arm of the very same validator** (`league-settings.ts`, the `startingSum < 1 || startingSum > 20` push); `rosterSettingsSchema` declares `starting_slots: z.array(startingSlotSchema)` with **no `.max()`** and bounds only each slot's `count` at 10. **Measured at the layer the claim was about** (30 slots × `count` 10, `auction_budget: 50`): `leagueSettingsSchema.parse` → **OK**, `deriveRosterSize` → **307**, `validateLeagueSettings` → `["roster_settings.starting_slots", "draft.auction_budget"]`, solvency message *"Auction budget (50) can't fill a 307-player roster at the $1 per-slot reserve — needs at least 307."* **The true statement is weaker and more useful:** at reserve 1 the arm is REDUNDANT WITH ITS SIBLING — nothing violates solvency without violating the roster-size bullet too — so it never fires *alone*. Redundancy between two arms of one validator is not vacuity. **Why the distinction is load-bearing rather than pedantic:** on the strength of the false premise this PR had already downgraded `settings-round-trip-db.test.ts`'s §7.3.8 per-field case to a Zod-range check, losing the only API-surface assertion that the solvency message and its field are wired — and **measured under a probe that made the arm dead code (`if (false && …)`), the downgraded test stayed GREEN while the restored one goes RED.** A guard recorded as vacuous is a guard the next session deletes. **Fixed here:** the per-field case is restored with an oversized `starting_slots` array against a $50 budget (asserting the field, the 307 number, *per-slot reserve*, AND the sibling arm firing beside it), the Zod-layer `auction_budget: 49` case is KEPT as a separate claim about a separate layer, and a new unit pin asserts the arm firing on a **Zod-parsed** object — the pin that would have caught the premise. **The species matters more than the instance:** this is §4 rule 9's exact failure — a claim about a layer inferred from a printed bullet rather than observed at that layer, written in the proved register beside claims that genuinely were proved. Everything else in this PR that was MEASURED held up under an independent re-derivation; the single item that was reasoned about did not. (6) **THE DATA MIGRATION WAS REHEARSED, NOT REASONED ABOUT.** Section 14 is a one-shot `DO` block, so a per-run pgTAP file cannot re-run it; 040 §G pins the MAPPING and the whole-database post-condition and says which is which. The block itself was driven on the local stack against planted rows — 4 leagues (min-bid 0/1/2/5) and 2 draft configs (0/3) — and produced, verbatim: the `>= 2` cohort NOTICEd by id for both stores, `retired auction_min_bid from 4 league(s) (1 => $0 nominations ON, 3 => OFF) and 2 draft config(s) (1 ON, 1 OFF)`, a second run reporting *nothing to convert*, and — with one value forced to `"abc"` — an ERROR naming the row and leaving it untouched. Transcript in the AP.1 PR. (7) **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE:** no named `AUCTION_BID_INCREMENT` constant (D199(1) reserves the named increment for **AP.2**, whose uncontestable predicate needs `high_bid + increment`); no change to `draft_place_bid` (089's head delegates and inherits); no touch to 091/AP.3's reactive-CPU arms, which sit outside every hunk; and no fix to the `draft-board-autopick-db` red, which is `main`'s and is **F94**.
- **D215 — The uncontestable instant award: the order Chris corrected mid-build, why the extraction had to be proved first, the third path nobody listed, and what is deliberately absent.** (1) **THE ORDER WAS RULED MID-TASK AND THE BUILD FOLLOWS THE RULING, NOT THE BRIEF.** This session was briefed with the message running BEFORE the award — a 3-second beat at the end of which the award lands. Chris corrected it in the middle of the build: *"No you've misunderstood. It awards the player immediately and then displays that message for 3 seconds until the next nomination."* So the server finds the nomination uncontestable and awards it **immediately, atomically, in that same determination**, and the 3 seconds is a display/pacing beat over an already-painted board, living in the gap before the next nomination opens. **What had been built for the pre-award version, and was removed:** two migration-banner sections (item 3's "announcement then board, in order" framing and an item 4 titled "THE RACE, ANSWERED"), one comment on the extracted award's phase guard claiming it "makes a double award structurally impossible", and the client's render ordering (the beat had been designed to replace the board for its 3 seconds; it now runs over it). **No pending-award state, no re-check-at-expiry, no cancellation path and no double-fire guard was ever coded** — the design was atomic from the first line of SQL because D199(4) already specified one transaction — so the correction cost prose and one component decision, not machinery. Spec **v2.13.4** folds it, because §8.6.9 and §16.5.4 both printed the wrong order and E67 repeated it.
- **D215 (cont.) — the general principle, which reaches past this task.** (2) Chris, same session: *"but a commish can pause a draft and change anything or someone can disconnect at any time. TBH in drafts that's known as a 'personal problem'"*. **Pause → change → resume is the sanctioned mechanism** (§8.7); a live window owes no defence against edits that belong inside a pause, and a mid-auction disconnect is what §8.6.2's system nomination exists for. Prefer decide-and-commit-in-one-step, then display the outcome. This does **not** relax genuine server-side races: two writers on one row, double submission of one RPC and §8.1/E2 idempotency stand exactly as before. The distinction — *defend against two writers, not against a person changing their mind* — is now spec text at §8.6.9, so the absence of those paths reads as a ruling instead of an oversight the next session "fixes".
- **D215 (cont.) — the build mechanics.** (3) **THE EXTRACTION'S LOSSLESSNESS WAS PROVED BEFORE THE SECOND CALLER EXISTED (the 087/R367 discipline, run as an actual build step).** ARM 2.6(b)'s 191 lines (092:3471–3661) became `draft_award_nomination_internal`, de-indented by exactly 8 spaces — `diff` of before and after under `sed 's/^[[:space:]]*//'` is EMPTY, so the move changed no non-whitespace character — with **one** substantive line changed (`v_auc_completed := … + 1` → `v_completed := TRUE`, because the counter belongs to the sweep and the answer belongs to the award). A variant of 093 carrying the extraction and the predicate but **not** the wiring was built and run: 41 files / **2855** assertions with 034, 035's behavioural half, 036, 037, 038 and 039 fully green, and exactly **three** failures — every one a `prosrc` / `pg_get_functiondef` SOURCE pin naming `draft_tick`'s body (035 §8's completion-writer delegation, 038 §135's R408 award-lookup scope, 040 §8's twelve-reserve-readers count). All three were RE-POINTED, none relaxed, and 035 and 040 each gained a **second** assertion so the delegation is pinned at both links rather than moved from one to the other. (4) **THE HEAD SET IS 092 FOR ALL FOUR, AND THE BREAKDOWN'S CITATIONS ARE STALE.** tasks-AP §AP.2 cites `089:2480–2671` and `089:658`; 091 and then 092 replaced those bodies. Re-derived at task time with `grep -lE '^CREATE (OR REPLACE )?FUNCTION +(public\.)?<name>\(' supabase/migrations/*.sql`, every claimed range re-checked to start on its own `CREATE OR REPLACE` line: `draft_tick` 092:2542–3749 · `draft_nominate` 092:2273–2529 · `draft_system_nominate_internal` 092:2155–2260 · `draft_force_pick` 092:858–1117. Per-function hunks: **3 (+17/−195) · 2 (+51/−9) · 2 (+33/−10) · 3 (+29/−2)**. (5) **THERE ARE THREE NOMINATION PATHS AND THE BREAKDOWN NAMED TWO.** `draft_force_pick`'s auction arm IS a nomination (087/R301 — a commissioner "pick for a manager" on an auction opens one at the floor, with its own `draft_bids` row and its own phase flip), and §8.6.9 is written about nominations with no qualifier on who opened one. Wiring it follows LAW rather than widening scope — tasks-AP's own preamble says the spec wins where the two disagree — and the precedent for this exact function being missed by this exact lane is **D214(1)**, where AP.1 found it absent from §1.3's read-site table. Pinned in 041 §F.
- **D215 (cont.) — the wire and the client.** (6) The uncontestable path performs two `drafts` UPDATEs in one transaction: the ordinary phase flip carrying an additive `"uncontested": true` and a **NULL** `current_deadline` (E67's "no bid clock is ever opened", made true on the wire and not only in the row), then the award. Both fire 070's row trigger, so the room learns of it with **no new column, event name or topic**. Two consequences worth writing down: **(a) the key never comes to rest** — both statements commit together, so by the time any SELECT can run `current_nomination` is already NULL, which is what makes §16.5.4's "a reconnect cannot lose the award", "a late joiner sees the completed award" and "never show it twice" structural rather than a matter of client discipline; **(b) `realtime.messages` exposes NO ordering key for two rows written in one commit** — measured: identical `inserted_at` (the transaction timestamp) and a random-uuid `id` — so 041 §H asserts SET MEMBERSHIP rather than a sequence. Under the corrected order that is exactly right: the award is committed either way, so a client processing the two payloads in either order paints the same board and shows the same message. (7) **THE CLIENT LATCHES AT THE PAYLOAD, NOT AT A RENDER, and it is the one non-obvious client decision.** Both events land in one commit, so React can coalesce them into a single render and a `useEffect` watching `current_nomination` would then never observe the marker at all; `useDraftRoom`'s broadcast handler sees every payload exactly once whatever React does with the renders. The 3 000 ms is ONE exported constant, the sentence is composed in ONE function (so Q18's ruling is a one-line change), the instant is read through `systemTime` — D3's one sanctioned wall-clock seam — and a PURE decision function decides while the timers only wake the component. **THAT SENTENCE WAS FALSE AS FIRST SHIPPED, AND REVIEW CAUGHT IT (R464) — recorded because the species matters more than the instance.** The first revision computed the decision against a `nowMs` held in component STATE whose only writers were the initialiser and a `setTimeout` callback, which made the timeout **the sole writer that could retire the message**: measured, it was still visible at t+4000 and t+9000, and background tabs clamp `setTimeout`, so that is ordinary rather than exotic. The docblock claimed the opposite in the proved register — **§4 rule 9 again, and the third time this lane has caught a claim about a post-change world written from the INTENT of the change rather than observed** (D214(5), R463, this). §16.5.4 is LAW that the beat is *"exactly 3 seconds … on every client"*, so **the code moved, not the claim** — withdrawing it would have left shipped behaviour violating the spec, which is the move AP.1's blocker punished. **As fixed:** the whole decision is `uncontestedBeatSentence`, a pure function of the latched beat and a sampled instant, and the component samples **at render** through `systemTime`, so every render re-decides and no timer can gate the answer; an exact-boundary `setTimeout` keeps "exactly 3 seconds" exact and a 500 ms `UNCONTESTED_BEAT_SAMPLE_MS` interval, cleared at the boundary, covers the clamped-tab case a timeout cannot. Every clock read on this path is `systemTime` — **the fix does not depend on F97's unfixed `Date.now()` and does not deepen it**, and the two hooks are deliberately not merged (they live in different components, so sharing one sampler would mean rehoming shipped L.C3.1 code and dragging F97 in). (8) **DELIBERATELY NOT DONE:** no server-side `pg_sleep`, scheduled action, `pg_net` or second cron (tasks-AP §4 rule 11 / D199(5)); **no client-side copy of the §8.6.9 predicate** — the server decides, and a TS mirror here would have been the third copy of the max-bid family that **F95** exists to prevent; no touch to `draft_place_bid` / `draft_place_bid_internal` (a bid can never meet an uncontestable nomination — pinned); no re-issue of `cron.schedule` (§22.3); no §7.3.8 knob (Chris ruled the rule, not a setting); and no fix to `draft-board-autopick-db`, which is `main`'s **F94** and was re-baselined this session on a `main` worktree against a `main`-chain database (`draft_nomination_uncontestable` present 0 times) failing identically.


**2026-08-17 — Architect (the draft-room redesign breakdown, PR #155 — merged 2026-08-17; transcribed verbatim from `tasks-DR-draft-room-redesign.md` §3 per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 / tasks-M3 D126–D143 precedent.** *Folded late, by the **DR.1** Builder on 2026-08-18: PR #155's own §6 owed this transcription "at merge" and the merge landed without it, so §4 ran D146 → D157 with the ten numbers D157 had just been renumbered around. Discharged here rather than left for DR.2 to trip over — the same PR also files the §6 row #155 owed, as **F63**.)*

- **D147 — The room escapes the shell by moving the guard up, not by duplicating it.** `src/app/app/layout.tsx` today does auth + username gate + `<AppShell>` in one component (:12–40). It splits: the **layout keeps the guards and becomes a pass-through**, and `<AppShell>` moves down into a route group `src/app/app/(shell)/layout.tsx` that holds every existing route, with the room in a sibling group `src/app/app/(room)/leagues/[leagueId]/draft/`. **Route groups do not affect URLs**, so `/app/leagues/[id]/draft` is unchanged — no redirect, no link rewrite, no broken deep link, and the `DraftBar`'s own-room path check keeps working. Chosen over the alternatives deliberately: a `usePathname()` conditional inside `AppShell` would make every app route pay for the room's special case and would still mount the shell's providers; a separate top-level `/draft/…` URL would break every shipped link and the spec's §16.1 route table. **The guard is not duplicated into two layouts** — one copy, above both groups, is what keeps cold-load auth honest (D148).
- **D148 — Cold-load correctness is an acceptance criterion with a named adversary.** A new browser tab is a server-rendered cold start with no client history, and so is a refresh mid-draft; the new-tab ruling makes this the *primary* path rather than an edge case. **Observation recorded 2026-08-17 (Chris, in two browsers):** loading the live draft URL directly bounced to `/app?redirect=%2Fapp%2Fleagues%2F…%2Fdraft` while in-app click-through worked. Two mechanisms exist and the Builder must distinguish them by evidence rather than assume:
  **(a) the dev-auth artifact (likely, and benign in production).** `devAutoLogin` (`src/lib/supabase/dev-auth.ts:26–45`) is a **client-side** `signInWithPassword`. On the very first cold load of a fresh browser there is no session cookie yet, so the server sees an anonymous request and `middleware.ts:36–42` redirects; the browser then signs in, and every later request has a cookie. That produces exactly the observed two-hop shape (`/app/leagues/…/draft` → `/login?redirect=…` → middleware's :45–50 branch sees a user, rewrites the pathname to `/app` and **keeps the search params** because it clones `nextUrl`, landing on `/app?redirect=…`).
  **(b) a real, production-plausible defect found while diagnosing (a).** `src/middleware.ts` writes refreshed auth cookies onto `supabaseResponse` via `setAll` (:18–27) but **both redirect branches return a brand-new `NextResponse.redirect(...)` (:41 and :49), which does not carry those cookies.** This is the documented `@supabase/ssr` footgun: a cold load holding an expired-but-refreshable token can be bounced *and* lose the refresh. It is not reachable through in-app client-side navigation, which is exactly why the redesign — whose primary entry is a cold tab — is what would surface it.
  **The task's obligation is to prove which one it is, on a real (non-dev-auth) session, and to leave a test rather than a memory** (DR.1, DR.8). Filed as ledger row **F63** so the routing is findable. *(Transcription correction, DR.1 2026-08-18: this sentence read **F61** when the breakdown was authored, and the entry's own §6 marked the number provisional per R312 first-filed-keeps. PR #156 filed F61/F62 first, so this row is **F63** — the number D158(4) reserved for exactly this re-point. Nothing else in this decision changed.)* *(Recorded but out of scope to celebrate: `login/page.tsx:24/:51` does honor `?redirect=`, so once a user logs in they do land in the room — the destination is preserved through the login page and lost only by middleware's `/login → /app` rewrite.)*
- **D149 — Three zones, two bands of chrome, and the on-the-clock line resolves INTO the status strip rather than becoming a third band.** The brief flagged three candidates competing for the top (the 54px bar, the Live/Round/order strip, and the on-the-clock line). They resolve to **two**: the command bar (54px, ink, pinned) and the status strip (`h-header` = 58px, the existing token). Chris's "move it to the left side of **the div**" is read as the div it already lives in — the status strip's flex row (`snake-draft-room.tsx:719–765`), where it currently sits **right-aligned next to the clock** (:743–759). Moving it left makes one band whose two ends read *whose turn* and *how long*, which is a better answer than a dedicated band and costs 112px of vertical chrome instead of ~170px. **A third band is out of scope and a Builder proposing one has left it.**
- **D150 — The dock is a NON-MODAL drawer, and that single choice settles most of its behavior.** The panels overlay the board; the board, the clock, the command bar and the presence strip stay visible and operable behind them. Therefore: **no focus trap, nothing `inert`, no scroll lock, no backdrop that swallows clicks** — a user must be able to watch the clock while browsing the pool, which is the entire draft-night workflow. Escape closes; clicking the active tab toggles it closed; **exactly one panel is open at a time** (two open panels is a rail again). Focus moves to the panel on open and **returns to the tab button** on close. Default state is **closed**. **This is deliberately NOT the shipped `Sheet`/Radix Dialog primitive**, which traps focus and marks the rest of the page inert by design — using it here would make the board unreadable while the pool is open. The dock is a plain positioned region with `role="tabpanel"`/`aria-expanded` wiring, not a modal.
- **D151 — Open height is fixed, and the board never resizes.** The open panel occupies a fixed fraction of the viewport (`min(60vh, …)` desktop / ~75vh mobile — the Builder pins the exact token) and is **absolutely positioned over** the board. The board's own geometry — the grid's `minmax(96px, 1fr)` columns and its horizontal scroll (`draft-board-grid.tsx:53–105`) — **must not change when a panel opens or closes**: a board that re-lays-out on every tab press is the thing a full-width board was asked for to avoid. No drag-to-resize in v1 (a resize handle on a drawer that overlays a horizontally-scrolling grid is a pointer-conflict problem worth its own task, not a freebie).
- **D152 — Elevation: the dock panels and the command bar are BOTH sanctioned resting shadows, and each says why in a comment.** CLAUDE.md's ruling is that nothing in normal flow rests elevated and shadows appear only behind an interaction prefix — **with an explicit exception for true overlays and for bars pinned over scrolling content**. The dock panels are true overlays (they float above the board); the 54px command bar is pinned chrome over scrolling content. Both therefore keep a resting `shadow-hard-*` **with a comment naming the exception**, exactly as `src/components/ui/elevation-rule.test.ts:38`'s `OVERLAY_FILES` allowlist requires of shared primitives — and any new file the test's sweep covers is added to that allowlist with its reason, never silenced. **Everything else the redesign touches obeys the ordinary rule:** the status strip does not rest elevated, and selected/on-the-clock/active states stay carried by fill (`bg-accent-soft`) or border (`border-accent`), never by a shadow.
- **D153 — `Draft Options` is a menu over the SHIPPED panel body, not a reimplementation of it.** CLAUDE.md forbids near-duplicate components, and `commish-draft-panel.tsx` is 956 lines of working, reviewed, refusal-aware controls. The menu lists the control groups; choosing one opens the existing panel at that section. **What actually changes in that file is its trigger** — the blue `Commish panel` button (:120–123) is deleted and the panel becomes trigger-less, opened by the bar. The eight sections keep their bodies, their gates, their confirm dialogs and their system-post semantics. **Nothing about §8.7's control semantics changes in this lane** — no new refusal, no relaxed one, no altered audit or chat behavior.
- **D154 — On a mock, the command bar is the launcher's bar, because a mock has no commissioner.** `isCommish` is already `false` on every mock (`snake-draft-room.tsx:443`, D110(1)). The bar's three variants are therefore: **commissioner** (Pause/Resume + Draft Options + status + Exit), **member** (status + Exit), **mock** (MOCK identity + status + Exit, plus — for `config.mock.launched_by` only — Pause/Resume practice and a reduced *Practice options* menu carrying delete-and-exit). The `MockBanner` at `:712` is **absorbed into the bar** rather than stacked beneath it (§16.5.4's v2.12 note): a permanent bar plus a permanent banner saying the same thing is the duplication §16.3's say-a-thing-once rule exists to stop. **No commissioner control becomes reachable on a mock** — the reduced menu carries only what D110(1) already permits the launcher.
- **D155 — The pause overlay stops narrating and starts illustrating.** With the bar announcing "Draft paused by @commish" for everyone, `DraftPauseOverlay`'s duplicate copy is retired; the board keeps a *visual* paused treatment (dimmed, non-interactive) and the clock keeps its shipped paused rendering (`pick-clock.tsx`'s paused mode). **The Resume affordance moves to where the actor is** — the bar's Resume button for a commissioner, the same for a mock's launcher — so `canResume`/`onResume` (`pause-overlay.tsx:38`, wired at `snake-draft-room.tsx:604`) lose their button rather than their meaning. One state, one voice, one place to act.
- **D156 — The two-tabs guard is a courtesy over a correctness boundary, and is scoped to say so.** *(**RULED by Chris 2026-08-17** — "The most recent one takes over and the others disconnect"; PROGRESS §3 **Q14** Resolved. This decision is now built, not proposed.)* The server is authoritative (§8.1), so two tabs can never corrupt a draft — a stale tab's action is refused by the same validators as anyone else's. What two tabs *do* cost is real but bounded: two sockets and two `draft:<id>` subscriptions against §9.3's ≤3-channel budget, two `draft_touch` heartbeats, and a presence list that shows one manager twice (presence is keyed by team id — `use-draft.ts:244`). The guard is therefore **client-local leader election** (`BroadcastChannel` keyed by draft id, `localStorage` fallback): newest tab holds the room, older tabs unsubscribe, stop the heartbeat, and render a takeover state. **Per browser profile, not per user** — a laptop and a phone are two legitimate clients and are left alone. **It adds no channel, no route, no server state.**

(5) **THE SCORING FAMILY COMES FROM THE LEAGUE'S OWN FROZEN RULES, NEVER FROM A DEFAULT.** "Projected points" is one of three `players` columns, chosen by the league's per-reception coefficient read from `leagues.scoring_rules_snapshot` (§7.3.3's frozen copy — 059's guard makes it non-null for any league in `drafting`+). A MOCK runs while its league is still `setup`/`scheduled` with no snapshot, so the read falls back to the chosen `scoring_systems.rules`, world-readable for the template rows every shipped league uses (058). If NEITHER resolves the family is **null**, the two dependent columns render "—" and the panel says *"Scoring not readable — projections hidden"*: §16.5.4's "never wrong numbers" forbids substituting half-PPR-because-it-is-usually-half-PPR. Cuts sit at the MIDPOINTS (0.25 / 0.75) so a league on 0.4 lands on the nearer family; both boundary instants pinned, plus the three shipped template values (0 / 0.5 / 1). (6) **DND IS A LABEL, AND THE PIN IS AN ENUMERATION, NOT A HOPE.** The write is a direct own-row RLS INSERT/DELETE — §12.24 ships the `FOR ALL` policy precisely so the client can own its prep, the `draft_queues` class the banner names — with no route and no channel (§9.2: marks are never broadcast). C42's ruling is pinned four ways: every SQL reference in the whole chain is 083's DDL and nothing else (comments stripped, so 088's own "still carries NO broadcast" note cannot satisfy it); **no dollar-quoted FUNCTION BODY anywhere mentions the table** (a skip would have to live in one); `src/lib/leagues/**` never names it; and the whole of `src/` reads it from exactly two dispositioned files. `filterRows` cannot even SEE the mark — pinned by reading its body. (7) **PERSISTED COLUMN STATE IS SAFE HERE FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON, NOT A LUCKY ONE.** The banner left persistence to the Builder; it persists (the `rail-store` shape) because draft rooms get RELOADED — a two-tab takeover, a reconnect, a second device — and rebuilding a table layout while a nomination clock runs is the wrong moment to make anyone re-pick anything. The usual hydration hazard cannot reach it: the dock's state starts CLOSED (`DockState = null`) and only a click opens it, so nothing this store feeds has ever been part of a server render — pinned, with the obligation recorded for any future host that renders on the server. The transition function stays in the ops layer (`columnsReducer` + `columnsAreDefault`), so the customizer's behaviour is golden-pinned without a DOM. (8) **THE BOUNDED WINDOW IS HONEST BY CONSTRUCTION.** Show Drafted, Favorites and §8.9's "Only this list" each promise a SET the ADP window need not contain, so all three feed ONE by-id read (`useAuctionPlayersByIds`) that merges with the window and dedupes — the "exactly 1000 rows" rule applied to a filter. That read CHUNKS its ids (300 at a time) rather than trusting one `.in()` against PostgREST's 1000-row cap, and it counts as pending only when it was actually asked for something (R283's disabled-query gate, restated for a second read). §8.9's overlay is carried over deliberately: re-parenting the panel must not silently cost the auction a shipped L.B4.2 capability. **CORRECTED 2026-08-20 (R445 batch — see D196):** as first shipped this claim was only HALF true. The capability's rows came across; its HONESTY did not — `overlayRows` appeared in neither the loading gate nor the error gate, so a failed or still-pending §8.9 read fell through to *"No players on this list are still available."* on a board where every player was available. `available-players.tsx:235` had shipped both halves (`onlyMode ? overlayRows.isError : pool.isError`, its own copy, its own retry, plus R283's `poolLoadPending`). D196 pays the honesty half and replaces the per-source special-casing with the enumerated gates. (9) **AN EMPTY TABLE SAYS WHY — and the first version of it lied.** `emptyReason` was written cheapest-first, `totalRows === 0` before the filter checks. Search and position narrow SERVER-side, so a term matching nobody empties `totalRows` itself, and a user who typed "zzzz" was told **"The player pool is empty."** — measured live at 1280, fixed to check active filters first, and pinned in both directions. Every branch's copy is true under COMPOSITION too, which is what makes the ordering a fix rather than a relocation. CLAUDE.md's "never let *nothing happened* mean *it worked*", in its empty-state form.
