- **D193 — L.C3.2 build mechanics (the commissioner auction rows; F72's disabled-states half and F77 discharged; the settings/lobby/recap spend surfaces).** **Number note (D161's grep-together rule):** R, D and F swept together across `main` @ b62a63c with **ZERO open leagues PRs** (`gh pr list` empty for this lane; `git ls-remote --heads origin` carries only main plus five unrelated Lists-v2/LV7 branches) — main tops at **R434 / D192 / F79** (`D700`/`F97` are the `#FFD700`/`#F97316` hexes in `spec-tier-view.md`, excluded per D180's note) — so this session takes **D193** and files **F80**; re-grep owed at merge. (1) **THE CATALOG IS PER DRAFT TYPE, AND MANUAL EDIT MODE REPLACES *FIX A PICK* RATHER THAN JOINING IT.** DR.3 left `DRAFT_OPTIONS_ENTRIES` extensible for exactly this; what the auction needs is not eight-plus-four but a different §8.7 surface, so `draftOptionsEntries(isAuction)` returns the shipped eight or the auction's ELEVEN. §8.7's v2.10 ruling says Manual Edit Mode *replaces* the drag/reassign articulation **for auction**, and offering both would put two doors on ONE pair of engine paths (`draft_reverse_won_bid` + the priced `draft_reassign_pick`/`draft_move_player`) — so the auction catalog carries `manual-edit` and NOT `fix-pick`. `order` and `force-pick` are RELABELLED there (nomination order; nominate-for-a-manager) because 087's arms make them different verbs on an auction — the order edit writes `nomination_order`, the force is a force-NOMINATION at the minimum bid. Both catalogs are stored-literal goldens, and the anchor pin now loops over BOTH, so an entry added without a panel anchor fails by construction. (2) **F72's REMAINING HALF: ONE PREDICATE, AND IT IS CHECKED AGAINST THE ENGINE, NOT AGAINST ITSELF.** `pauseFirstGate(draft)` returns `blocked` exactly when `status === 'live'` — migration 090's own predicate — and the copy is the engine's sentence minus the verb prefix and the § tag (the auction and snake/linear variants both). The pin that makes this falsifiable reads the MIGRATION CHAIN: it parses every `CREATE [OR REPLACE] FUNCTION` in `supabase/migrations/`, keeps each name's HEAD body (D137's rule, mechanised), and asserts that the set of functions calling `draft_auction_pause_gate_internal` is EXACTLY the six the UI maps to groups (`draft_set_clock`, `draft_undo`, `draft_reassign_pick`, `draft_move_player`, `draft_reverse_won_bid`, `draft_cancel_nomination`), that the head predicate is type-NEUTRAL, and that both clauses appear verbatim in it. A future migration that gates a seventh verb — or ungates one — reddens the UI suite instead of shipping a control that lies. The gated/not-gated lists also PARTITION every id in both catalogs, so a new group must be dispositioned. **Not gated, per the ruling's own exclusions:** budget, force-pick (which has the OPPOSITE gate — 069 refuses it while paused), order, autopick, seats, reset, end. (3) **MANUAL EDIT MODE'S CELLS ARE THE SECTION'S OWN, AND THAT WAS A DELIBERATE READING OF TWO RULES THAT PULL APART.** D142/§8.7 say *enter mode → click any drafted player's cell → a modal with exactly two choices*; the v2.12 amendment says every auction control lands as a `Draft Options` SECTION, *"not as a new trigger, panel, or floating affordance"*. Arming the live board's team columns would have satisfied the first by violating the second (the sheet would have to close, leaving a commissioner-armed board — the second door §8.7's v2.12 note exists to retire). So the mode renders its cells INSIDE its section: every team in nomination order with its remaining budget and its buys with prices, built from `buildAuctionColumns` — the SAME derivation the board's columns use, not a second one. The mode toggle stays real (money-moving paths are not one stray click away), and the modal keeps EXACTLY two choices: *Reset pick* → `reverse-bid`, and *Move player to a different team* → the priced `move-player` with the commissioner re-entering the cost. The cost box is capped at the RECEIVING team's max bid, the E5 idiom applied to E28 (the cap prevents the refusal; the server refuses independently with its own numbers), full rosters are offered as visibly unavailable, and a pick whose row id has not reconciled yet cannot be reset — never a guess. (4) **THE IDEMPOTENCY AUDIT, BY SIGNATURE — AND THE ONE PLACE THE PENDING-DISABLE IS LOAD-BEARING.** None of 087's four auction verbs takes an `action_id` (D188(4)), so the wire has no dedupe key. Three are self-guarding on a replay: a second `reverse-bid` meets *"pick % is not a live pick"*, a second `cancel-nomination` meets *"no player is nominated right now"*, a second `end` meets *"already complete"* — each refuses, and no money moves twice. **`draft_adjust_budget` is the exception**: `v_after := v_before + p_delta` is CUMULATIVE, so a double submit moves twice the money and nothing refuses it. Every submit in the new sections is disabled while its mutation is pending; the budget editor's is PINNED (the disabled expression itself, not merely an `isPending` somewhere in the section) and was driven live — two clicks in separate tasks produced **one** `POST …/draft/budget` and `budget_adjustments` read `-20`, not `-40`. *(R442: the guard is MOUNT-SCOPED — `SheetContent` has no `forceMount`, so closing and reopening the panel mid-flight destroys the `useAdjustBudget` observer and re-enables the submit; and the engine residual stands regardless — `draft_adjust_budget` takes no `action_id`, so a retry after a lost response double-charges. Owned by **F82**; see D195(4).)* (5) **END'S HARD CONFIRM IS 100% CLIENT-SIDE, SO IT IS PINNED LIKE A SERVER RULE.** The route deliberately takes no confirm phrase (D188(3)), which means nothing but this dialog stands between a click and a terminal, un-undoable transition. Treatment: the Reset section's type-a-word idiom with its OWN word (`END` — a half-typed `RESET` can never fire it), the C41 consequence list rendered verbatim with the unfilled-slot COUNT derived through the same budget family `draft_end` counts with (and no number at all when the mirror cannot derive one — a wrong number in a terminal confirm is worse than none), and a required reason. Pinned: one `.mutateAsync` call site in the whole section, behind the word AND the reason AND the pending guard. Measured live: fresh dialog disabled → a bare click fires ZERO requests → `end` (wrong case) disabled → `END` without a reason disabled → `END` + reason enabled. (6) **THE AUCTION'S FINAL BOARD IS THE SPEND, IN NOMINATION ORDER — THE GRID CANNOT REPRESENT IT.** `DraftBoardGrid` places a pick by the snake/linear mapping of `pick_number` → (round, seat) and then labels the cell with the ROW's team, so an auction would render each buy in an unrelated team's column (the same coercion R427 caught feeding the status strip; `draft-order.ts`: *"auction has no board order — callers never ask"*). The recap therefore branches once, exactly like the room: `recapBuysInOrder` renders every live buy as `#seq · player · team · $price` inside its own scroll container. The roster cards gain `$N spent · biggest buy X $Y` (ties to the EARLIER nomination) and a price per row, and the row LABEL drops the snake `1.03` coordinate for `#seq` on an auction. Both recap variants (mock and real) inherit it — one branch, no fork. The roster tracker's needs line gains `$N left · max bid $M · K spots to fill` off the same §4.7 mirror the columns use, passed in by the room so the component derives no money of its own. (7) **TWO SECTION-BODY CORRECTIONS TAKEN UNDER THE DR.3 PRECEDENT (D178(3)), NOT AS RESTYLES.** D153 forbids restyling the shipped bodies; both of these are the same class DR.3 took: a control that says something untrue. **`OrderSection`** read `draft.draft_order` while the PATCH it fires writes `nomination_order` on a started auction (087's arm) — the list would have gone stale the moment the two diverged, so on an auction it reads (and is titled) the nomination order. **`ForcePickSection`** called a force-NOMINATION a pick; its title, hint and button now say what 087's auction arm does. (8) **`nomination_order_mode: manual` IS GATED OUT OF THE SETTINGS PICKER, AND THE REASON IS THE ENGINE'S.** 084's manual arm validates a STORED `drafts.nomination_order`, and 087's `draft_set_order` refuses to write one before an auction starts (*"set nomination_order_mode and its order in League settings"* — where no such field exists), so `manual` today makes the draft UNSTARTABLE. Offering it would be offering a refusal (D110(1)'s rule, applied to a settings value), so the picker offers the two working modes — and still shows `manual` when a league already STORES it, labelled for what it is, so the select never renders blank and the way out is one click. The editor that would make the mode reachable is **F80**. Pinned in both directions, with the two RAISE texts read out of the migration chain. Covered by the central fix; no test can reach it without inventing a state the route cannot produce. (1) **A VOID EMITS AN EVENT — ONE PER VOID STATEMENT, NEVER PER ROW — and the two rejected options are recorded with their reasons.** The task banner's three candidates: (a) an `UPDATE OF voided_at` arm is right in KIND and wrong in GRANULARITY if per-row — D162 situation (c) stamps a whole run in one statement and R379 forbade "one event per row"; the shape taken is a **STATEMENT-level AFTER UPDATE trigger with OLD/NEW transition tables**, emitting ONE event per draft per statement naming the DISTINCT (seq, player) pairs voided. - **D185 — L.C1.6 review fix cycle (M3 batch 7, PR #171): the bid feed's fetch window (R401), the fix shape taken, and the four nits.** (1) **Fix shape: (b) BUFFER-AND-REPLAY, not (a) the drafts-event gap detector — and why.** R401 offered two shapes. (a) would compare `current_nomination` / `current_pick_number` against the feed cache on every `drafts` event and invalidate on mismatch; it is leaky in the window it is meant to close: at the moment a `drafts` event arrives mid-fetch the cache may already hold the interim (about-to-be-discarded) write, so the detector sees a match and fires nothing, and the NEXT `drafts` event compares only the CURRENT high bid — a bid lost from history, or a cancelled nomination's zombie rows at a seq the live nomination shares (D143: the seq is not consumed), never trips it; it also depends on the relative delivery order of `drafts` and `draft_bids` within one transaction. (b) addresses the mechanism itself: `use-draft-feed-sink.ts` — `createFeedSink(queryClient, key, reduce)` queues events FIFO and drains only while the query's `fetchStatus === 'idle'` (or no query exists), with a `QueryCache` subscription that drains the moment a fetch SETTLES (success / error / cancel) onto the rows the fetch produced — exactly what the held events post-date; an INSERT the snapshot already holds dedupes, a void it already reflects strikes nothing. FIFO is load-bearing (pinned): an event arriving between the settle and the async cache notification must not overtake a held one (a held VOID of (seq, P) applied AFTER a fresh INSERT of the D143 renomination of the same P would strike the live row). No cache + no fetch ⇒ dropped (the mount-time fetch carries history — the chat precedent); a reducer's `refetch` starts a fetch, so the events behind it queue. Generic over the reducer so chat can adopt it (F75). Lifetime = the channel effect (created with it, `dispose()` in its cleanup); anything held at dispose is reconciled by the next confirmed join's refetch, which every (re)open ends in. `use-draft.ts`'s `draft_bids` handler is now `bidSink.push({operation, record})` — source-pinned (the handler body contains no `getQueryData`/`setQueryData`/`reduceBidEvent(`). - **D181 — DR.6 build mechanics: the newest-wins election as a pure model, release through the EXISTING cleanups, and an inverted phantom-canvas pane artifact.** **Number note (D161's grep-together rule):** R, D and F swept together across `main` @ 97fa430, `origin/docs/SE-scoring-editor-breakdown` (the one open PR, #161) AND its local worktree (same commit 07d2113) — main tops at R392/D180/F73 (the `D700`/`F97` grep hits are the `#FFD700`/`#F97316` hexes in `spec-tier-view.md`, excluded per D180's own note), #161 at R384/D175/F71 — so this session takes **D181**; **no new F-row** (nothing is deferred: the one deliberate in-place reading this task leaves — the Practice CTA below — is a disposition recorded in a PINNED enumeration, not an unowned hand-off). Re-grep owed at merge. (1) **The Q14 ruling is an ORDERING, and the election is a pure model of it** (`single-room-tab-ops.ts`): claims are `{tab_id, claimed_at, seq}`; the election compares ONLY `(claimed_at, tab_id)` — newest instant wins, a same-millisecond mount race breaks on `tab_id` so exactly one holder settles (pinned as the both-directions XOR). `seq` is a TRANSPORT nonce pinned OUT of the election — it exists because a `storage` event only fires when the stored string CHANGES, and a defend re-announces an UNCHANGED claim (`claimed_at` untouched: a defender must never out-new a genuinely newer claim in flight). A holder defends against a losing claim (the clock-skew guard); a released tab never defends — exchanges terminate. 18 ops pins including the one-unit two-claims-one-tick-apart golden. (2) **Release is the ABSENCE of a draft id, never a second mechanism** (§4.5's no-change-to-`use-draft*.ts` rule, kept to the letter — `git diff` on `src/hooks/` touches only the two NEW entry-target files): `draft-room.tsx` computes `heldDraftId = released ? undefined : draftId` and feeds THAT to `useDraftRoom`, whose own effects bail on `!draftId` — the §9.3 channel cleanup's `removeChannel` and the heartbeat cleanup's `clearInterval` have then already run. - **D158 — M3 batch-3 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.3, PR #156; R328–R336).** (1) **A SERVER-AUTHORITATIVE VERB THAT TAKES ONLY A VALUE CANNOT KNOW WHAT THE CALLER WAS LOOKING AT — and that is a wrong-outcome bug, not an ergonomics gap (R330, the headline).** `draft_place_bid(draft, amount, action_id)` read `player_id` from `current_nomination` and `nomination_seq` from `current_pick_number`, both fresh under the lock, so a bid in flight across a nomination boundary was applied to whatever player was live when it executed: reproduced on 034's own fixture — t3 nominated p09 at $1 (nomination 2) and a $40 bid intended for p01 (nomination 1) was ACCEPTED against p09, `stale_bid_landed_on = pgtap-ab-p09 | amount = 40`. E2 does not help (a first-time submit carries a fresh action_id), and 086's award would then hand that player over at that price. **The generalizable rule: when a server verb's target is implied by mutable server state rather than named by the caller, the caller must be able to NAME the target it believed it was acting on — an optional identity argument that refuses on mismatch, never a route-layer check.** The snake analogue never had the bug because `draft_make_pick` carries `player_id`. Fixed IN THE RPC (D157(10)); the route obligation is F64. §5's interface sketch prints the amount-only signature, but the same paragraph says "Builder finalizes exact fields" — so this was LATITUDE, and a residual left silent in the banner, the D-entry and the PR body all three. - **D157 — L.C1.3 build mechanics (migration 085).** (1) **THE E2 MECHANISM IS THE OPENING BID ROW, and it is the same row for both verbs.** The task left the choice open ("`draft_bids` opening row or a config echo"); `draft_nominate` writes the opening bid to `draft_bids` exactly like a raise, so §12.5 carries one uniform history, the room's bid feed needs no special case, and both RPCs replay through ONE lookup — `SELECT … FROM draft_bids WHERE draft_id = … AND action_id = …` under the draft-row lock, the 066:917 select-then-insert pattern. It is **never** an `ON CONFLICT` upsert: `uniq_draft_bid_action` is PARTIAL and a bare arbiter raises 42P10 (D144(7)/R310, read before writing rather than discovered at runtime). Replay semantics inherit R125 verbatim — an action_id is consumed forever, no `is_undone` or phase filter — and 034 pins the consequence that matters: a replayed NOMINATION during the BIDDING phase returns its original row instead of the phase refusal, which is exactly the reconnect case E2 exists for and would fail if the replay arm sat below the validations. (2) **D126's phase rule needed two readings the spec does not print, and both are recorded and pinned.** Through the BIDDING phase `on_clock_team_id` stays the NOMINATOR (it is the seat 086's rotation advances FROM, and the room's "X nominated" attribution), and `current_pick_number` is NOT consumed by opening a nomination — it is that nomination's sequence number until the award. Both are pinned in 034, and where the file needs a second nomination it performs a PRIVILEGED "simulated close" (clear `current_nomination`, bump the sequence by hand) with a comment saying so, because a pin that leaned on 086's award arm would be pinning code that does not exist yet. (3) **Anti-snipe is implemented as `deadline := GREATEST(deadline, now() + anti_snipe)`, with the zero case as its own branch.** GREATEST states D128 as "the clock may only be EXTENDED": above the threshold the standing deadline wins (the countdown continues — Chris's own clarification), at the threshold the two are equal, below it the floor wins. The `auction_anti_snipe_seconds = 0` case is a separate branch on purpose — **and the reason was recorded WRONG at first landing; corrected in the batch-3 fix cycle (R329).** It is NOT that GREATEST would hand an expired clock "a fresh now()-based clock": at anti_snipe 0, `now() + make_interval(secs => 0)` IS now(), so the two forms agree on every LIVE deadline and `GREATEST(expired, now())` is merely now() — still due, not fresh. The branch is observable in exactly two states, both of which are the disabled extension declining to touch a clock: an ALREADY-EXPIRED deadline, which an unconditional GREATEST would REWRITE forward to now() (pinned, 034 pin 61, and it is the ONLY pin the probe reddens), and a NULL one, which GREATEST — ignoring NULLs — would INVENT (unreachable today: nominate always writes a deadline and the one NULL-deadline state is `paused`, which both verbs refuse first). **The counterpart is now recorded rather than silent:** with anti_snipe > 0 a bid landing after the clock already read zero receives a FULL FRESH WINDOW (`now() + anti_snipe`) — D128's letter, and consistent with snake's posture that the TICK is the enforcer of expiry, not the deadline column; pinned at 034 pin 62. **The exact-threshold instant is observationally a no-op** (flooring to 10s when 10s remain changes nothing), so the discriminating pins are threshold − 1s (floors) and threshold + 1s (does not), both pinned to the second against the transaction instant. (4) **The max-bid clause IS §8.6.8 at the bid layer, and it is pinned by its CONSEQUENCE, not only by its refusal.** Bids move no money (D131(2)), so no bid can break solvency; an AWARD of an over-large bid can. `max_bid = remaining − (open_slots − 1) × min_bid` is precisely the largest amount whose award leaves the winner exactly on the floor — so 034 simulates the award AT max_bid (solvent, at equality) and ONE DOLLAR ABOVE it (insolvent), and carries the cross-cutting property "no bid above its bidder's max bid exists in history", bracketed by a population count so the NOT EXISTS cannot pass over an empty table (R307). (5) **Validation ORDER is a UX decision, recorded: capacity is checked BEFORE the bid bounds.** A complete roster reads `max_bid` 0 (084's E27 branch), so bounds-first would refuse a full team with "over your max bid of $0" instead of "your roster is complete" — the message would be true and useless. (6) **MOCK AUCTIONS ARE REFUSED BY BOTH VERBS — a deliberate seam, not an omission (F61).** No auction mock can exist today (071's `create_mock_draft` refuses auction configs and a mock's `draft_type` is snapshotted at creation), so the refusal is unreachable; the alternative was silence, and silence becomes a hole the moment L.C1.7 lifts the 071 refusal — every league member could bid inside another member's solo practice until the D103(2) launcher gate is retrofitted. Bidder-team resolution for mock seats is genuinely L.C1.7's design (CPU seats bid through the tick, D132), so the seam refuses now and lifts there, with the two 034 pins flipping in that PR. Its sibling obligation is **F62**: 086's system nomination must keep the invariant 085 establishes — every nomination opens with a `draft_bids` row (`action_id` NULL for the system path, which is why C39 made the column NULLable). (7) **PROBE-ORDERING DISCIPLINE — learned by running the DoD probe twice.** The first shape of 034 put the E5 over-max refusal in the MIDDLE of a bid ladder; under the probe the refused bid landed, the next pin's bid became a self-raise, and that raised an ERROR outside `throws_ok` which **aborted the file at 42 of the then-84 asserts with a single RED** — the probe destroyed the evidence it was supposed to produce. Reordering so that each ladder's over-max refusal is its LAST act and comes from a seat that is NOT the standing high bidder gives the honest signature: **6 of 91 RED and the file runs to the end** (the count re-captured against the batch-3 plan; §F's new R330 identity block obeys the same discipline — its ACCEPTED arm first, both refusals from seats that are not the standing high bidder — which is why its own probe leaves 5 RED instead of aborting), including the property pin and the two population counts that show the refused bids landed. *Rule to carry forward: a break probe that aborts the suite proves less than one that leaves its wreckage on the floor to be counted — order the pins so the mutation's damage stays observable.* (8) **Recorded residual (no bespoke message):** a RETIRED seat's manager reaching a bid path would get 084's loud P0002 from `draft_team_budget` (R321) rather than a bespoke refusal. Deliberate — retirement is M4's, a retired seat is outside both the rotation and the invariant's team set, and a loud honest raise beats inventing UX copy for a state this milestone cannot produce. (9) **Break-probe results AS RUN (the R306 lesson), all three re-captured against the batch-3 plan of 91:** (a) the DoD probe — dropping `IF p_amount > v_max_bid` — turned **6 of 034's 91** pins RED: 48 (LA's $187 vs a $186 max), 81 (E25's $2 vs a $1-max seat), 87 (the same at min_bid 0), 66 and 88 (the two population counts: the refused bids landed), and **89**, the property pin — plus **2 of 3** cases in the wire suite. The NOMINATION-side max-bid pins (29, 79) stayed GREEN by construction — they are `draft_nominate`'s own §8.6.7(a) clause, a different arm in a different function — as did §G's solvency-consequence pair, which are privileged award simulations that never route through the probed function. (b) the R330 probe — removing the nomination-identity guard — turned **5 of 91** RED (44, 45 the two refusal arms; 46 the per-nomination row count; 66 and 88 the population counts), with pin 43 (the matching-identity ACCEPTANCE) GREEN by construction. (c) the R329 probe — replacing the zero branch with an unconditional GREATEST — turned **exactly 1 of 91** RED (pin 61), with pin 60 GREEN, which is the finding it was written for. All reverted; 91/91 and 3/3 re-verified. (10) **NOMINATION IDENTITY ON THE BID PATH (R330 — landed in the batch-3 fix cycle, before 085 ever merged).** `draft_place_bid` gained two OPTIONAL trailing arguments, `p_nomination_seq` and `p_player_id`, refusing on mismatch with §16.3's "just went off the board" copy; omitted ⇒ shipped behavior, so no caller broke. **Why the RPC and not the route:** the RPC is the server-authoritative boundary (spec §4/§8.1 — clients never compute, and every caller must be safe, not only HTTP ones); a route guard would leave the sim, the pgTAP suite and every future caller exposed, and L.C1.4's completion path awards on exactly this data. **Why BOTH arguments:** neither subsumes the other — `player_id` catches the ordinary moved-on case, and `nomination_seq` catches the two cases where the same player is live under a different nomination (D143's cancel-and-renominate does NOT consume the sequence number; an undone award returns a player to the pool at a later sequence). The route obligation is **F64**. (11) **RECORDED RESIDUAL — the E2 replay lookup is VERB-BLIND (R331, ledger row F65).** Both verbs replay on `(draft_id, action_id)` with no verb discrimination, so an action_id used by one verb returns a false success through the other (proven live). The contract is therefore per-verb and enforced at the MINT SITE (L.C2.1), and the three in-body shapes were each rejected with a stated reason: **narrowing** the lookup is forbidden because the UNQUALIFIED lookup under the draft lock is exactly what makes a duplicate action_id un-insertable (it is the recorded reason no `EXCEPTION WHEN unique_violation` wrapper is owed, and narrowing re-opens a raw 23505 on the PARTIAL `uniq_draft_bid_action`); **argument-consistency** discrimination contradicts R125 and the two shipped 034 E2 pins, which deliberately replay with DIFFERENT arguments and assert the original row comes back; and **position-based verb inference** ("an opening row is the earliest row of its nomination_seq") breaks under D143's cancel-and-renominate, which writes a second opening under an existing seq and would make the rule FALSE-REFUSE a legitimate reconnect retry in L.C1.5's world — a worse bug than the one it closes. A verb column on `draft_bids` would settle it exactly and is recorded as the option rather than taken (085 ships no DDL, and the table is L.C1.1's).

A privileged probe on `main` @ 9c81f7c — an 8-team $200/min-1 auction started through `draft_start_internal`, deadline rewound to now() − 60s, one `draft_tick()` — wrote `draft_picks(pick_number=1, round=1, price=NULL, is_auto=t, made_via='autopick')`, advanced `current_pick_number` and moved `on_clock_team_id` by `draft_team_for_pick`, with **zero `draft_bids` rows** and `current_nomination` still NULL: a free player, no nomination, no bidding. ARM 2's claim and its under-lock re-verify now both exclude auctions; 035 §C pins it behaviourally. This session therefore takes **D162** and **no F number at all** (it grows two existing rows instead of filing a new one). (1) **THE VOID QUESTION IS ANSWERED WITH A COLUMN, AND THE TWO REJECTED OPTIONS ARE RECORDED WITH THEIR REASONS.** tasks-M3 §6 printed three options. "Merged history is acceptable; every reader filters by `player_id`" is **not sound, and the counter-example is reachable through the shipped verbs**: D143 restarts the SAME nominator's clock, nothing stops them renominating the SAME player at the SAME amount, and then `nomination_seq`, `player_id`, `team_id` and `amount` all tie across the void boundary — leaving 086's `ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC` as the only separator, which is exactly the shape D161(2) forbade one task earlier. "A second nomination identity that a cancel advances" works but costs a new `drafts` counter, a stamp in BOTH nomination writers, a reset rule at every award, and a new invariant that can drift — and an attempt number still cannot tell the room's feed WHICH rows to strike through. So: **`draft_bids.voided_at TIMESTAMPTZ NULL`**, stamped by ONE helper. (2) **IT IS NOT A BREACH OF THE APPEND-ONLY RULING, AND THE DISTINCTION IS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.** 083:136's sentence is about POLICIES; 087 adds none, and 036 §B re-runs 032's literal per-role write matrix (member + commissioner × UPDATE/DELETE via RETURNING-count, INSERT 42501, each bracketed by a privileged count before and after) **after** the column lands — so "clients still cannot write `draft_bids`" is a measurement in the post-change world, not an inference from intent. D131(2)'s substance is that rows STAND; a stamp keeps every row standing and rewrites none of its bid facts. (3) **`voided_at`'s MEANING IS MECHANICAL, and the asymmetry is deliberate.** It marks a row as no longer belonging to the live-or-future nomination at its `nomination_seq`, which happens in exactly the two cases that make a sequence number ambiguous: the sequence is CLEARED WITHOUT AN AWARD (cancel, `draft_end`), or it is REWOUND ONTO (`draft_undo`). **A reversed pick is deliberately NOT in that list** — `draft_reverse_won_bid` consumes no sequence number and rewinds nothing, so the reversal stays recorded on `draft_picks.is_undone` where reversals have always lived. Two facts, two columns. 036 pins the exclusion explicitly so a later session does not "fix" it. (4) **D160(8) IS NOW FALSE, AND IT WAS MADE FALSE BY DRIVING IT, NOT BY SHIPPING THE VERB AND ASSUMING.** The forge D160(8) used was rebuilt at both layers and put through the whole loop; the load-bearing observation is not that cancel succeeds but that **0 picks were destroyed and the league stayed `drafting`** — `draft_reset`, the only prior exit, would have cleared both. The wire suite runs it across separate COMMITTED transactions, which is the one thing a single-transaction pgTAP file cannot show. (5) **`draft_adjust_budget` WRITES FIRST AND RE-DERIVES, rather than re-implementing the arithmetic.** The ONE family reads `budget_adjustments`, so the only way to validate the POST-edit world without a second copy of the math is to make the edit and ask; every E28 refusal RAISEs, which rolls the write back inside the caller's transaction (the 084 start-backstop pattern). E28's arm 1 is strictly a special case of arm 2 and is kept separate ON PURPOSE: it is the arm with a different remedy, and a commissioner told "you are under the solvency floor" when the real problem is that they cut a team below what it has already SPENT will fix the wrong thing. (6) **THREE SIGNATURES WIDEN BY DROP+CREATE, and that is not a departure from D137's vehicle but a consequence of it.** A defaulted trailing parameter added by `CREATE OR REPLACE` creates an OVERLOAD, and every existing 4-argument call then fails "function is not unique". Because PostgREST resolves by NAMED argument, dropping the old arity and creating the wider one leaves every shipped route and `draft-service.ts` call site working untouched — verified by `npm run test` (100 files / 1666) rather than reasoned. The REVOKEs are re-issued explicitly (a DROP takes the ACL) and 036 §A pins both halves: the new arity EXISTS and the old arity is **`to_regprocedure(...) IS NULL`**, because the absence is the load-bearing part. (7) **`draft_force_pick`'s auction arm MINTS an `action_id` when the caller omits one.** Attribution is read off the bid row at the award (D160(3)), so a NULL there would make an unraised commissioner nomination close as an `autopick`. A commissioner nomination is a human act; the honest row carries an id. Cost: no E2 replay when the caller omits one — which is exactly what 069's snake arm already does with a NULL `action_id`. (8) **A PIN THAT CANNOT DETECT ITS OWN ADVERTISED MUTATION IS NOT A PIN (the R329 species, self-caught).** Break probe 5 — delete the priced-move max-bid refusal — turned **0 of 150** on its first run. The pin was `throws_ok(sql, 'P0001', null, …)`, and a NULL expected message accepts ANY error of that SQLSTATE: the §4-rule-7 solvency backstop three statements later was still refusing the move, with different words. The backstop is not redundant (it is what makes the failure safe), but a pin aimed at the targeted refusal must be able to tell them apart. **Every refusal in 036 whose identity matters now names its exact message; zero NULL-message P0001 pins remain**, and probe 5 turns 1 of 150. - **D165 — M3 batch-6 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.5, PR #159; R375–R383).** **Number note (R, D and F checked TOGETHER across every open branch per D161, the fifth time this rule has been applied):** `main` @ 4930bd8 is at R366 / D161 / F67; this branch already holds R374 / D164 / F69; the only other open PR is #152 (docs), which claims R≤311 / D≤144 / F≤59 — above nothing. Two fixes, not one: the reset ends its run's history (the representation), and the lookup scopes by `drafts.started_at` (the discriminator). Recording the situation in the enumeration was NOT optional — that list is what the next verb author reads. **(4) EXCLUSIVITY CHECKS THAT QUERY ONLY `draft_picks` ARE INCOMPLETE ON AN AUCTION, BECAUSE THE AUCTION HAS A SECOND PLACE A PLAYER CAN BE.** R380: between nomination and award a player is spoken for and holds no pick row. `draft_reassign_pick` is the only verb that can put a player somewhere without first finding him somewhere, so it is the only one that needs the guard — stated in the body so a future reader does not "fix" the asymmetry. **(5) `pg_proc.prosrc` INCLUDES COMMENTS, AND A NO-DRIFT PIN THAT GREPS IT IS A PIN A COMMENT CAN SATISFY.** R381, and it was not argued — the pre-R381 predicate was evaluated under the exact mutation it is supposed to catch and returned TRUE. Two hardenings: match the CALL FORM (`PERFORM public.X(` / `:= public.X(`), and assert CARDINALITY, because `bool_and` over a shrunken set is also TRUE. This is the R329 species (a pin that cannot detect its own advertised mutation) reaching the tripwires themselves, and probe 1's red set growing 3 → 4 is the receipt. **(6) FOUR OF NINE FINDINGS THIS ROUND WERE A SENTENCE ASSERTING MORE THAN THE CODE OR THE PIN MEASURES** (R375's "025 pins a body that no longer exists", R381's "all three verbs reference the helper", R382's inverted causality, R383's "measured rather than inferred") — on top of three last round (R369a, R369b, R371) and R365 the round before. **Every one was fixed by making the MEASUREMENT match the sentence rather than the sentence match the measurement**, which is the direction this build has now chosen eight times: §M's composite was widened, not narrowed; §A's pins were hardened, not softened; the mock sweep was kept and its reason corrected. **(7) BREAK-PROBE RESULTS AS RUN**, each applied to the LOCAL database only as a `CREATE OR REPLACE` from a patched copy of 087 and reverted by re-applying that function's unmutated text — never `db push`, never hosted; 199/199 green before and after every one, verified by re-running the file after each revert. **The six earlier probes, RE-RUN against the enlarged file (D161(5)):** (1) arm 3 removed from `draft_adjust_budget` → **4 of 199** (13, 85, 86, 88 — was 3 of 181; (8) `draft_reset`'s bid sweep dropped → **1 of 199** (164); (9) the undo's run scoping dropped → **1 of 199** (167); (10) the under-nomination guard dropped → **3 of 199** (145–147); (11) `draft_reset`'s mock guard no-op'd → **2 of 199** (194, 195) **with the pre-R383 composite re-run under the same mutation turning 1** — the receipt for R383. **Wire counts: 0 of 3 throughout**, green by construction and CHECKED at the call sites rather than assumed (`auction-commish-db.test.ts` drives tick/start/pause/resume/undo/set_clock/cancel_nomination/end/solvent at `AUCTION_MIN_BID = 1`, and calls no reassign, no move, no adjust_budget, no reset and no mock). - **D163 — ROSTER CONSTRUCTION IS NOT ENFORCED FROM THE DRAFT (Chris, ruled in session 2026-08-18; recorded in the L.C1.5 batch-5 fix cycle, R374).** Recorded because **nothing in `docs/specs/` carried it**: §3 Open said "None currently", there was no §4 entry, and `grep` for "roster construction" / "positional legality" across `docs/` returned nothing. **The ruling, in Chris's framing:** *"A user may draft 16 WRs — that is their problem to solve in free agency. The draft never consults positional legality: capacity is a pure count, and positional slots are a weekly lineup concern. It can be a legitimate strategy to draft only RB/WR and pick up a QB, K, DST and TE once the season starts. **But whenever AUTODRAFT is doing the picking or nominating**, it should first attempt to fill the remaining **holes** with the final picks rather than add positional depth — 'this roster's only open slot is a Kicker, so draft a kicker with the final pick.' A user can do whatever they want; autodraft should not leave them without a QB/K/DST."* **(1) THIS CONFIRMS SHIPPED BEHAVIOR — it is recorded with the evidence rather than as a new requirement, and every clause was verified before it was written down.** **Capacity is a pure count**: 084's `draft_team_budget` derives `open_slots = total_rounds − non-undone picks` (084:67) with no positional term anywhere in the family, and the v2.8.11 manual-pick rule ("slot validation at pick time = capacity only") is what the priced Manual Edit paths and `draft_nominate` both enforce (D129(1): "humans may buy a 3rd QB"). **The autodraft half is the forced arm**: the auction inherits the snake resolver unchanged at `086:648` — `v_forced := v_remaining <= v_unfilled` — so while a roster has more picks left than holes the chain adds the best available player, and once picks-remaining equals holes it fills the holes. **(2) D129(2)'s OBLIGATION IS THEREFORE DISCHARGED, AND IT WAS DISCHARGED IN L.C1.4 — NOT LEFT OPEN.** D129(2) closed with "(no rounds in auction; deferral holds until open slots force them — Builder finalizes the documented rule, pins the boundary)". The rule was finalized in the **C32 erratum (spec v2.12.1)** — §8.4's K/D-ST deferral maps to its FORCED-only arm because an auction has no rounds for the "final 3 rounds" escape to refer to — and **the boundary is pinned one unit either side in 035 §G**: "ONE UNIT SHORT of FORCED (remaining 2 vs unfilled 1): the auction seat still declines the kicker and takes an RB" (035:955) and "FORCED (remaining 1 = unfilled 1, a K seat among them): the deferral lifts and the kicker is resolved" (035:964), against a SNAKE control in the identical state (035:945). The parenthetical in D129(2) is marked discharged in place. **(3) THE C33 ERRATUM'S *FIX* STANDS BUT ITS *REASONING* DOES NOT, and the spec is corrected (v2.12.3).** C33 argued that §8.6.7(e) "can select a player the NOMINATOR cannot roster" and that (b) would then award an **illegal** pick. Under this ruling that is not a legality problem at all: capacity is a count, and §8.6.7(c)'s rotation-skip already guarantees the nominator has an open slot, so ANY player is rosterable by them. The system nomination still runs the nominator's own §8.4 chain — **no behavior changes** — but the reason is now **"so an absent manager gets a player their own board would have picked"**, which is a quality-of-outcome argument, not **"so the award is legal"**. A wrong reason attached to a right fix is how the next session justifies the wrong change. **(4) WHAT IS NOT RULED, and is deliberately left alone:** whether the autodraft hole-filling should look further ahead than the forced arm does (e.g. a soft preference for holes before the boundary), and anything about weekly lineup legality, which is M4's. No spec section moves for either.
- **D164 — M3 batch-5 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.5, PR #159; R367–R374).** **Number note (R, D and F checked TOGETHER per D161, across every open branch):** `main` @ 4930bd8 is at **R366 / D161 / F67**; the only other open PR is #152 (docs), which claims R≤311 / D≤144 / F≤59 — above nothing. This branch already holds **D162**, so the ruling takes **D163** and these mechanics **D164**, and the two new ledger rows take **F68** and **F69**. **(1) A PRE-WRITE CHECK AND A POST-WRITE CHECK ARE NOT THE SAME CHECK, AND CALLING BOTH "the E28 algebra" IS WHAT HID THE BUG.** R367: the priced Manual Edit paths asked `price <= max_bid` **before** the write. That question is about the world in which the pick has NOT landed. The stuck clock is created **by** the pick landing — the receiving team's `open_slots` and `remaining` both fall, its `max_bid` falls with them, and if it is the live high bidder its own standing bid becomes unaffordable. `draft_auction_solvent` cannot see it either, because a bid holds no money (D131(2)) so no derivation reads it: the team passes `remaining >= open_slots × min_bid` and the award is still refused forever. **Rule this cycle adopts: when a guard's subject is changed by the write it guards, the guard must be re-asked after the write.** The two questions now have two implementations at three call sites and ONE helper behind them. **(2) A SECTION THAT CANNOT FAIL FOR THE CASE IT CLAIMS TO COVER IS THE DEFECT, NOT THE MISSING PIN.** 036 §I is titled "the priced Manual Edit Mode paths" and its fixture (LG) is paused **with no live nomination**, so no priced-path pin could ever run against a high bidder. This is the same shape as R362 (an arm nothing swept) and R329 (a pin that could not detect its own mutation). **Rule: when a section's title names a surface, its fixture must be able to reach every state that surface has** — and "is there a state this fixture cannot be in?" is now a question to ask of a fixture before writing pins against it. §I(b) adds the world (LH) rather than editing LG, so §I's own boundary story stays readable. **(3) TWO MORE COVERAGE SENTENCES OUTRAN THEIR PINS — SEVEN TASKS RUNNING.** R369: the banner said §B swept member/commissioner/outsider/anon × INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE (it swept member × 4 and commissioner × 2) and that "§H sweeps all eleven" mocks (§H is the reverse-won-bid section; §M swept four). R371: the banner said §G's decoy was "built through the REAL verbs … renominate the same player at the same amount" when §G's own comments say the renomination is the TICK's and the collision is forged privileged. **In all three the substance held** — the reviewer probed outsider/anon directly, and rebuilt the D162 collision through real verbs only (three rows at seq 1, two tying; pre-D162 lookup returns 2, shipped lookup returns 1). **Disposition: EXTEND THE PINS where the claim is the coverage you would want (R369, both halves), CORRECT THE PROSE where the claim was about provenance (R371).** A banner sentence being accidentally true is not a defence. **(4) A HAND-OFF IN A SESSION-LOG CELL IS NOT A HAND-OFF (R51, again — R372).** `voided_at`'s broadcast/payload treatment was deferred to L.C1.6 in a migration comment and a free-text session-log cell, with no ledger row and no amendment to `tasks-M3-auction.md`'s L.C1.6 banner (a file this PR never touched, written before D162 existed). It is now **F69** plus a read-list line. **(5) A DIVERGENCE YOU CHOOSE TO KEEP MUST BE PINNED AND SAID (R373).** `draft_set_order` refuses a pre-start order edit on an auction and accepts one on snake. **Disposition: PIN, do not align** — aligning would be a behavior change to a shipped verb inside a fix cycle, the auction's message points at a real editor (League settings / `nomination_order_mode`, §7.3.8) so it is a UX asymmetry rather than a hole, and which way it should align is the same standing product question F57 already carries. Pinned at 036 §K (auction half) against 023:1248 (snake half). **(6) "RED ON MAIN TOO" IS ANCHORED TO A COMMIT, AND THE MERGE TARGET IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS (R370).** F56's extension recorded the E2E failure against `main` @ 5a1bf1c; on the merge target 4930bd8 the failure set is **larger and different in kind** — `draft-live.spec.ts:162`'s `getByText('Draft lobby')` reproduces **in isolation on a clean stack** and is **DR.1 test debt**, not F56: DR.1 moved the room out of the app shell, so `PageHeader` writes a store `AppHeader` reads and `AppHeader` is shell chrome (the comment at `draft-lobby.tsx:188` on `main` says so outright). Filed as **F68**, owned by the DR lane, deliberately not fixed here. **(7) RECORDED COUNTS RE-RUN, AGAIN (D161(5) applied without being asked).** 036 grew 150 → 181, so all five original probes were re-run against the enlarged file; every original RED SET reproduced exactly (3 / 2 / 10 / 2 / 1), which is the evidence that the first record was honest. Probe 6 is R367's own: **10 of 181** — and its tenth RED is **§A's new no-drift source pin**, added in this cycle because "one helper so the three cannot drift apart" was otherwise unpinned prose, which is the same species of claim R369/R371 were filed for. The D141 gate helper had such a pin from the start; E28 arm 3 did not, and R367 is what the absence buys.
- **D161 — M3 batch-4 fix-cycle mechanics (L.C1.4, PR #158; R362–R366).** **Number note (R312 first-filed-keeps, the FOURTH time this rule has been needed — and the fourth instance was created by this very entry):** this cycle renumbered R339–R343 → **R362–R366** against the open branches, wrote the rule down, **and then filed its own ledger row as `F66` without applying it** — `F66` was already taken by the held DR.1 PR #157 (the unmatched `/app/*` root-404 row). Corrected to **F67** by the orchestrator at review time. The lesson is narrower and more useful than "check the open branches": **check every counter, not the one that just bit you.** R and D were checked here; F was not, because the collision that prompted the check had been an R collision. Until #157 lands, `git show <open-branch>:docs/specs/PROGRESS-leagues.md` must be grepped for **R, D and F together** before any of the three is assigned.  D157–D158 are #156's, D159 belongs to the OPEN Chris-held DR.1 PR #157, D160 is this PR's original entry — so the fix cycle takes **D161**. The reviewer's own R-numbers collided the same way (R339–R343 against #157's R339–R361) and renumbered to R362–R366. **(1) A SECOND DOOR TO THE SAME WRITER IS STILL THE SAME DEFECT, AND "NO ARM CLAIMS IT" IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT A READING.** 086 closed ARM 2's auction door with a probe it ran, then asserted in three places that a live auction mock is claimed by no arm — without running that one. ARM 2.5 claimed it and snake-autopicked it (R362). The general rule this cycle adopts: **a sentence of the form "X is claimed/handled by no Y" must name the observation that establishes it, and the observation must sweep every Y, not the two the task was thinking about.** The pin that makes it stick is not the zero — it is the pin BEFORE the zero asserting the fixture was genuinely claimable, and the pin BESIDE it asserting nothing merely failed (`mock_cpu_failures = '[]'`); a zero with neither is the CLAUDE.md "nothing happened means it worked" trap wearing a test's clothes. **(2) A COMMENT THAT JUSTIFIES A `LIMIT 1` IS A CLAIM, AND D143 ALREADY REFUTED THIS ONE.** "Unique by construction" was written about a triple that a ruled-but-unbuilt verb makes non-unique (`draft_cancel_nomination` does not consume the sequence number). The lookup was correct only by an ordering, and the tiebreak behind that ordering is `gen_random_uuid()`. **Rule: when the discriminator is a column you already have, put it in the WHERE — do not let an ORDER BY carry a correctness argument.** `player_id` is now in the WHERE and 035 §K pins the disambiguation with a decoy the ordering deterministically prefers. **(3) D143'S "OPEN BIDS ARE VOIDED" HAS NO SCHEMA REPRESENTATION, and 086 is its first consumer.** `draft_bids` is append-only with no UPDATE/DELETE policy for anyone (083, D131(2)), so a voided nomination's rows stay and merge under one sequence number for every reader keyed on `nomination_seq` alone. 086's award survives it; the room's bid feed, L.C1.6's broadcast and the recap have not met it yet. Routed into **L.C1.5's read-list in tasks-M3 §6** with the three options and the instruction to record the decision or raise a spec question — not left as a comment for someone to find. **(4) A REFUSED AWARD HAS NO REMEDY UNTIL L.C1.5, and pause is not one.** Driven, not reasoned: pause → resume leaves the nomination standing and the next tick reproduces the identical refusal (D160(8), corrected). **Rule: "Z can be recovered by W" is the same species of claim as (1) — drive W before recording it.** **(5) RECORDED COUNTS MUST BE RE-RUN WHEN THE FILE THEY COUNT CHANGES.** Adding 11 pins made "35 of 105" unreproducible, so all three original probes were re-run (D160(10)); the 1–105 sets reproduced exactly, which is the evidence that the original record was honest. **(6) A PIN THAT READS A WHOLE-TICK ARRAY REPORTS A NEIGHBOUR'S FAILURE AS ITS OWN.** §K's first draft asserted `auction_failures = '[]'` and went red under probes that break other worlds; scoped by `draft_id`, it is deterministic. The existing pins 79/87 read `auction_failures->0` and have the same shape — left alone (no drive-by) and filed as **F67**, with the mechanism named: `now()` is transaction-stable inside a pgTAP file, so every forced `now() - interval '1 second'` deadline ties and ARM 2.6's `ORDER BY current_deadline` breaks the tie arbitrarily.


**2026-08-14/15/16 — Architect (the M3 breakdown, PR #150 — merged 2026-08-16; transcribed verbatim from tasks-M3-auction.md §3 per the tasks-M2 D86–D101 precedent; D139–D143 fold Chris's 2026-08-15/16 auction-UI rulings, spec v2.10/v2.10.1):**
- **D126 — Auction state lives on the drafts row; phase is `current_nomination`'s NULLity.** No new state columns: `current_nomination` NULL ⇒ **nominating** (`on_clock_team_id` = the nominator per `nomination_order` rotation, `current_deadline` = nomination clock); non-NULL ⇒ **bidding** (`current_nomination = { player_id, high_bid, high_bidder_team_id }` per 065:121's printed shape, `current_deadline` = bid clock). `current_pick_number` doubles as the 1-based **nomination sequence** (§12.4's "sequence # (auction)"); `draft_picks.round` is NULL for auction rows; `current_round` tracks the rotation lap (display only). `total_rounds` keeps its D91 meaning (draftable slots = starters + bench) — it is the auction's per-team roster capacity, not a rounds count.
- **D127 — Budgets are always DERIVED, never stored counters.** `remaining_budget(team) = auction_budget + adjustment(team) − Σ price(non-undone picks)`; `open_slots(team) = total_rounds − count(non-undone picks)`; `max_bid(team) = remaining − (open_slots − 1) × min_bid` (§8.6.1). One SQL derivation fn family (§5), used by every validator — a stored counter could drift from truth; a derivation cannot. Commissioner budget edits need storage: **additive column `drafts.budget_adjustments JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`** (team_id → integer delta; spec-absent schema recorded here + erratum, the D102 precedent) — validated per E28 at edit time, room-visible (D134), history via the D97 system chat post until M6's audit rows. *Recorded nuance:* the settings-layer floor (league-settings.ts:541) uses roster_size incl. IR — deliberately conservative vs the engine's D91 open-slots; both stand.
- **D128 — Bid-clock semantics: a fixed window with an anti-snipe floor (the E6-consistent reading).** The bid clock starts at `auction_bid_seconds` when bidding opens (at nomination) and is **not** reset by bids; a bid landing with remaining < `auction_anti_snipe_seconds` resets remaining **to** `auction_anti_snipe_seconds` (§7.3.8's own words: "resets clock **to it**"; Appendix C L.C1: "reset bid clock to auction_anti_snipe_seconds"; E6: 3s left, threshold 10 → clock reads 10s). `auction_anti_snipe_seconds = 0` disables extension (pure fixed window). §8.6.3's looser "each bid resets the bid clock per anti-snipe" is read as "each bid applies the anti-snipe rule". **C34 flags this for Chris's read before build** — pacing is product feel; the alternative (Sleeper-style reset-to-full-per-bid) contradicts E6 as printed and would need a spec change. **RULED 2026-08-15 (Chris, in-session): CONFIRMED** — his own scenario language: 30s total clock; bids above the threshold neither reset nor pause it — the countdown continues uninterrupted (Chris's explicit clarification); a higher bid landing inside the final 10 seconds resets the clock to 10 seconds (his "bid with 3 seconds left → clock resets to 10"), repeatable. D128 as written is the LAW reading; no spec change.
- **D129 — Nomination discipline.** (1) Human nomination validates: nominator's turn, player undrafted, opening bid ≥ `auction_min_bid` AND ≤ nominator's max bid (§8.6.7(a)), **capacity-only fit** (open_slots ≥ 1 — the v2.8.11 manual-pick rule extended: need-fit is a system-path rule, humans may buy a 3rd QB). Rotation-skip (§8.6.7(c)) guarantees the nominator has an open slot, so the §8.6.7(b) nominator-award is always legal. (2) **System nomination (timeout) = the M2 autopick resolution chain run for the on-clock team** (queue → primary board → Big Board → ADP with need-fit; 068's `draft_autopick_resolve`) at an opening bid of `min_bid` ($0 legal when `min_bid = 0` — C38; R305) — this satisfies §8.6.7(e)'s "fits *some* team's open slot" (it fits the nominator's) and makes (b) safe; one implementation, snake and auction (C33 records the reading). K/D-ST deferral maps to the forced-only arm (no rounds in auction; deferral holds until open slots force them — ~~Builder finalizes the documented rule, pins the boundary~~ **DISCHARGED in L.C1.4, migration 086 — marked 2026-08-18 (R374/D163(2)), not left open:** the rule is finalized in the **C32 erratum, spec v2.12.1** (§8.4's deferral maps to its FORCED-only arm because an auction has no rounds), and the boundary is pinned ONE UNIT EITHER SIDE in **035 §G** — 035:955 "ONE UNIT SHORT of FORCED (remaining 2 vs unfilled 1) … declines the kicker" and 035:964 "FORCED (remaining 1 = unfilled 1) … the deferral lifts" — against a snake control in the identical state at 035:945. The forced arm itself is `086:648`, `v_forced := v_remaining <= v_unfilled`). (3) The **D102 grace contract carries to the nomination clock**: autodraft/no-user/FRESH seats system-nominate AT deadline; a STALE seat's nomination is held to deadline + grace, manual nomination allowed during the hold. (4) **No auto-bidding for absent seats** (§8.6.5/OQ 10) — grace applies to nominations only; you cannot be timed *into* a bid.
- **D130 — Award path.** Bid-clock expiry under the draft-row lock: winner = `current_nomination.high_bidder_team_id` (or the nominator at the opening bid when no raises — §8.6.7(b)/E26); write `draft_picks` (pick_number = nomination seq, round NULL, `price`, `made_via`/`is_auto` per actor: system-nominated no-raise awards are `is_auto = TRUE, made_via = 'autopick'`); clear `current_nomination`; advance rotation to the next team with open_slots ≥ 1 (E27 skip); next nomination deadline. **Completion = no team has open slots** → the 072 completion txn extended to write `acquisition_cost = price` (D111(3)); "budgets exhausted" (§8.6.6) is unreachable — solvency guarantees every open slot is affordable at min_bid, pinned as a property.
- **D131 — Auction reversals.** (1) **`draft_reverse_won_bid`** (§8.7's "undo a won bid"): targeted soft-undo of a specific auction pick (`is_undone = TRUE`) — player to pool, budget restored by derivation (free), the team re-enters the rotation if it was complete; live/paused drafts only (post-completion reversal is F44's M6 class). (2) **Undo/cascade (E29):** when a nomination has live bids, `draft_undo` FIRST voids the nomination (clear `current_nomination`; `draft_bids` rows stand as append-only history — "bids returned" costs nothing because **bids never hold budget, only won picks do**), then reverts picks; on_clock rewinds to the target nomination's nominator with a fresh nomination clock. (3) Undo is provably solvency-preserving (remaining' = remaining + price ≥ (open+1) × min_bid whenever price ≥ min_bid — pinned as a property). (4) **E28 extends to the live nomination:** a budget edit that would make the CURRENT high bid insolvent for its bidder is refused (friendly: void the nomination or reverse won bids first) — otherwise the close could award an unaffordable player.
- **D132 — CPU bidders: tick-driven, value-based, same validators (one implementation, two consumers).** Mock auction CPUs nominate via D129(2) (their own resolve chain) at humanized think-time (the D93 PRNG pattern) and **bid** via a seeded value model: dollar value = f(ADP rank, budget scale, roster needs) × (1 + seeded noise), deterministic per (draft_id, nomination_seq, team_id, pass) — a CPU raises only while `high_bid + 1 ≤ min(its value, its max_bid)`, at most one raise per tick pass per nomination (bids land ~5s apart — humanized pacing for free), with the near-buzzer tail falling out of the think-fraction distribution (anti-snipe becomes visible, §8.8). E62 by construction: CPUs pass the same server-side max-bid/solvency validator as humans. The sim's auction personas (L.C4.1) drive the same decision spine through real RPCs (D100).
- **D133 — Client Broadcast STAYS CLOSED (the D109(5) decision, made).** M3 adds no `extension = 'broadcast'` INSERT policy: the "bid-button pulse" IS the authoritative `draft_bids` INSERT broadcast (sub-second, already fan-out-cheap), and v1 auction needs no typing indicators. A member who could client-broadcast could forge a server-shaped bid event to the room — the same spoof D109(5) refused. Those earlier files are deliberately NOT edited — they run before 077. Nothing numbered after it may touch the column. (3) **D115(4) is REVERSED, and this is the whole risk of the PR.** "The other five readers are left alone" was right while the column existed and was permanently NULL. Once it is gone the same five — `notify_list_followers`, `create_league`, `seat_league_member_internal`, `get_join_preview`, `draft_actor_name` — break at RUNTIME on the next call, because Postgres records no dependency from a function BODY to a column: the drop does not block, nothing fails at apply time, and the first symptom is a live error. `notify_list_followers` is the dangerous one — it runs on every list update and Lists is one of three launch surfaces. All five are re-pointed FIRST, in the same transaction as the drop, so no instant exists in which a live function references a missing column. (4) **The bodies are production's, not the repo's.** Each was dumped with `pg_get_functiondef` from the live database and edited by removing exactly the `display_name` term from its `COALESCE`; signature, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER/INVOKER, `search_path` pin, grants and surrounding logic are untouched. (Repo and production agreed for all five this time — verified — but authoring against the repo is precisely what caused the reconciliation, so the rule stands regardless of the result.) `CREATE OR REPLACE` updates the `pg_proc` row in place, so ACLs and any dependent trigger survive: 038's `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM PUBLIC, anon` on `notify_list_followers` is preserved by being left alone, not re-issued. For the record `notify_list_followers` is NOT trigger-bound — it is a two-arg `RETURNS void` RPC called from `src/lib/lists/helpers.ts`, and production has zero triggers whose body mentions the column. (5) **No observable behaviour change.** Every row's `display_name` was already NULL, so every chain already fell through to the handle. `get_join_preview` and `draft_actor_name` still render the BARE handle; `notify_list_followers` still renders `@handle` — D115(4)'s corollary stands. (6) **The drop is guarded.** A `DO` block counts non-NULL values first and raises rather than destroying one; the whole migration is one implicit transaction, so the function replacements roll back with it. `DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS` + an existence-gated, dynamically-executed check make a re-run a no-op. Verified before authoring: 6 profiles, 0 with a value. (7) **`ai_personas.display_name` and `expert_profiles.display_name` are untouched** — public parody brand copy and a dead legacy table, neither a person's name; pinned PRESENT so an over-broad sweep fails. New pgTAP **027** pins the outcome universally over `pg_proc.prosrc`, so a future function — or a `CREATE OR REPLACE` hotfix authored against a stale body, the exact failure the runbook warns about — fails loudly. **2026-08-05 — Builder (identity ruling — not a milestone task):**
- **D115** Identity-ruling build mechanics (Chris's ruling 2026-08-05; spec v2.9; migration 075). (1) **No schema change, on purpose.** The earlier attempt (PR #96) renamed `profiles.display_name` → `full_name`; three reviewers rejected it, and the deploy-order argument is the one that generalizes: production runs the current schema, so any rename breaks the site in one merge order or the other. Storing nothing needs no DDL — the column is NULLABLE with no default, so the old app reads NULL and falls back to `@username` (the post-ruling render anyway) and the new app never reads it. (2) **The stored names are cleared, not just stopped.** Accounts created before the ruling already carry OAuth real names, and `profiles` is world-readable, so stopping the write alone would leave the leak alive for exactly the users who hit it. `UPDATE profiles SET display_name = NULL` is DML, idempotent, and invisible to both app versions. Restoring them is a real bug worth its own PR — smuggling a handle-namespace behaviour change into a privacy fix is how the 051 regression happened in the first place. **Flagged for a follow-up, deliberately not fixed here.** (4) **The other five readers are left alone.** `notify_list_followers` / `create_league` / `seat_league_member_internal` / `get_join_preview` / `draft_actor_name` each read the column through `COALESCE(..., username)`. With it permanently NULL they resolve to the handle with no edit — and `CREATE OR REPLACE`-ing league functions that do not exist in production would plant orphans there. (5) **Personas keep their name, under their existing column.** The privacy rationale does not apply to a fictional analyst with no human behind it, and the "(AI)" suffix is a transparency device (spec-ai-expert-personas §4.6). Rendering `@bathew-merry-ai` instead of "Bathew Merry (AI)" would be an unrelated product regression. PR #96's `ai_personas.display_name` → `persona_name` rename is DROPPED: no schema churn in this PR. `expert_profiles.display_name` is likewise left alone — dead legacy, no reader anywhere in the app. (6) **Two-line identities collapse to one.** Surfaces that rendered "name" over "@handle" (account menu, profile header, follower rows, command palette) now render the handle once — keeping both lines would print the same string twice. `PublicListCard` and the explore feed gained an OPTIONAL `name`, set only for personas, rather than forking a second card component. PR #96 shipped helper text promising privacy the database did not provide; the fix is not better copy, it is having nothing to describe. - **D26** Synthetic-tier design points. (1) **PRNG streams are keyed by (seed, playerId) only — never scenario id** (FNV-1a + mulberry32, `synthetic/prng.ts`): same-seed scenarios share stat lines, which is what makes the `provider_outage` back-fill proof an *equality against a same-seed `happy_path` world* instead of a self-referential recomputation. **2026-07-21 — Builder (M1 batch-5 findings remediation, R57–R61):**
- **D58** Scoring-module failure semantics for corrupt inputs (the two R58/R59 rulings, both pinned by test). **(1) R58 — an unmappable tier source value is UNREPORTED (family absent → pending), never an all-zero delivered family.** The decision hinged on whether the published bucket tables are real-contiguous (which would justify clamping/flooring a fractional value into a bucket) or integer-gapped: they are **integer-gapped** — ESPN's Scoring-Formats article prints PA `1–6 / 7–13 / 14–17 / …` and YA `100–199 / 200–299 / …` (re-verified value-for-value by the batch-4 review), leaving real-valued gaps between adjacent buckets (13.5, 99.5), so the tables' domain is the integers and there is no defensible bucket to clamp into. Consequence: `familyMaps` requires an INTEGER inside ≥1 bucket; a fractional value is out-of-domain even when it happens to sit inside an interval (14.5 pends the family, same as 13.5 — no partial acceptance of corrupt data), and a negative PA (below `def_pa_0`'s pinned floor) pends. Pinned at the exact review-probed gap values (PA=13.5, YA=99.5, negative PA, plus in-interval-fractional PA=14.5); the one-hot property extended beyond integers (fractional/negative/non-finite sweep) asserting *delivered ⇔ integer-in-a-bucket, and delivered ⇒ exactly one hot per platform set*; a named counter-pin proves the all-zero-family state (and partial-family emission) is unconstructible. **(2) R59 — a corrupt rules coefficient THROWS (TypeError naming every offending key), the loud option:** a non-finite-number coefficient in `scoring_rules_snapshot` is corrupt config, not missing data — marking it pending would misbadge corrupt config as "waiting on stats" (the reviewer's own analysis), and letting it through NaN-poisons a total `NUMERIC(8,2)` will store (Postgres numeric has NaN — live-verified in the review). Validation runs up-front over all rules keys (including keys with no delivered stat — corrupt config is never quietly parked as pending); string-numerics (`"0.5"`) throw too, since silent coercion masks the corruption the L.A1.11 freeze should have caught. Pinned: NaN can never reach the return value — every adversarial coefficient shape either throws TypeError or yields a finite total, plus a finite-total assertion inside the 250-run property. The M4 worker (L.D1) decides catch-and-quarantine vs fail-the-run at the call site (F23's composition row is where that lands); the module's contract is simply *never emit a poisoned or silently-wrong breakdown*. **(3) R61 taken:** the round(full sum)≠Σ(rounded perKey) rule now has a stored-literal discriminating pin (`{a:0.111,b:0.111}×{a:3,b:3} → 0.67`; Σ-of-rounded yields 0.66) beside the statistical property. **(4) R57's spec fold-back is v2.8.4** (§7.3.3 parenthetical + changelog; header Version field corrected 2.8.1 → 2.8.4 in passing — it had been stale since v2.8.2).

Claimed-then-revoked multi-use: revocation refuses FURTHER claims even with uses remaining; prior claimers keep their seats (not retroactive) — both pinned. (4) **E54 mechanics:** the stint INSERT runs FIRST in the seat-targeted block so an occupied seat hits `one_open_stint_per_team` (the spec-named mechanism; `league_members`' UNIQUE(league_id, team_id) is the second net, same handler); the 23505 handler marks the invite expired (`expires_at = now()` — instantly expired under (3)), notifies the commissioner (type `league_invite`, event `seat_conflict`), and returns seat_filled. (6) **Capacity under the league-row lock:** claim/join take the league FOR UPDATE before counting active (non-retired) franchises, so concurrent joins serialize and teams ≤ team_count holds; the same lock serializes against 061's F28 shrink floor (`team_count >= seated count`, both writers). At capacity → friendly "league is full", ZERO writes (D47 — no unseated member rows). (1) **The hole:** the declared "settings = the FULL L.A1.6 contract object" contract was unenforced — every `leagueSettingsSchema` field default-fills, so a one-key body (`{settings:{median_game:true}}`) parsed clean and silently reset the ENTIRE settings surface to catalog defaults (review live-proof: team_count 14→12, faab_budget 777→100 with the §12.2 re-seed amplifying it to every seat's balance, and `draft.draft_scheduled_at` NULLED while status stayed `scheduled` — exactly the state the gate-item-3 enforcement point exists to prevent). (2) **The choice, merge over reject-partial:** merge is the REST-correct PATCH reading, matches what L.A2.4's settings panel will send (per-group saves — the panel can send just its group), and a FULL object merges to itself so the sanctioned GET-detail → edit → PATCH-back round-trip is byte-identical to before; reject-partial would have forced every client to always send full objects and still needed a deep-required schema variant to close the NESTED variant of the same hole (a partial `draft` block default-filling `draft_scheduled_at` to null). (3) **Mechanics:** the settings path ALWAYS reads the CURRENT stored settings first (RLS-scoped client, same service call) and deep-merges the raw partial over them — plain objects merge recursively; arrays, scalars, and null REPLACE wholesale (null is a VALUE for the nullable fields — deliberately NOT RFC-7386 key-deletion); `undefined` skipped (unrepresentable in JSON). The MERGED WHOLE then re-enters the ONE canonical strict schema (unknown keys at ANY level reject; no default can ever fill — the current row supplies every key) and `validateLeagueSettings` (cross-field rules run against the merged whole). The partial input is validated POST-merge through the single catalog schema — no hand-maintained deep-partial schema, so the D60(10) anti-pattern stays dead; the wire schema's `settings` is now `z.looseObject({})` (any JSON object; shape enforced post-merge). (b) The read-merge-write is NOT held under the RPC's row lock — D70's last-write-wins-wholesale concurrency caveat extends to interleaved read-merge-write (single-commissioner M1 reality; revisit if co-commissioner concurrent edits become real). ### Should-fix

**L.A0.5c — grants migration**

- **R2 · should-fix · PROGRESS:104 (D23) + 037_explicit_api_grants.sql:8 + commit 3d813ef — refs: tasks-M0 L.A0.5c stop condition.** The re-verification record miscounts its own surface: "all 36 public tables" — there are **40** (40 `CREATE TABLE`s, zero `DROP TABLE`s, in 001–036; 36 is the count of *applied migrations*) — and "all 7 privileges" contradicts the ACL D23 itself quotes (`arwdDxtm` = 8 bits incl. PG17 MAINTAIN). Compounds R1: the stop-condition verification record is internally inconsistent.
- **R3 · should-fix · 037:36–41 — refs: spec §12 ("RLS on every table"); spec §12.0 (REVOKE EXECUTE on league RPCs); plan §8.1–8.2; D23.** The default-ACL model flips the failure mode fail-closed → fail-open: pre-037, a forgotten grant produced a loud 42501; now a future migration that forgets `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` ships a table on which anon holds full privileges, silently. No automated backstop landed. A one-line pgTAP global assertion in 001_api_grants.sql (e.g. `is_empty($$ select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname='public' and not rowsecurity $$)`) would machine-enforce spec §12; the same fail-open logic will apply to §12.0's per-RPC REVOKEs.
- **R4 · should-fix · supabase/tests/001_api_grants.sql:30 — refs: D23 ("pins the surface"); tasks-M0 L.A0.5c item 3.** The pin has holes: the canary table (`id int primary key`) creates no sequence and there is no `has_sequence_privilege` assertion, so 037's sequence catch-up grant *and* sequence default ACL have zero coverage — deleting 037 lines 29 and 38–39 still passes 10/10. No existing-routine catch-up witness either (e.g. the 004 reorder RPC), and the table/function checks sample SELECT/INSERT/EXECUTE rather than the full privilege set D23 claims to pin.
- **R5 · should-fix · 037:30 + 019_list_update_notifications.sql:18 — refs: spec §12.0; plan §8.3; D23.** D23's doctrine "grants stay uniformly broad and RLS is the only effective gate" is false for routines: SECURITY DEFINER bodies bypass RLS. 037 versions anon EXECUTE on `notify_list_followers(p_list_id, p_actor)` — SECURITY DEFINER, zero `auth.*` checks in the body, caller-supplied `p_actor` — which can insert notifications attributed to arbitrary users. The exposure pre-exists under the legacy model, but the migration now codifies it; the doctrine needs a SECURITY DEFINER carve-out, and future league RPCs need §8.3 in-body auth + explicit REVOKE discipline.
- **R6 · should-fix · 037 (process) — refs: plan §8.1 ("staging-clone rehearsal noted"); plan §2.3.** §8.1's rehearsal line is silently skipped: no note in the migration, D23, the session log, or commit 3d813ef, and no waiver covers it (contrast D10/D23, which waive other checklist lines explicitly).

**Verified sound (claims audited and confirmed):**

- **RETURNING-count RLS deny pattern (003_nfl_weeks.sql) is sound, not masking.** The layering closes every hole I could construct: a permissive UPDATE/DELETE policy flips the count 0→18 and fails; `policies_are` catches a `USING (false)` decoy write policy by name; RLS-disabled trips both the count tests (18 affected) and the 001 global backstop; and the "0 rows because the seed is missing" mask is excluded by the same-role SELECT-sees-18 pin immediately before each deny block. INSERT correctly expects 42501 (the one write RLS raises on rather than filters).
- **2026 seed verified against its claimed source.** Live Sleeper schedule fetch: week 1's first game IS Wed 2026-09-09, week 12 IS the second Wednesday slate (Nov 25) — the banner's claims are true, and all 18 `starts_at` rows equal "Wednesday 00:00 ET preceding the week's first game" for the fetched slate (incl. wk18's Sun-only slate → Wed 2027-01-06). DST handling correct: Nov 1 2026 fall-back puts wk8's window at −05 while its start is −04, wk9 onward −05/−05; every correction window is the following Thursday 06:00 ET per §23.4.
- **Plan §8.1/§8.2 pass literally for 039** with both waivers now recorded in-banner (D10 realtime; §8.1 rehearsal per the R6 go-forward rule); typegen committed with the hand-written alias block preserved (memory risk avoided).

An off-by-one (`>` vs `>=`) at any of these instants fails a test.
- **Record→replay equality WOULD catch broken Date revival:** the round-trip transcript compares live `Date` objects against revived bodies with `toEqual`, which distinguishes `Date` from ISO string; a dedicated `instanceof` + gameDate-stays-string pin backs it up. D27 parse rejects unknown format and version loudly (both asserted).

| R26, R30 (nits) | **Left for L.A0.6 as the review routed them:** R26 records that writer-side back-fill is unproven (a gate-task premise, nothing to fix here); R30 documents the sanctioned `recordedProviderName` wrapper the gate builder writes when composing byte-identical replay ingestion. *(Both resolved 2026-07-19 in L.A0.6: R26 → writer-side cumulative back-fill gate assertion; R30 → `impersonateRecordedProvider` opt-in, D29/D30.)* |

### Should-fix

- **R22 · should-fix · .eslintrc.json:50 — refs: D3/R15 ("mechanical, not convention"); D26 item 5.** The new `Math.random` guard did not inherit the R15 widening the Date guard got. Empirically probed via ESLint stdin against `src/lib/leagues/**`: `globalThis.Math.random()` and `const M = Math; M.random()` are both **lint-clean** — the exact two escape shapes (globalThis routing, constructor/object aliasing) R15 closed for `Date`. `crypto.getRandomValues(...)` is also unbanned (a common "random" reach). D26 records "two new D3-style lint selectors," but the shipped guard is strictly narrower than the D3 guard it cites. Add `MemberExpression[object.name='globalThis'][property.name='Math']`, Math-aliasing selectors, and (optionally) a crypto.getRandomValues ban.
- **R23 · should-fix · synthetic-stats-provider.test.ts:128 + scenarios.ts:21 — refs: §23.6 ("versioned, deterministic, re-runnable"); D26 (library versioning).** No test pins any concrete PRNG-derived stat value against a stored golden constant. Both determinism tests compare two in-process runs of the same code (`fullWeekTranscript` twice; outage vs happy_path), so an *unintended* behavior change — a draw-order refactor in `finalLine`, a range tweak, a `mulberry32` edit — changes every scenario's "deterministic" world while the entire suite stays green. That defeats the versioning contract the schema declares ("bump `version` on ANY behavior change"): nothing can detect an unversioned behavior change, and any future fixture/simulator run pinned against library v1 silently diverges. One golden test (e.g. the full DEFAULT_SEED stat line for one player per position, as literals) makes version bumps mechanical instead of honor-system.
- **R24 · should-fix · live-stats.test.ts:40 — refs: the falsifiability standard this batch claims throughout; §23.2.** The seam's game-window boundary is the one instant-sensitive edge in this diff with **no** boundary pin: tests run mid-window (18:00Z on game day) and 3 days out, never at `kickoffDay` exactly or `kickoffDay + 36h` exactly (live-stats.ts:163 — both edges inclusive). An off-by-one in either comparison (`>=`→`>`, `<=`→`<`) passes the suite. Two exact-instant cases close it; the window semantics are load-bearing for the finalization pass (`weeksToFinalize` gets `inWindow` from this check).

### Nit

- **R25 · nit · synthetic-stats-provider.ts:249 — refs: D25 ("provider-reported calendar day").** Synthetic derives `gameDate` from the kickoff's **UTC** day, so the SNF game (Sun 8:20pm ET) reports Monday `2026-09-21`, while the sleeper tier reports the ET day (checked-in 2025 fixture: Sunday games carry the Sunday date). Literally D25-compliant but a cross-tier semantic drift in the same field: composed with the seam's UTC-day-start+36h window it shifts a late game's window by a day vs. real data. Harmless on the current slate (earlier games open the window); worth aligning to the ET day before L.A0.6 composes synthetic with the seam.
- **R26 · nit · scenario-beats.test.ts:290 (D26 back-fill proof) — refs: §23.2 (back-fill on recovery).** Answering the brief directly: the outage-vs-happy_path equality is genuinely cross-scenario (it would catch PRNG streams keyed by scenario id, or outage state leaking into values — the two ways this provider *could* regress), but it is **not an independent computation**: both sides run the identical pure `finalLine`/`progress` code on identical inputs, and since the provider is stateless the equality is near-tautological. What §23.2 actually cares about — writer-side cumulative back-fill after a degraded window (upserts catching up in `player_stats`) — is untested anywhere in this batch and lands on L.A0.6. Fine for M0 provider scope; recorded so the gate task doesn't inherit "back-fill is proven" as a premise.
- **R27 · nit · scripts/record-fixtures.ts:90,99 — refs: D27 (identity lives IN the artifact).** The CLI hardcodes `provider: 'sleeper'` in the header and `sleeper.jsonl.gz` in the path instead of reading `provider.name` — re-introducing at write time exactly the guessing D27 exists to prevent. Equal today; a silent lie the day the CLI wraps any other provider.
- **R28 · nit · fixture-format.ts:68 — refs: D27 ("parse-rejected loudly on mismatch").** Loud rejection covers `format`/`version` only; a header missing `provider`/`season`/`week` parses fine and yields `name = 'fixture:undefined'` downstream. A three-field presence check would make the identity guarantee total.
- **R29 · nit · fixture-replay-provider.ts:104 — refs: D6 (failures replay as failures).** Recorded failures replay as a generic `Error` carrying the message only — the recorded `status` (e.g. 429 vs 500) is dropped, so a future consumer branching on status sees a different shape live vs replay. No consumer branches today.
- **R30 · nit · D24/D28 seam composition (live-stats.ts:94 + fixture-replay-provider.ts:58).** D24's "record/replay reproduces today's writes" is true for every column *except* `source`: the writer stamps `provider.name`, and replay's name is `'fixture:sleeper'`, so a replayed ingestion writes `source: 'fixture:sleeper'`. That is D28's intended honest default — but the documented opt-in (`recordedProviderName`) has **no supported mechanism** reaching the writer; L.A0.6 will have to hand-roll a delegating wrapper that overrides `name` to get byte-identical rows. Deliberate-by-design per D28; recorded so the gate builder budgets for it (and so the wrapper, when written, is recognized as the sanctioned deliberate-impersonation path, not a smell).
