Review-only — nothing fixed. **No blockers.**

**Verified clean (for the record):**

- **§12.23/§12.17 column-for-column, exactly.** `055_league_invites.sql` matches the spec's printed DDL (`docs/specs/spec-redraft-leagues.md:1282-1304`) column-for-column, plus exactly the two authorized additive pieces: the D46 send-tracking pair (`created_at NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`, `last_sent_at` nullable — erratum v2.7.1 item 4) and nothing else. `056_league_weeks.sql` matches §12.17's printed DDL (`spec:1139-1153`) column-for-column, plus exactly the two D55-recorded additions: the `status` CHECK enumerating the four values the spec only comments, and `FOREIGN KEY (season, week) REFERENCES nfl_weeks(season, week)`. pgTAP 009/010's `columns_are` pins assert the exact column sets (009:50-54, 010:42-45) — no undocumented drift in either migration.
- **The general multi-use league link is schema-complete and ungated.** No CHECK or policy in 055 ties `invited_email`/`invited_username` to anything — both are independently nullable with no constraint requiring either. A row with `target_team_id`, `invited_username`, AND `invited_email` all NULL (the unrestricted/open-link case) is fully insertable and, being unconstrained, remains claimable-by-anyone at the schema level — confirmed by direct constraint inspection (`pg_constraint` on `league_invites`: only FKs + the `token` UNIQUE + PK, no CHECK at all). Separately, `leagues.invite_code`/`invite_slug` (the persistent per-league link the Q5 "always visible and copyable" bar actually rests on, per `tasks-M1-league-foundation.md:341`) is **not** reachable via a direct client SELECT on `leagues` today — the 052 policy swap (`is_league_member(id) OR owner_id = auth.uid()`) never carried an invite-code carve-out, before or after 055/056 — but this is by design, not a regression: the join flow's own plan (`tasks-M1:284,350`) routes every pre-auth resolution (seat token → invite_code → invite_slug) through `get_join_preview`, a planned `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC with a documented anon-`EXECUTE` carve-out, which bypasses `leagues` RLS entirely by construction. Nothing in 055/056 narrows or blocks that plan; it's simply not built yet (tracked as L.A1.14, already on the checklist — see the ledger gap below for the one piece of it that isn't tracked as sharply as it should be).
- **Privacy posture on `league_invites` holds.** The only policy touching the table anywhere in 001–056 is `"Invites viewable by commish"` (`is_league_commish`-scoped SELECT) — grepped for every migration and every function/view; nothing else references `league_invites`. pgTAP 009 counter-pins a non-commish member (sees 0), a non-member (sees 0), and cross-league (a commish sees 0 of another league's invites) — independently re-derivable from the policy predicate alone (no `OR` branch exists for `invited_email = auth.email()` or `claimed_by = auth.uid()`). `invited_email` is therefore unreachable pre-claim by anyone but the commissioner reading the row directly; D48 additionally commits the not-yet-built preview RPC to return only league name + team label + inviter display name (no email). Confirmed clean.
- **Record integrity.** D54 (`PROGRESS:215`) matches `055_league_invites.sql` exactly (RLS shape, CITEXT-first claim, `expires_at`-vs-`created_at` boundary framing); D55 (`PROGRESS:218`) matches `056_league_weeks.sql` exactly (RLS shape, the two additive deviations, the pgTAP-009-already-taken numbering note). The 055→059 renumbering is consistent everywhere checked: PROGRESS §2's checklist, `tasks-M1-league-foundation.md`'s §7 table and per-task headers, and the decisions log all agree on 055/`league_invites` and 056/`league_weeks` — no stale "043"/"044" references survive for these two. The branch+PR rule (CLAUDE.md Active Builds, added `3d82493`) is fully respected in the visible history: `git log --first-parent` on `main` is a pure chain of "Merge pull request" commits, and both 055's commit (`8f16707`) and 056's commit (`ed2e94f`) sit on feature branches (`feat/M1-L.A1.4-league-invites`, `feat/M1-L.A1.5-league-weeks`) merged via PR #28/#30 — neither landed on `main` directly, before or after the rule existed.
- **`league_weeks.status`'s CHECK is real defense-in-depth, not just a client-facing gate.** Live-probed as the Postgres superuser (RLS-bypassing) role: `INSERT ... status = 'banana'` still throws `23514`. ### Resolution — 2026-07-20 (Builder, branch `fix/M1-batch3-review-findings-R47-R48`)

*Both findings resolved, docs-only — no migration, no schema change (rationale below). No proof run owed: nothing executable changed; the pgTAP suite's 401/401 baseline from the review session stands.*

|---|---|
| R47 | this commit — **§6 Forward obligations ledger** added (18 entries, F1–F18) seeded from a full sweep of the D/R/Q records: the four R47-named scatterees (D53 retire cycle, D48 preview exposure, R46 stint hand-off, D55 transition trigger) plus the Q6 free-user negative tests and 13 more found sweeping (D7/D10/D16/D23-R1/D38/D40/Q2-D15/Q3/Q5-D37/Q7.2/R19/C11-C12). Header states the discharge rule: builders MUST flip a listed obligation in the same PR that builds its task; reviewers audit every batch |
| R48 | **Ledger entry F6, NOT a migration — Builder judgment call as delegated.** Why not DB CHECKs now: **(a)** the mutual-exclusivity CHECK (`NOT (revoked_at AND claimed_at)`) would encode claim semantics L.A1.14 hasn't defined — the review's own probe B shape (claimed_at set AND later revoked_at set) is plausibly *legitimate* for a multi-use invite: some uses claimed, then the commissioner revokes further use; a CHECK baked in now risks a revert migration the day the claim RPC defines this. **(b)** `CHECK (use_count <= max_uses)` alone is safer but settles a clamp-vs-block question that belongs to the RPC (055's own comment says commissioners "may raise" `max_uses` — whether one may ever *lower* it below `use_count` is undefined), and shipping half the backstop invites false confidence. **(c)** Cost: a CHECK-only migration would take 057 and shift the schema lane a third time in one week (057 def_ya → 058, cascading the §7 table + PROGRESS §2 again) for two backstops on a table with **zero writers of any kind** — failing the D53 proportionality test 056's status CHECK passed (that one was free, in-table, at creation). The invariants land as `claim_league_invite`'s in-body duty with pins, tracked as F6 so L.A1.14 can't start without tripping over it |

### Should-fix

- **R47 · should-fix · no consolidated forward-obligations ledger (PROGRESS-leagues.md).** The pre-auth claim preview's field-exposure boundary (§12.23 as amended by D48: league name + team label + inviter display name — explicitly **not** `invited_email`) has no pgTAP pin yet, because `get_join_preview` (L.A1.14) doesn't exist. That's expected — but unlike D53's explicit phrasing for `retire_franchise`'s cycle-rejection duty ("a pgTAP pin due when that RPC lands (M4, D42)", `PROGRESS:212`), no comparable "pin due" sentence exists anywhere for this one; `055_league_invites.sql:32-36` and D48 (`PROGRESS:199`) describe the *plan*, not a tracked duty a future session is instructed to check off. Auditing PROGRESS for siblings turned up at least two more of the same shape, none consolidated: (a) R46's "started_at-reuse hand-off note" (`PROGRESS:384,403`) — the claim/assign RPCs (L.A1.14/L.A1.15) "must close-before-open and never reuse a `started_at`" or collide with `team_managers`' `UNIQUE(team_id, user_id, started_at)`; (b) D55's deferred `league_weeks` status-*transition* validation (`PROGRESS:218`) — legal transitions between the four CHECK-enumerated values are unenforced until M4's `league-week-advance` job lands, with no forward pin recorded beyond the migration-comment aside. All three (plus D53's own) currently live only inside decisions-log prose or migration-comment asides — nothing a session landing L.A1.14 or M4's schedule engine is pointed at systematically. Recommend a dedicated "Forward obligations" section in PROGRESS (or a checklist column) enumerating at minimum: `get_join_preview` field-exposure pin (L.A1.14), `retire_franchise` cycle-rejection pin (M4/D42, already named in D53), claim/assign `started_at`-reuse guard (L.A1.14/L.A1.15), `league_weeks` status-transition trigger (M4 `league-week-advance`).

### Nit

- **R48 · nit · `league_invites` has no algebraic CHECK backstops (055_league_invites.sql:57-73) — probed live (local stack, rolled back).** None of the following are constrained at the DB layer: `use_count` exceeding `max_uses` (inserted `max_uses=1, use_count=5` cleanly); `revoked_at` and `claimed_by`/`claimed_at` set simultaneously (inserted cleanly — a row can be both "claimed" and "revoked" with no ordering relationship enforced, confirmed both `claimed→revoked` and the reverse timestamp order both insert cleanly); `expires_at` in the past at INSERT time (inserted cleanly, `already_expired = true`). All of this is currently inert — no role has a write path to the table at all — so the gap is `claim_league_invite`'s (L.A1.14) future in-body responsibility, the same "no scheduled owner yet" situation R40/D53 already named for the succession-cycle gap. Unlike that gap, this one isn't recorded as a hand-off anywhere, and — notably — 056 shipped in the very same session added exactly this class of free algebraic backstop pre-emptively (the `status` CHECK, justified specifically because "the same gap on a fresh table gets fixed at creation instead of waiting for a review pass," `056_league_weeks.sql:19-21`) while 055 didn't extend that reasoning to its own table's obvious candidates (`CHECK (use_count <= max_uses)`, `CHECK (NOT (revoked_at IS NOT NULL AND claimed_at IS NOT NULL))`). Cheap, no rush given the zero-writer state, but worth a line in R47's ledger so it isn't the thing nobody remembers when L.A1.14 starts writing to this table.

Method: **semantics review, not schema** — the pending/zero boundary, the F20 structural guarantee, and the rounding contract each probed with live constructed inputs (`tsx` against the shipped modules); **the NUMERIC(8,2) rounding claim tested live on the local stack** (temp table on `supabase_db_fieldscout`, both numeric-literal and float8 assignment paths), not reasoned from documentation; full 60-test suite re-run green this session. Review-only — nothing fixed. Findings R57–R61 (4 should-fix, 1 nit); **no blockers**.*

**Verified sound (for the record):**

- **The §7.3.3 dot-product contract holds under adversarial inputs.** Unknown stat keys ignored (probed: extra keys leave the breakdown deep-equal); undelivered rules keys land in `pending` with no `perKey` entry in every path — a stat delivered AS `null` (out-of-type but JSONB-realistic) resolves pending via the `typeof`/`isFinite` gate, same as absent, which is the honest reading; delivered-zero is the pinned opposite (real `perKey: 0`, no badge). No mid-computation delivery hazard exists: `Object.entries(rules)` snapshots and the function is pure/synchronous.
- **F20's structural guarantee survives every input shape tried.** Inbound `def_pa_*`/`def_ya_*` keys are stripped unconditionally and re-emitted only from a delivered source (probed: bogus `def_pa_46_plus: 1` without source → absent; with source → recomputed to 0); families deliver independently (PA=0 without YA → full PA family 0/1, all 9 YA keys absent → exactly the YA rules keys pending — tested and re-probed); non-finite source → family absent → pending. Within `deriveTierIndicators` an indicator-without-source state is unconstructible. *(The guarantee is module-local — the composition obligation is R60(b).)*
- **NUMERIC(8,2) live result: half away from zero, matching the implementation.** Temp-table assignment on the local stack: `−0.005 → −0.01`, `−0.015 → −0.02`, `−2.675 → −2.68`, float8 path identical — `roundHalfUp`'s pinned `−0.005 → −0.01` is exactly what the DB does. D57(2)'s reading is now live-verified, not just asserted. *(The spec-term ambiguity is R57.)*
- **E38's round(sum)≠sum(round) rule is genuinely carried by the property test.** The 250-run recompute accumulates at full precision then rounds once; generated contributions carry 3 decimals, so a Σ-of-rounded-perKey implementation diverges from the recompute with near-certainty across 250×~12 keys. `perKey` full-precision values cannot currently leak into a display path: the modules have **zero consumers** (grep-verified — only the two modules + their tests), and both the interface docstring and D57(3) mark `perKey` as full-precision/not-the-stored-total. *(That no stored-literal pin discriminates the two implementations is R61.)*
- **The one-hot property would catch both bug classes asked of it, on the integer domain.** A both-buckets-hot bug fails the per-platform sums (=2) at every overlapping value; an off-by-one boundary (e.g. `def_pa_14_17` hi=18 or hi=16) fails the sum at the seam integer (=2 or =0) inside the scanned PA 0–80 / YA −30–650 ranges, independently of the edge pins — the pins and the property each catch it alone. The platform-set literals in the test are themselves anchored by the both-directions registry cross-check. *(The property's integer-only domain is the gap — R58.)*
- **Record integrity clean.** D57 matches what shipped item-for-item (test count 60 re-run green; 11/9 family sizes; −0.005 pin; toPrecision(13) snap; mulberry32 seeding; key-agnostic calculator verified — no registry import); the prompt-vs-doc discrepancy (the task prompt's "migration 058" parenthetical vs tasks-M1's pure-TS L.A1.8) is recorded in both D57 and the PR #37 body; F20's flip carries the required semantics + pointer (D57(1)) and correctly records "no ruled alternative"; branch+PR discipline respected (`feat/M1-L.A1.8-scoring-calculator`, PR #37); session-log claims re-verified.

### Resolution — 2026-07-21 (Builder, branch `fix/M1-batch5-review-findings-R57-R61`)

*All four should-fixes resolved; nit R61 taken. Semantics decisions recorded as **D58** (both R58 and R59 required a deliberate ruling, not just a guard). Proof (shown in session): fresh `db reset` 001–057 clean · `test:db` **435/435** · vitest **234/234** (12 new in `src/lib/leagues/scoring/`) · `test:gate` **24/24** · type-check clean · lint (pre-existing `auction-draft-room.tsx` warning only). **Three new-pin break probes run live then reverted:** (i) R58 guard removed (emit family whenever the source is finite — the exact pre-fix behavior) → **exactly the 6 new R58 tests fail** (the 4 gap-value pins at 13.5/−3/14.5/99.5, the family-independence test, the unconstructibility counter-pin), nothing else; (ii) R59 throw removed → **exactly the 5 new corrupt-coefficient pins fail**, nothing else; (iii) Σ-of-rounded-perKey substituted for full-precision accumulation → the R61 literal pin fails (0.66 ≠ 0.67) alongside the 250-run property, confirming the pin discriminates on its own.*

### Should-fix

- **R57 · should-fix · calculator.ts:36-49 (`roundHalfUp` doc) + spec §7.3.3 precision rule — "half-up" is ecosystem-ambiguous and the spec never pins which meaning; the implementation's choice is right but lives only in the decisions log; refs: E38 (determinism), D57(2), the §3 fold-back discipline.** The two authorities the rounding question names genuinely diverge at negative half-cent boundaries: strict "round half up" (the Wikipedia/IEEE toward-+∞ convention) gives `−0.005 → −0.00`, while Postgres `NUMERIC(8,2)` assignment — **tested live this session, both numeric-literal and float8 paths** — gives `−0.005 → −0.01` (half away from zero; Java's `RoundingMode.HALF_UP` also means away-from-zero, so the bare term supports both readings). The implementation sides with the DB, which is the only coherent choice under E38's determinism rule (JS result ≡ stored result), and pins it at `−0.005 → −0.01`. But the spec text still says bare "half-up": a future implementer (or the L.D1 writer's author) reading §7.3.3 alone can pick the toward-+∞ reading and diverge from both this module and the column type on negative totals (all-miss K weeks, INT-heavy QB weeks). The divergence window is narrow — with 2-decimal template coefficients × integer stats every sum is exact at 2 decimals, so a negative half-cent boundary needs ≥3-decimal coefficients — but the determinism rule is absolute and the fix is one line. Fold a spec erratum (changelog + §7.3.3 parenthetical): *"half-up = round half away from zero, matching NUMERIC(8,2) assignment; −0.005 → −0.01"* — per the repo's own rule that resolved ambiguities get folded back into the spec, not left in D-rows.
- **R58 · should-fix · derive-stats.ts:83-91 (`emitFamily`) — a delivered source value that lands in no bucket emits an all-zero family: delivered-zero everywhere, nothing hot, nothing pending — the silent-wrong-total class E61/F20 exist to prevent; refs: §23.5, E61, F20, D57(1).** Probed live: `def_points_allowed: 13.5` → all 11 PA keys delivered as 0 (13.5 falls between `def_pa_7_13` and `def_pa_14_20`; both platform sums = 0, violating the one-hot invariant the property test asserts — but that property only scans **integers**, so the state is invisible to it); `def_yards_allowed: 99.5` → same for YA; a (bogus) negative PA → same, since `def_pa_0` pins lo=0. Downstream, every tier rules key scores a delivered 0 with an empty `pending` — for ESPN templates that silently erases the D/ST tier component (up to ±5 points/side) with no badge, which is a *worse* state than the pre-F20 all-pending bug (that one was at least honest). Reachability today is low — `player_stats` sources are INTEGER columns (057), and nothing calls these modules yet — but the helper's input is provider-shaped `Record<string, number>`, not column-shaped, and nothing range-guards it. Cheap close: treat a source value matching **no** bucket as unreported (family absent → pending; for PA that also covers negatives), and extend the one-hot property to assert *delivered ⇒ exactly one hot per platform set* over non-integer samples so the wrong fix (leaving the gap) can't pass.
- **R59 · should-fix · calculator.ts:64-72 — the delivered-stat guard is one-sided: a malformed rules **coefficient** poisons the total to NaN, and NUMERIC(8,2) accepts NaN, so the poisoned total is storable; refs: E61 ("never a silent wrong total"), §7.3.3 snapshot rule, D57(3)'s defensive clause.** Probed live: `{ receptions: "abc" }` (rules values come from `scoring_rules_snapshot` JSONB, which can carry strings) → `contribution = NaN` → `total: NaN` (`roundHalfUp` propagates it), and `INSERT 'NaN'` into a `NUMERIC(8,2)` column **succeeds** (live-tested — Postgres numeric has a NaN value), so nothing downstream is guaranteed to throw. A string-numeric coefficient (`"0.5"`) silently coerces and scores (×4 → 2) — works by accident, masking a corrupt snapshot. The module already defends the *stats* side against exactly this class (non-finite → pending, D57's "never poisoning a total"); the rules side, same trust boundary (a JSONB blob), has no guard. Reachability requires a corrupt snapshot — v1 rules are code-authored templates frozen via the L.A1.11 RPC — but the v1.1 custom editor (F21's scope) makes rules user-shaped, and this module is the last line. Semantics call for the Builder to make **and record**: marking a bad-coefficient key `pending` would misbadge corrupt config as "waiting on data," so the honest options are throw (corrupt snapshot = programming/config error, loud) or a distinct breakdown flag; either way, pin it with a test.
- **R60 · should-fix · PROGRESS §6 — two hand-offs this task created live only in prose; per the §6 header rule (R51: "creating a hand-off without an F-row is itself a review finding") both need rows; refs: R51 precedent, E38, F20/D57(1), D44.** **(a) Rounding vs the real writer (L.D1):** D57(2)'s NUMERIC-matching claim carried no DB evidence at build time (this review supplied it — live temp-table proof, see header), and the actual consistency obligation — the L.D1 writer stores the **JS-rounded** total into `matchups`/`team_week_results` `NUMERIC(8,2)`, with a pin proving no path lets the DB do the rounding on a diverging value (benign only while both round half-away-from-zero; E38's determinism must be *pinned* at the writer, not inherited silently) — belongs to a task that doesn't exist yet in any ledger row. Add F22 → discharged by L.D1 (M4). **(b) The derive→score composition:** F20's guarantee is module-local — `scorePlayerWeek` happily accepts raw stats that never passed `deriveTierIndicators` (tier rules keys then read pending forever), and a worker that skips derive also loses the inbound-indicator stripping (D44's "never stored" laundering guard). The composition appears only in L.A1.10's task-text usage sketch (`scorePlayerWeek(template.rules, derive(stats))`); the production call site is M4's `score-league-week` (§22.2/L.D1), and no F-row keys it. Add F23 → *`score-league-week` composes `deriveTierIndicators` before `scorePlayerWeek`; pinned at the worker* — discharged by L.D1 (M4), with L.A1.10 as the interim proof-of-pattern.

### Nit

- **R61 · nit · calculator.test.ts — no stored-literal golden pin discriminates round(full sum) from Σ(rounded perKey); only the 250-run property carries E38's precision rule; refs: §4.3(a) (golden pins as stored literals), E38, D57(3).** Every literal pin's contributions are exact at ≤2 decimals (QB 11.48+8−2+2+1.2; E38 tie 9.2+6+0.04) — a Σ-of-rounded implementation passes all of them; the single-key `0.335×3 → 1.01` pin rounds identically under both (one entry). The property test does catch the wrong implementation (near-certainly, per the verified-sound note), but §4.3(a)'s point is a falsifiable *literal*: one two-key pin, e.g. rules `{a: 0.111, b: 0.111}` × stats `{a: 3, b: 3}` → full sum 0.666 → `total: 0.67` (a Σ-of-rounded impl yields 0.33+0.33 = **0.66**), pins the rule as a stored literal instead of a statistical consequence.

Behavior is correct today (verified: set → slug, clear(NULL) → null column, idempotent re-clear, preview `{found:false}`, join `not_found`), but the regression mode is real and specific: change `.nullable()` to `.optional()` in `setSlugInputSchema` and the cast ships `undefined`, PostgREST drops the key (no DEFAULT on `p_slug`), the service's catch-all returns 500, and every existing test still passes. *Fix direction: one pgTAP assert (`set_league_invite_slug(<l2>, NULL)` → `{"invite_slug":null}` + column IS NULL + preview `{found:false}`) and one vitest case (crosses the PostgREST wire — that one is load-bearing).*

## Review findings — 2026-07-26 (M1 batch 15)

*Reviewer session (fresh context, red-team brief): diff = PR #60 (`feat/M1-L.A1.15-member-management` — L.A1.15, migration 063 member management + 062 amended in place + pgTAP 017 + `members-service.ts` + 3 routes + the stack suite). **Method: a 101-agent adversarial pass — 7 review lenses plus a completeness critic and a gap round, every surviving candidate put through 3 INDEPENDENT refuters each required to reproduce from its own fixture rather than re-run the reporter's. 29 candidates reached refutation; **19 were REFUTED** and dropped; 10 survived (R90–R99: 5 should-fix, 5 nits). Live probing ran exclusively inside `BEGIN … ROLLBACK` with residue counts and `git status --short` verified clean after every probe.** VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — no blocker, no spec violation, no data-corruption path reachable on M1's shipped surface. Findings recorded verbatim below; resolution on the SAME branch (fix-then-merge — no new PR). The refutation count is recorded because it is the evidence that the surviving 10 are not noise.*

**What the pass CONFIRMED (recorded so no later session re-litigates it):** the S1 fix on the amended 062 (the seat-targeted claim branch and `assign_manager` genuinely FILL an existing placeholder; the live-proven 23505→`seat_filled` mislabel is gone); mode semantics (takeover closes with `replaced` and reseats with no `league_invites` row touched; vacate sets `orphaned` per §7.2.1(c) and closes `kicked`; leave closes `left`) — two candidates attacking them were refuted 3/3 against §7.2.1(a); the atomic transfer under the league lock (exactly one commissioner survives every path including the failed replay; the co-commissioner coup raises 42501; creator protection fires on the correct target); capacity across all five seat paths including the F28 cross-writer re-run; and the S2 policy drop's blast radius — the loudest counter-thesis (that dropping the DELETE carve-out makes `add_placeholder_seat` a one-way door burning capacity and killing the open-join link) was raised by three lenses in four shapes and **refuted every time**. The whole 062-arity cluster (amend-in-place with a signature change, no `DROP FUNCTION` guard, orphaned overload) was refuted 3/3 on the unreleased-history/F12 precedent.

### Should-fix

- **R90 · should-fix · `supabase/migrations/063_league_member_management.sql`:935** — `leave_league` and `remove_manager` reassign `teams.owner_id` only on the departing member's own franchise, so every placeholder seat that user created stays owned by a proven non-member on an `ON DELETE CASCADE` FK. *Evidence:* `add_placeholder_seat` stamps `owner_id = v_uid` (063:381-383); the owner_id reassignment in `leave_league` (063:935-939) and `remove_manager` vacate/takeover (063:809-813 / 784-788) is scoped `WHERE id = v_team.id`. Three independent live probes (BEGIN…ROLLBACK, zero residue) reproduced the residual in two shapes — departed creator, and a `vacate`'d co-commissioner. In the second shape `DELETE FROM public.profiles WHERE id = <removed user>` silently destroyed both of their placeholder franchises (team_count 8, seats_counted 4 → 2) and, because `league_members_team_id_fkey` is `ON DELETE SET NULL`, left two `league_members` rows with `team_id NULL` — precisely the "invisible to every capacity check" shape ruling S2 / erratum v2.8.8 / D74(3) removed policies to eliminate. 063's own banner (063:151-152, 807-808) names this exact hazard as the reason it moves `owner_id` at all, then dodges it for one franchise. Secondary limb: the departed non-member retains `team_lineups` FOR ALL via 001:856-861 (unscoped `teams.owner_id` key, unlike 053:71-72) — INSERT and UPDATE both succeeded live — contradicting the shipped wording at 017:953/957, F36 and D74(11) ("no write path survives"). That limb sits on the pre-dispositioned C12/F18 surface; the ownership residual and its CASCADE consequence do not. *Fix direction:* in all three arms, add `UPDATE public.teams SET owner_id = <sitting commissioner>, updated_at = now() WHERE league_id = p_league_id AND owner_id = <departing user> AND id <> v_team.id`, and either land it or reword 017 §L / F36 / D74(11) so the prose stops attesting an invariant the code lacks.
- **R91 · should-fix · `supabase/tests/017_league_member_management.sql`:425** — pgTAP test 49 (and its vitest analogue) cannot fail for the reason it claims: the R86 cross-league scoping can be deleted and both suites stay green. *Evidence:* the test targets `_seat2`, which already carries u4's open stint, and asserts `throws_ok(…, 'P0001', null, …)` — code only, message wildcarded (verified against pgTAP directly: a NULL errmsg passes on a different message; the non-NULL control fails). A mutant of `assign_manager` with only `AND t.league_id = p_league_id` removed (063:571) raises `P0001 … that franchise already has a manager` on the same fixture, so the assertion still passes; the real function raises `P0001 … not part of this league`. Retargeting at a fresh unoccupied seat makes the mutant succeed outright — writing an L2 `league_members` row pointing at an L1 franchise (count=1 confirmed). `members-api-db.test.ts:283-285` is masked identically (`seatTeamId` is L1's occupied franchise, `successorId` not yet in L2, and members-service.ts:56 flattens every P0001 to 400). `grep -rn "not part of this league" supabase src docs` returns only the migration — no third pin exists. Violates tasks-M1 §4.3:73. *Fix direction:* retarget the cross-league call at a stint-free `add_placeholder_seat` seat with a user seated in neither league **and** switch to `throws_like`/message assertion — both halves are required.
- **R92 · should-fix · `supabase/tests/017_league_member_management.sql`:419** — pgTAP test 48 ("manager already has a team") is non-discriminating; deleting the pre-check it names leaves the open-stint guard raising the same SQLSTATE. *Evidence:* the target `l1_commish_team` carries the creator's open stint (opened by `create_league`, 060:302; probe: `commish_team open stints = 1`) while u4 is already seated — one call satisfies both guards, and `throws_ok(…, 'P0001', null)` pins neither. A mutant deleting only the RAISE at 063:593-594 still throws P0001 (`that franchise already has a manager`) on the test-48 fixture. On an EMPTY seat — the case that isolates the guard — the mutant instead emits `that seat was just claimed by someone else — refresh and try again`, i.e. race-flavored copy advising a refresh that cannot help. Enumerated every `assign_manager` call site in 017 (380/408/414/420/426/435/580/610/1026/1053) and the full vitest block (251-305): none covers already-seated-user → empty seat. §4.3:73 again, in the file whose own header claims to avoid the R11/R14/R26/R34/R52/R70 vacuous-fixture class. *Fix direction:* re-aim at an empty placeholder seat **and** pin the message with `throws_like` — an empty seat alone is insufficient, since the `unique_violation` handler re-raises P0001 there too.
- **R93 · should-fix · `supabase/migrations/063_league_member_management.sql`:461** — commissioner authorization is read before the `leagues … FOR UPDATE` and never re-verified, so an actor demoted while blocked on the lock still completes one privileged write. *Evidence:* `add_placeholder_seat` (345→355), `set_member_role` (428→436), `assign_manager` (544→552) and `remove_manager` (659→667) all evaluate `is_league_commish` ahead of the lock; `leave_league` alone inverts it (lock 867-870 before the role read at 876) and says so in its comment (864-866, restated in D74(8)). `set_member_role` re-reads `v_actor_role` under the lock at 461-463 but consumes it only at 473 and 488, never as a gate — a demoted actor reads back `'manager'`, misses 473/480/485, and reaches the UPDATE at 508. Same shape at 694-696/699. Probed both halves: with the pre-lock check forced to pass, a live-`manager` actor successfully promoted an accomplice to `co_commissioner`; and a separate probe confirmed a plpgsql statement re-snapshots after a lock wait (`snapshot BEFORE 4322 / AFTER 4329`, a transaction committing at 4323 while blocked), so the demotion IS visible post-lock and the function writes anyway. The "newly racy" premise holds — 054:76 dropped the FOR ALL policy and no pre-063 RPC mutates `league_members.role` or clears `user_id`. Two aggravations: the target may be the actor's own row, letting them repeatably undo their own demotion; and the creator anti-coup guards key on `v_actor_role='co_commissioner'`, so a stale actor reading `'manager'` is strictly *more* powerful than a legitimate co-commissioner. *Fix direction:* after each `FOR UPDATE`, gate on the fresh actor role (`IF v_actor_role IS NULL OR v_actor_role NOT IN ('commissioner','co_commissioner') THEN RAISE … 42501`) at 063:463 and 063:696, move the `is_league_commish` call below the lock in the other two, and pin the ordering in 017 the way `leave_league`'s is.
- **R94 · should-fix · `supabase/migrations/063_league_member_management.sql`:480** — replaying a successful commissioner transfer returns P0001/400 with copy asserting the target is not commissioner, breaking the D63 idempotency contract 063's own banner states for `set_member_role`. *Evidence:* 063:117 says "setting the role a member already holds is an idempotent success (D63)"; D63(5) gives the motive verbatim ("client retries must not error"). The guard at 063:479-482 is unconditional in `p_role` and sits ahead of the idempotent arm at 503-506, so any request whose target already holds commissioner dies there. Probed: T1 transfer u1→u2 → `{"role":"commissioner","transferred":true}`; T2 identical call replayed by u1 → P0001; T3 replayed by u2 (the new commissioner) → P0001; T0 transfer-to-self → P0001; falsifying controls T4/T5 (co_commissioner re-set, twice) → `{"transferred":false}` both times. `members-service.ts:56-58` maps P0001 → 400 with the RPC message as UX copy (its header says so outright), and PATCH `/members/[mid]` has no dedupe. The three sibling RPCs in the same file all ship the retry-safe arm (588-592, 713-718, 762-763); 017 §I pins the guard only for `p_role='manager'` (the genuine headless-demote), so nothing pins this either way. State stays correct after the refusal — no authz or capacity consequence. One correction carried from verification: the finding's claim that the 42501 arm "fires first when the retrier is the creator" is wrong — 473 keys on the *target* being the creator. *Fix direction:* add an idempotent arm before 063:480 returning `{member_id, role:'commissioner', transferred:false}` when `p_role='commissioner'` and the target already holds it, pin it in 017 §I beside the existing `transferred:false` assert, and keep 480's P0001 for the headless-demote it exists for — or narrow the 063:117 banner sentence instead.

**Reviewer batch (comprehensive single-reviewer pass of PR #67 — L.A2.7 league-home-states + index wiring + the mock deletion, `main...feat/M1-L.A2.7-league-home`). VERDICT: CLEAN — merged by the orchestrator per the (b) ruling.** The −1575-line deletion was the risk center: verified via a whole-tree grep (no surviving import of any removed `league-mock-data` export; the three `MOCK_LEAGUES` hits are each a file's own local const; draft mocks resolve to `draft/mock-draft.ts`, untouched) AND a **production build** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_AUTH=false npm run build` succeeds — the full import graph + prerender, which `tsc`/vitest don't exercise; the earlier build failure was purely the gitignored dev-auth flag left true, the guard working as designed). ## Review findings — 2026-07-27 (M1 batch 20)

**Findings-remediation Builder session on `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page` (PR #66 — fix-then-merge, no new PR). One should-fix (R114) from the PR #66 review: the join-by-code dialog dead-ended on a pasted `/join/…` link — the exact affordance its own copy advertises. Purely input-normalization on the join-by-code entry; the F2 surface, the six-state claim logic and the v2.8.10 erratum are untouched.**

### Should-fix

- **R114 · should-fix · `src/components/leagues/leagues-index.tsx`:65** — the join-by-code dialog breaks on a pasted `/join/…` link, the exact affordance its own copy advertises. *Evidence:* the submit handler does `router.push(\`/join/${encodeURIComponent(trimmed)}\`)`, passing the whole pasted string verbatim as the `[token]` param with no code/token extraction. But the dialog's DialogDescription tells the user to "paste a fieldscout.gg/join/… link" and the label reads "Invite code or link". The real share artifacts ARE full absolute URLs: `buildJoinLink` (invite-panel-ops.ts:264) returns `${origin}/join/${codeOrToken}`; the wizard copy button (league-create-wizard.tsx:996) copies `${window.location.origin}/join/${result.invite_code}`. `encodeURIComponent('https://fieldscout.gg/join/a1b2c3d4e5')` yields the single unresolvable segment `/join/https%3A%2F%2F…`; `get_join_preview` matches only exact token / lower(invite_code) / lower(invite_slug), so a full URL → `{found:false}` → "This link isn't valid" on a VALID invite. Typing a bare code works; pasting a link (an explicitly-offered input) dead-ends. F2 intact, no security issue. *Fix direction:* before pushing, if the input contains `/join/`, take the last non-empty path segment (strip query/hash) and encodeURIComponent only that; otherwise use the trimmed value as-is.

### Resolution — 2026-07-27 (Builder, same branch `feat/M1-L.A2.6-join-page`, PR #66)

| Finding | Resolved by |
|---|---|
| R114 (should-fix) | this commit — extraction lifted into a PURE helper `extractJoinCode` in `invite-panel-ops.ts` (the §7.2 share-link section, directly beside `buildJoinLink` as its exact inverse — NOT buried in the dialog's onClick), and `JoinLeagueDialog.handleSubmit` + the Continue-button `disabled` gate now push/enable on `extractJoinCode(code)` instead of the raw trim. The helper trims, cuts everything from the first `?`/`#`, then takes the last non-empty path segment after a case-insensitive `/join/` marker; a bare code/slug (no `/join/`) passes through trimmed. It keeps the segment's original case (seat tokens are case-sensitive; the RPC lower()s codes/slugs itself) and does NOT URL-encode — the caller still `encodeURIComponent`s the route param. Pinned in `invite-panel-ops.test.ts` §8: a 16-row table (full absolute URL, bare-host, protocol-relative, path-only, trailing slash, `?query`, `#hash`, query+slash, custom-slug link, whitespace-wrapped link, bare-code + bare-slug passthrough, empty + whitespace-only) **including the two REAL share artifacts** — `buildJoinLink('https://fieldscout.gg', CODE)`'s own output and the wizard's `${origin}/join/${invite_code}` shape — plus a case-preservation pin (mixed-case token unchanged) and an empty-code pin (`/join/` with no segment → `''`, so the dialog no-ops rather than pushing a dead segment). **Break probe shown:** helper body forced to `return raw.trim()` (the pre-R114 verbatim passthrough) → **exactly 14 of the table rows fail** (every link form), while the bare-code and empty rows STAY green — proving the table discriminates the fix rather than passing vacuously; reverted, re-proven green. **D39 browser pass (pre-auth, cheap):** against a seeded local league (`invite_code='r114probe1'`, `status='setup'`, 12 seats), navigated the EXACT URLs `router.push` targets before vs. after — `/join/https%3A%2F%2Ffieldscout.gg%2Fjoin%2Fr114probe1` (the OLD verbatim-encoded target) renders "This link isn't valid" (the bug reproduced on a valid invite); `/join/r114probe1` (the extracted bare code the NEW helper produces) renders the real "R114 Probe League · 12 seats open" claimable card. `get_join_preview` confirmed the same split at the RPC (`{found:true,status:ok}` on the bare code vs. `{found:false}` on the full URL). The authed dialog-click on `/app/leagues` could not be walked in this session (a local GoTrue seed-auth limitation — the hand-seeded user's client login didn't complete its post-sign-in redirect under automation; an environment constraint, not R114), so the observable behavior was verified at the pre-auth route it feeds — the dialog's onClick is a three-line wiring of the unit-pinned helper into `router.push`, and the URL it produces (`/join/r114probe1`) is exactly the one shown resolving. All seeded rows CLEANED (0 leagues/users/profiles/identities after teardown). Proofs: `test` 37 files / **684** (stack up; invite-panel-ops 33→**39**) · `test:gate` **24** · `type-check` clean · `lint` pre-existing-only. **D81** |

The v2.8.13 §8.5.5 erratum this PR folded says the stale seat's pick "is held open until deadline + disconnect_grace_seconds — a returning manager may pick manually during the hold — then autopicks"; the code re-derived the branch each tick with freshness as of now(), so a post-deadline heartbeat retroactively granted the fresh-at-expiry branch. No 022 pin covered a post-deadline heartbeat (the 44s/46s pins both predate the deadline).

### Blocker

- **R456 · blocker · a real test deleted on a false premise, and the premise written into LAW — TAKEN, fixed here.** v2.13.2's erratum 2 rested §7.3.8's solvency redundancy on `roster_size` *"topping out at 20 starters + 20 bench + 6 IR = 46"*. **The 20-slot cap is not a schema bound** — it is a sibling arm of the same validator, and `rosterSettingsSchema.starting_slots` is a bare `z.array(...)` with no length bound. Reproduced by this Builder before fixing (30 slots × `count` 10, `auction_budget: 50`): `leagueSettingsSchema.parse` → **OK**, `deriveRosterSize` → **307**, `validateLeagueSettings` → `["roster_settings.starting_slots","draft.auction_budget"]`. On the strength of the false premise, `settings-round-trip-db.test.ts`'s §8.6.8 per-field case had been downgraded to a Zod-range check, losing the only API-surface assertion that the solvency message and its field are wired. **Fixed three ways:** (a) the per-field case is restored with an oversized `starting_slots` array against a $50 budget, asserting the field, `307-player roster`, `per-slot reserve` and the sibling arm beside it — the Zod-layer `auction_budget: 49` case is KEPT, as a separate claim about a separate layer; (b) a new unit pin asserts the arm firing on a **Zod-parsed** object, which is the pin that would have caught the premise, plus the reserve-0 half where the solvency arm drops out and its sibling stays; (c) spec **v2.13.3** withdraws erratum 2 and restates the redundancy as being between two arms of ONE validator. **Falsifiability, measured:** with the arm made dead code (`if (false && …)`) the restored test goes RED while the downgraded Zod-layer test stays GREEN — which is exactly the coverage that had been lost. Mechanics at **D214(5)**.

### Should-fix

- **R457 · should-fix · the D90 TS-vs-SQL parity differential covered only the toggle-OFF column — TAKEN, fixed here.** D198(5) and AP.1 item 4 both require both, and the ON column had been resting on two hand-written literals (pgTAP 040 §B's `max_bid 200` and `auction-budget.test.ts`'s `maxBid: 200`) — parallel goldens, not a differential. `auction-api-db.test.ts`'s existing sweep now runs a **second pass over the SAME planted board with the flag flipped**, re-reading the config off the wire, re-querying `draft_team_budget` for every franchise, and asserting (a) TS ≡ SQL again at reserve 0, (b) that the two columns differ by exactly `(open_slots − 1) × $1` on every open roster while E27's complete roster reads 0 in BOTH — the negative control — and (c) the ON-column literals. Board restored afterwards. **Proved discriminating:** with the TS mirror made toggle-blind the new pass goes RED (`expected … to match object { auctionBudget: 200, reserve: +0 }`), which two parallel goldens could not do.
- **R458 · should-fix · F94's root cause is deeper than recorded, and the `test:db` number is order-dependent — TAKEN as a ledger widening, NOT fixed (scope; routed to the dev-environment task).** Re-measured here: `supabase/seed.sql` contains **zero** `insert into players`, so after any `db reset` the pool is EMPTY and the premise both suites rest on — *"behind the ENTIRE real pool"* — is unsatisfiable locally. Files=41, Tests=2855, Result: PASS`. **F94** widened to name both instances and the empty-pool root cause; the session log now states that `test:db` is green on the reset-first ordering.

- **R428 · should-fix · `auction-block-ops.ts` — "same nomination key + later deadline" is NOT unique to an anti-snipe extension; a RESUME produces exactly that shape — TAKEN, closed with a SIZE test, pinned in both directions.** `draft_pause` writes `current_deadline = NULL` + `deadline_remaining_ms` (069:353-357) and `draft_resume` writes `now() + remaining` (069:485-492) — strictly later, by the pause duration, with `current_pick_number` and `current_nomination.player_id` untouched, so `nominationKey` is unchanged. The reviewer's probe against the real module moved a deadline **12 seconds** (`T+18s` → `T+30s`, key unchanged) and got `reArmed: true` — announced on screen as *"Anti-snipe — clock reset to 10s"*. **They are separable by SIZE:** 085's re-arm is `GREATEST(current_deadline, now() + anti)` (085:780-791), so whenever it moves the deadline at all the new remaining is exactly `anti_snipe`, never more, while a resume restores the pre-pause remainder. `antiSnipeView` now additionally requires `deadlineMs − (nowMs + offsetMs) <= seconds * 1000 + ANTI_SNIPE_REARM_SLACK_MS` (1,500ms, sized for §9.3 offset error and no larger — every millisecond of slack is a millisecond of resume-shaped movement that still slips through). The reviewer's live probe: **mgr3 — a non-nominator during BIDDING — POSTed the nominate route with mgr2's `action_id` plus the (player, amount) read straight off `draft_bids`, and got HTTP 200 carrying `bid.team_id` = mgr2's team.** The shipped pin passed only because it happened to pick opening_bid 1 against a $2 raise; it would have stayed green if the check compared amount alone or player alone, and the converse (`nomination_seq` under the same policy) is symmetric. Blast radius was bounded — nothing written, no money moved, the settle-invalidate corrects the transient false "success" — but the CLAIM SITES said more than the code did. **Fix (the reviewer's preferred option, taken over narrowing the claims): IDENTITY is the discriminator.** The returned row's `team_id` is compared to the caller's ACTING SEAT — own `league_members.team_id`, or on a mock `config.mock.human_team_id` — resolved by the same helper the queue writers already use, renamed `resolveActingSeat` and re-documented as mirroring the RPCs' own team resolution (089:1201/1476). The argument comparison is KEPT as the second arm (it catches a caller reusing their OWN id across verbs, where the seat matches by construction). `nominatePlayer`/`placeBid` take `userId`; the routes pass `user.id`, which they already held. **The reviewer's exact probe is now the pin** — the read premise measured as mgr3, the forgery built ONLY from what that read returned, both directions, `not.toContain` on the other manager's team id, nothing written and the high bid AND its holder unchanged.

Check the player and the price, then place it again."** — no internal identifier, and a remedy that works (a fresh gesture mints a fresh id; the hooks' settle-invalidate has already refetched the room).

## Review findings — 2026-08-19 (M3 batch 7 — L.C1.6)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #171 — L.C1.6, migration 088 + pgTAP 037 + the client half, `main...feat/M3-L.C1.6-auction-realtime`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one should-fix (a real correctness hole in a claim the PR makes), four nits. All taken same-branch same-day; mechanics at D185; F75 filed; spec → v2.12.7.**

- **R401 · should-fix · the bid feed's "run-pure by construction / the reset's one event empties a held cache" claim (D184(3)) had a hole in exactly the window the join-refetch opens — TAKEN, fix shape (b) buffer-and-replay, pinned RED-first.** Mechanism: `SUBSCRIBED` → `invalidateQueries(feed)` starts a refetch (snapshot at T0); the `'draft_bids'` handler did `getQueryData → reduceBidEvent → setQueryData`; React Query REPLACES the cache with the fetch result on resolve, discarding every interim `setQueryData`. So a bid landing in the window was lost; rows VOIDED in it (cancel/undo/reset) came back as zombies from the pre-void snapshot; after a reset run-1 zombies merged with run-2 INSERTs at seq 1 until the next rejoin; the first fetch dropped events outright. The feed has no gap detector, so nothing repaired it until another confirmed join. D184(3)'s "cannot happen by construction" sentence was false — **withdrawn in place with the mechanism named.** Fix: NEW `use-draft-feed-sink.ts` (`createFeedSink` — FIFO queue, drained only while `fetchStatus === 'idle'`, a `QueryCache` subscription drains on settle; generic over the reducer), `use-draft.ts` pushes every `draft_bids` event through it and disposes it with the channel. Why (b) over (a): the drafts-event detector is blind in the very window (the interim write may still be in the cache when the `drafts` event arrives, and later `drafts` events compare only the current high bid — a lost historical bid or a cancelled nomination's zombies at a shared seq never trip it) and leans on intra-transaction delivery order. Pin: `use-draft-feed-sink.test.ts` (**18**) — mechanism control, window, hold, first-fetch, dedupe, ZOMBIES, CROSS-RUN, FIFO, error-settle, immediate path, no-cache drop, reducer-doubt via a live `QueryObserver`, dispose, spine source pins. **RED against the pre-fix handler shape: 7 of 16**, on the survival assertions; reverted ⇒ green. NOT deferred to L.C3.1 (the reviewer's instruction; the room is about to consume this feed).
- **R402 · nit · `use-draft-bids.ts` hand-rolled offset paging that `page-all.ts` already warns against (short-page stop without a count; order not ending in a UNIQUE column) — TAKEN.** Now `pageAll(...)` with `{ count: 'exact' }` and `.order('id')` as the final key; `DRAFT_BIDS_PAGE` removed; source-pinned (the exact order sequence). Theoretical today (hosted `max_rows` = 1000; live rows unique on (seq, amount) in practice) but the CLAUDE.md "exactly 1000 rows looked like the whole table" class.
- **R403 · nit · tasks-M3 §2:35 still read "non-strict Zod parses" while the PR said the claim was CORRECTED (the correction lived only in `use-draft-ops.ts` + D184(4)) — TAKEN.** The §2 line is amended in place with a dated note naming the real mechanism (plain interfaces + `isDraftsRecord`/`isPickRecord` structural guards; named-field copy is why additive keys never leak).

## Review findings — 2026-08-18 (M3 batch 6 — L.C1.5, FINAL fix round)

**Nine findings on PR #159: R375-R377 from the stack-owning reviewer's verification pass, R378-R383 from four independent static lenses that read the diff only. VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one BLOCKER-class, four should-fix, four nits.** Merge target `main` @ 4930bd8; `git merge-tree` clean. **The framing that matters: every pin involved passed. The lenses found what a live verification structurally could not, and three of the six are further doors into the same D160(8) insolvent/stuck-clock state R367 was filed for — R378 being R367's exact species recurring INSIDE R367's own fix. That is four consecutive rounds in which a correction re-introduced its own defect class.**

- **R378 · BLOCKER-class · the E28 arm-3 gate reproduced ONE of the award's TWO refusals, and at a settings-legal `auction_min_bid = 0` the arithmetic that masked the missing one disappears — TAKEN, fixed in the helper.** §3b's header promised "THE COMPARISON IS THE AWARD'S, RE-ASKED AFTER THE WRITE" and implemented it as the single test `v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`. `draft_tick`'s award arm asks **two** things: `open_slots < 1` (E27, `087:3479`) and `price > max_bid` (`087:3484`), and every other consumer pairs them (`draft_force_pick 087:2168-2173`, `draft_nominate 085:478`) because 084:349's `CASE WHEN v_open <= 0 THEN 0` makes a complete roster's `max_bid` a **semantic** zero — at which point `high_bid <= max_bid` is no longer the affordability question. At `min_bid >= 1` the gap is masked (`high_bid >= min_bid >= 1 > 0`, so the money arm raises anyway, with a message about dollars); at **`auction_min_bid = 0`, which is legal** (`league-settings.ts:220` = `min(0)`; 084:210 names the $0 league), both nomination writers open AT min_bid, so an unraised nomination stands at $0 and the gate computed `0 <= 0` and RETURNED. `draft_auction_solvent`'s floor there is `remaining >= 0`. **Driven:** budget $200 / min_bid $0 / total_rounds 2, t2 the standing high bidder at $0 with one pick; `draft_move_player(..., t2, null, 50)` filled its last slot, committed, and every tick then raised E27 into `auction_failures` forever. **Fix:** the gate re-derives `open_slots` alongside `max_bid`, its pass condition is `v_open >= 1 AND v_high_bid <= v_max_bid`, and the capacity case gets **its own sentence** (folding it into the max-bid message prints "$0 max bid" and sends the commissioner after money instead of a roster slot). **The coverage gap was the fixture, not the pin:** new **§I(c)** on a min_bid-$0 world (LM), one unit of `open_slots` either side, plus a min_bid-$1 pin proving the arm is the award's first question rather than a $0 special case. **Probe 7 → 5 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R379 · should-fix · `draft_reset` left the previous run's `draft_bids` live at sequence numbers the restart re-issues, so `draft_undo`'s auction on-clock recovery could seat the WRONG franchise — TAKEN, both halves.** `nomination_seq` IS `current_pick_number`; `draft_reset` rewinds it to 1 (`087:2573`) and `draft_start_internal` re-issues from there (`084:692`/`084:697`), while the recovery lookup (`087:1423`) had **no run discriminator at all** — no `voided_at` filter (deliberately: it must read rows the undo just voided) and no time bound. Two runs' nominations therefore collide on one sequence number, and since the seq→nominator map is not positional (§8.6.7(c) skips complete rosters) the earliest row names a DIFFERENT franchise. **Fix (a):** `draft_reset` stamps its run's rows `voided_at` — rows KEPT, §12.5 stays append-only, the same posture as the `draft_picks` soft-undo beside it — and reset is added as situation **(c)** in the D162 enumeration at `087:230-250` (whose lead-in said "exactly two situations" and now says three), in the spec (**v2.12.4**) and in `voided_at`'s writer inventory, which had said "written ONLY by two sites". **Fix (b):** the lookup scopes to `b.created_at >= v_draft.started_at`, the one discriminator available to a reader that must see voided rows, with a LOUD refusal when `started_at` is NULL on a live/paused draft rather than a silently widened window. Pinned both ways in §K, including the unscoped measurement that shows the ambiguity is real. **Probes 8 and 9 → 1 of 199 RED each**, reverted.
- **R380 · should-fix · `draft_reassign_pick`'s exclusivity check was blind to the one player who must not be assigned: the one under nomination — TAKEN.** On an auction the nominated player has **no** `draft_picks` row until the award writes it (`087:3497`), so a sweep of `draft_picks` passes for exactly him; nothing else on the path reads `current_nomination` (the E28 arms are about money; the §3b gate returns silently when the receiving team is not the high bidder). The award's INSERT then hits `uniq_draft_player_live` (065:178), ARM 2.6's `EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS` (`087:3581`) swallows it into `auction_failures`, and the nomination never clears — the same stuck clock, reached through the board instead of through the money. `draft_move_player` cannot reach it (it requires a live pick), which is why the guard lives on reassign and only there. Refusal points at `draft_cancel_nomination` — the verb this task shipped. **Probe 10 → 3 of 199 RED**, reverted.
- **R381 · should-fix · the no-drift pin whose entire job is preventing R367 from recurring was satisfied by a COMMENT — TAKEN, and the weakness was measured rather than argued.** `pg_proc.prosrc` is raw body text INCLUDING comments; `draft_adjust_budget` names the arm-3 helper twice (the R367 comment at `087:776` and the `PERFORM` at `087:781`), so deleting the call and keeping the comment left the pin GREEN. **Proof, not assertion: probe 1 was re-run with exactly that mutation and the pre-R381 predicate still evaluated `TRUE`.** All three sibling pins (`036:230/238/244`) now match the CALL FORM as each helper is actually called (`PERFORM public.X(` for the two gates, `:= public.X(` for the void helper, which returns a count) and assert **cardinality** (`count(*) = N`), because `bool_and` over a shrunken set also returns TRUE. Probe 1's red set consequently GREW by exactly pin 13 — **3 of 181 → 4 of 199** — which is the finding, measured.
- **R375 · should-fix · the stated justification for the eleven-verb mock sweep was false — TAKEN (the sweep KEPT, the reason replaced).** The 087 banner and 036 §M both said "025 already pins their mock refusal" is a claim about function bodies that no longer exist. **It is not:** `025_mock_draft_mode.sql:765-782` pins the mock refusal of `draft_set_clock`/`draft_reassign_pick`/`draft_move_player`, `supabase test db` runs 025 against the fully migrated 001-087 chain, and 025 calls them positionally with fewer arguments — resolving to the new arities through the defaults. Those pins exercise the **post-087 bodies**. The true reason for the sweep is CO-LOCATION: three of the seven were DROP+CREATEd here, so 036 pins the eleven in the post-087 world BESIDE 025's rather than instead of them. **Third instance in this PR of a justification outrunning the facts** — v2.12.3 says exactly why that is dangerous.
- **R382 · nit · pin 127's description inverted the causality — TAKEN (description only; the pin and its arithmetic were right).** It said a cross-team move is refused "because the SLOT it consumes is what shrinks the max bid". From 084:349-350 consuming a slot **raises** max_bid by one min_bid: t2 goes 151/2/150 → 149/1/149, where the $2 price costs $2 and the slot rebates $1, net −$1. The section's own setup comment stated it correctly. Reworded to the measured cause — t2 sits at exact equality after the $49 correction, so any net reduction refuses.

Now a 025-§F-style capture of the WHOLE drafts row and the WHOLE leagues row (so `updated_at` alone falsifies a smuggled UPDATE) plus pick/bid/chat/liveness counts. **Probe 11 → 2 of 199 RED; the pre-R383 composite re-run under the identical mutation turned 1** — it watched a mock whose league and draft rows had just been rewritten and reported zero side effects.

## Review findings — 2026-08-18 (DR batch 1)

**Reviewer batch (adversarial review of PR #157 — DR.1, the full-screen draft-room route, `main...feat/DR.1-fullscreen-route`). VERDICT: FIX-THEN-MERGE — one BLOCKER (a real regression on two surfaces), two should-fixes, three nits; ALL SIX TAKEN plus both lane-level recommendations; resolution on the SAME branch per house precedent.** *(The reviewer's own framing, and it is the durable output of this batch: **every claim in the PR that had been MEASURED held up** — the route-manifest diff, the same-cookie middleware differential in both directions, F66 measured on production builds both ways, the D147–D156 verbatim transcription, the shell-provider enumeration surviving an independent 98-file transitive closure. **Every claim that failed was one species: an assertion about the post-change world inferred from the INTENT of the change rather than observed**, written in the *proved* register beside claims that genuinely were proved. Each was one `grep`, one `wc -l`, or one DOM inventory from being caught. That pattern is now **tasks-DR §4.9**, a standing rule for the lane, and **DR.8's item 5 is extended to re-check disclosure PARAGRAPHS, not only F-rows** — three disclosures were wrong here and not one of them was an F-row.)*

- **R340 · BLOCKER · the route-group split REGRESSED a working exit on two surfaces, and every disclosure site asserted the opposite — TAKEN (both components fixed, six sites pinned, measured before and after).** Mechanism: on `main`, `src/app/app/layout.tsx` returned `<AppShell>`, which renders `<AppHeader />` inside `hidden lg:block`; `AppHeader` reads `useHeaderStore`, which `PageHeader` writes. Both components are byte-identical on `main` and this branch — so the lobby's and the launcher's *Back to league* **did render at ≥`lg` on `main` and render nowhere on this branch**. DR.1 did not create the mobile hole (tasks-DR §1 already named it); it widened a below-`lg` defect into an all-widths one, on the two surfaces nobody enumerated. **Reproduced independently before fixing** (dev-local :3123, a purpose-built SCHEDULED league where the dev-auth user is a plain manager, so `isCommish` is false): the lobby inventoried **one link, pointing DEEPER** — `…/draft?practice=1 :: Practice this draft` — and **zero buttons**; the launcher's past-pre-draft arm inventoried **zero links, zero buttons**; its pre-draft arm inventoried **zero links** and four controls that all go further in. The contradicted claim, verbatim (tasks-DR §1, repeated in D159(5) and the PR body): *"the lobby keeps Draft setup / Practice this draft, so no state is a dead end in the meantime"* — but **Draft setup is inside `{isCommish && …}`**, so a plain member never sees it. **Resolved:** `draft-lobby.tsx` gains an in-card *Back to league* **outside** the commissioner gate; `mock-draft-launcher.tsx` gains one at container level, **above the `preDraft` fork**, so both arms and every `MockList` state keep it. Not deferred to DR.2, per the finding. **Re-measured after the fix, same URLs:** lobby → **2 links** (`…/leagues/<id> :: Back to league` + the practice CTA), launcher pre-draft arm → **1 link** (the exit), launcher past-pre-draft arm → **1 link** (the exit) where it had none. New pin file **`src/components/draft/room-exits.test.ts` (5 pins)**, written to survive DR.2: every assertion runs against the source with **`<PageHeader …/>` elements deleted**, so a header can never satisfy them and they stay green when DR.2 removes those calls. **Four probes shown and reverted** — delete the lobby exit → 2/5 RED (both lobby pins); move it back inside `{isCommish && …}` → **exactly 1/5 RED** (the gate pin alone, proving it discriminates placement, not presence); delete the launcher exit → 2/5 RED; move it inside the `preDraft` arm only → **exactly 1/5 RED** (the both-arms pin). The correction is written at all three disclosure sites (tasks-DR §1, D159(5), the room docblock) and **the live room is now named as the one remaining exit-less state**, which is DR.2's Exit Draft to close.
- **R339 · should-fix · the C46 rename note claimed line numbers "still land" when every one was off by +22 — TAKEN (renumbered, and the offset proven wholesale).** The claim: *"the file is still 1013 lines … every `snake-draft-room.tsx:NNN` citation still lands (re-verified)"*. True of the `git mv`; false of the commit, which added a 22-line docblock above every landmark. Verified: `main` 1013 → branch 1035; `:389`→411, `:443`→465, `:450`→472, `:666`→688, `:719`→741, `:768`→790, and §1's `PageHeader` list `:666/:169/:250/:949/:969/:1001` was really 688/191/272/971/991/1023. **Six task banners (DR.2–DR.7) navigate by these numbers.** **Resolved:** after this cycle's own docblock corrections the file is **1052 lines** and the offset is **+39**; **tasks-DR §1 and the DR.2–DR.7 banners are renumbered** with each anchor also named by symbol (§4.9's preference — a symbol survives the next edit), and §3's D-entries / §6's dispositions are deliberately left at their as-authored numbers because §4 here quotes D147–D156 verbatim (both the note and the room docblock say "add 39" for those). The offset is established rather than spot-checked: **`main:snake-draft-room.tsx` line *N* is byte-identical to `draft-room.tsx` line *N+39* for every *N* in 101–1013**, the single exception being the renamed `export function` line — and every renumbered anchor was re-read by content afterwards.
- **R341 · should-fix · `(shell)/not-found.tsx`'s docblock was rewritten FOR accuracy and still opened with a false sentence — TAKEN, and the measurement turned out to be bigger than either side had it.** The sentence: *"Renders inside the app shell, so the nav survives and the user is never stranded."* **Measured on production builds, signed in, both revisions** — and the two halves disagree, which is why the claim survived so long: **server-rendered HTML has NO shell** (`/app/nfl/ZZZ` → 404, branch 17,621 bytes / `main` @ 9c81f7c 17,109 bytes, `pr-rail-strip` ×0, `h-header` ×0, no sidebar links; control `/app/lists` on the same session → 200, 44,187 bytes, `pr-rail-strip` ×1, `h-header` ×2, sidebar "Home" ×2), while **after hydration the shell IS there** (same URL, fresh `navigate`: DOM 34,450 bytes branch / 33,938 `main`, `pr-rail-strip` ×1, two sidebar "Home" links). So the nav does survive — but the **first paint of any `/app` 404 is chrome-less, and stays that way if JS fails**, which makes the page's own *Back to home* button the only exit the server actually sends. Identical on `main`, so still not a DR.1 regression. **Resolved:** the docblock now carries both measurements instead of the claim, and **F66's row is widened** to say the `/app` 404 boundary never renders inside `AppShell` server-side **for any case** (the caught case regains the nav on hydration; the unmatched-URL case falls through to the root 404 and never has it). One inherited overclaim fixed while there: "byte-for-byte the same" is wrong for the unmatched-URL comparison — 18,536 bytes branch vs 18,496 `main`, structurally identical, tens of bytes of build id apart.
- **R342 · nit · two docblocks pointed at a test file that does not exist — TAKEN.** `src/app/app/layout.tsx` and `(room)/leagues/layout.tsx` both cited `src/app/app/route-groups.test.ts`; the file is **`src/lib/route-groups.test.ts`**. The pins were written; only the path was recalled. Both corrected.
- **R343 · nit · `middleware.test.ts`'s `request()` helper never delivered the cookie it names — TAKEN (helper fixed + a pin that the harness builds what it claims).** Probed independently against Next 15.5.19, both forms in one run: `new NextRequest(url)` then `req.headers.set('cookie', …)` → `req.cookies.getAll()` **`[]`**; `new NextRequest(url, { headers: { cookie } })` → **`[{name:'sb-127-auth-token',value:'base64-STALE'}]`**. The D148(b) pins still discriminated (the mocked client never calls `getAll`), but the comment at the auth-page pin narrated a request state the test never built. **Resolved:** the cookie goes in through the constructor, and a **sixth pin** asserts `request()` puts it in `request.cookies` — the harness's own claim is now falsifiable. **Probe shown and reverted:** restoring the old helper turns **exactly 1 of 6** RED — the new one — and leaves the five middleware pins green, which is precisely R343's point about what they did and did not cover.
- **R344 · nit · D159(1)'s "all 43 route files moved under `(shell)/` by `git mv`" was imprecise — TAKEN.** `git diff -M --name-status main..HEAD` scores **43 renames: 41 into `(shell)/`, ONE into `(room)/` (the draft-room page), and ONE component rename that is not a route at all** (`snake-draft-room.tsx` → `draft-room.tsx`). And `src/app/app/not-found.tsx` is a **delete plus a new `(shell)/not-found.tsx`**, not a `git mv`, because its docblock was rewritten in the same commit. D159(1) now says exactly that.

**The two lane-level items, both implemented (they are the reviewer's recommendations and the orchestrator endorsed them):** **(1)** `tasks-DR-draft-room-redesign.md` **§4 gains rule 9** — any claim of the form *"X still lands" / "Y is not a dead end" / "Z was corrected" / "the pin covers it"* must name the command or observation that establishes it, the discipline §4.3 already imposes on goldens applied to prose; the rule cites the manifest diff and the cookie differential as the model and lists all five failures with what would have caught each. **(2)** **DR.8's item 5** (ledger honesty) now also requires re-checking the lane's **disclosure paragraphs** — §1's amendments, the task banners, the D-entries, the merged PR bodies — against the finished room, because R339/R340/R341 were three wrong disclosures and none of them was an F-row, so F-row hygiene alone would have caught nothing.

**Verification environment (R207):** everything browser-measured ran against the LOCAL stack, never hosted — the room surfaces on the `dev-local` config (:3123, where feature flags default ON), the 404 measurements on **production builds** of both revisions (`next start` :3125 branch / :3126 a `main` @ 9c81f7c worktree, `NEXT_PUBLIC_DEV_AUTH=false`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:54321`). *(Incidental re-verification of D159(2)'s hazard: on those production builds `/app/leagues/**` — including the room — redirects to `/app`, because `featureFlags.leagues` defaults OFF outside development. The `(room)/leagues/layout.tsx` gate DR.1 added is doing its job on a real build, not just in a source pin.)*
